def run(cmd: list[str]) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", " ".join(cmd))
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    """Actual encoded duration of a built segment, via ffprobe -- NOT the
    EDL-nominal (end - start), which can drift slightly from what actually
    got encoded (this project has been bitten by that drift before; xfade's
    `offset` param needs the real number since it's measured against input
    0's own timeline)."""
    r = subprocess.run(
        [FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
         "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FFPROBE FAILED:", path)
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def build_transition(seg_a: Path, seg_b: Path, out: Path, dur: float = XFADE_DUR, style: str = XFADE_STYLE) -> None:
    """Replace the hard cut between two already-built segments with a single
    merged clip: full seg_a, crossfading (video via xfade, audio in parallel
    via acrossfade) into full seg_b over `dur` seconds at the boundary. This
    one output clip REPLACES both seg_a and seg_b in the final concat list
    (its own duration is dur_a + dur_b - dur, since the overlapping tail/head
    now live once, blended, instead of twice). Both segments are already
    1920x1080/60fps/libx264/yuv420p/aac from the per-segment build step, so
    they're safe to feed straight into xfade/acrossfade as two -i inputs with
    no extra normalization needed.

    `offset` (xfade's crossfade-start point, measured on seg_a's own
    timeline) is computed from seg_a's REAL encoded duration via ffprobe, not
    the EDL's nominal (end-start) -- see probe_duration()."""
    dur_a = probe_duration(seg_a)
    offset = dur_a - dur
    if offset < 0:
        print(f"FAILED: segment {seg_a} too short ({dur_a}s) for a {dur}s crossfade")
        sys.exit(1)
    filt = (
        f"[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition={style}:duration={dur}:offset={offset}[v];"
        f"[0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d={dur}[a]"
    )
    cmd = [
        FFMPEG, "-y",
        "-i", str(seg_a), "-i", str(seg_b),
        "-filter_complex", filt,
        "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:a", "aac",
        str(out), "-loglevel", "error",
    ]
    run(cmd)


def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
    # Supersample before zoompan (4x linear) so the crop window's pixel-rounded
    # position error shrinks proportionally at output res -- this is what
    # actually kills the end-of-ramp "vibration": zoompan rounds x/y to whole
    # *input* pixels each frame, and near the top of an ease-out curve many
    # consecutive frames have nearly-but-not-quite-identical zoom, so the
    # rounded crop position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution.
    # At 4x input res, that same 1px dither is a quarter-output-pixel: gone.
    # Rounding the zoom value itself to 4 decimals removes the sub-pixel
    # floating-point noise that was driving the dither in the first place.
    fps = 60
    rsf = z["rs"] * fps
    rdf = z["rd"] * fps
    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy given in 1x source coords; input is prescaled 2x here
    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
        orsf = z["out_rs"] * fps
        ordf = z["out_rd"] * fps
        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
    else:
        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw_zoom})*2000)/2000"
    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"


def afade(dur: float) -> str:
    fo = max(0.0, dur - 0.03)
    return f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={fo:.3f}:d=0.03"


def build_intro_replacement(start: float, end: float, out: Path) -> None:
    """Intro-graphic beat: full-screen motion graphic (silent), seeked to
    whatever internal offset matches this range's start time, + his real
    voiceover from screen.mp4's audio track for the same time range, with
    fades. Seeking into the graphic (rather than always starting at its own
    t=0) lets this beat begin partway through -- e.g. cutting to it right as
    the title phrase starts, mid-graphic, as if it had been playing the
    whole time behind the webcam shot."""
    dur = end - start
    graphic_offset = start - INTRO_GRAPHIC_SOURCE_ANCHOR
    filt = f"[1:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    cmd = [
        FFMPEG, "-y",
        "-ss", f"{graphic_offset}", "-i", str(INTRO_GRAPHIC),
        "-ss", f"{start}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", SCREEN,
        "-filter_complex", filt,
        "-map", "0:v", "-map", "[a]",
        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-c:a", "aac",
        "-shortest", "-t", f"{dur}",
        str(out), "-loglevel", "error",
    ]
    run(cmd)


def _shrink_u_expr(graphic_start: float, graphic_end: float, td: float) -> str:
    """0..1 blend factor for the webcam hero<->corner shrink-aside: 0 = full
    hero size/position, 1 = settled corner size/position. Ramps 0->1 (ease-out
    cubic) over `td` seconds ending exactly at graphic_start (so the shrink
    completes right as the graphic's own CRT entrance begins), holds at 1 for
    the graphic's whole window, then ramps back 1->0 over `td` seconds
    starting at graphic_end. Same min(ease_in,ease_out) shape as
    crt_transition_filter's s_expr, just inverted (0 at the edges instead of
    the middle is what we want here since 0 = hero/full-frame, matching s=1
    there -- so this reuses s_expr as-is: s=1 in the hold matches u=1 here)."""
    ws, we = graphic_start - td, graphic_end + td
    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    ease_in = f"(1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))"
    ease_out = f"(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3))"
    return f"min({ease_in}\\,{ease_out})"


def _hero_transform(idx: int, windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
    """Piecewise scale(w,h)/position(x,y) expressions for the webcam feed,
    blending between the hero-stage size/position and this range's
    ASIDE_CENTER size/position across one or more graphic windows (see
    _shrink_u_expr). Multiple windows combine via max() (they don't overlap
    in time)."""
    cx, cy = ASIDE_CENTER[idx]
    aside_w, aside_h = ASIDE_SIZE[idx]
    aside_x, aside_y = cx - aside_w / 2, cy - aside_h / 2
    u_terms = [_shrink_u_expr(gs, ge, td) for gs, ge in windows]
    u_expr = u_terms[0]
    for term in u_terms[1:]:
        u_expr = f"max({u_expr}\\,{term})"
    w_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({aside_w}-{HERO_W})*{u_expr})/2))"
    h_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({aside_h}-{HERO_H})*{u_expr})/2))"
    x_expr = f"({HERO_X}+({aside_x}-{HERO_X})*{u_expr})"
    y_expr = f"({HERO_Y}+({aside_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u_expr})"
    return dict(w=w_expr, h=h_expr, x=x_expr, y=y_expr, u=u_expr)


def build_webcam_primary(
    idx: int, start: float, end: float, out: Path,
    include_grain: bool = True, apply_scrim: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Hero-stage webcam_primary layout: retrowave-loop background, the
    webcam feed enlarged to ~980px tall (its native 4:3 aspect preserved,
    never distorted) and centered, a neon border loop scaled/recentered to
    hug the new larger webcam box, and a subtle full-frame grain/flicker loop
    on top of it all. Ranges in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES additionally shrink the
    webcam+border ASIDE to that range's ASIDE_CENTER (60-70% of hero size,
    moved to whichever side of the screen is clear of that graphic's real
    content), eased, while that range's own graphic overlay(s) are on screen
    (see OVERLAYS[idx] + _hero_transform), holding there for the graphic's
    window before easing back to hero size. The neon border scales/repositions
    continuously in lockstep with the webcam throughout (not just at the two
    settled endpoints) -- see the border_dyn block below.
    The rounded-corner mask (pip_mask.png) is scaled in lockstep with the
    webcam feed itself (same w/h expressions) so the corner radius scales
    proportionally with the box at every point in the animation, hero size,
    corner size, and everywhere in between.

    `include_grain` (default True) and `apply_scrim` (default False) are
    per-build toggles, not permanent feature removals -- added for the
    demo_60s_v2 mockup, which needs grain OFF ("no static", per the user's
    latest direction, still going back and forth on it) and a background
    scrim ON. `apply_scrim` darkens the RAW retrowave background plate only
    (via colorchannelmixer, equivalent to alpha-compositing a flat black
    layer at SCRIM_OPACITY opacity: out = src*(1-SCRIM_OPACITY)), same
    layering principle as the existing grain fix above -- applied to the
    background before the border/webcam/graphic are drawn on top, so it
    never darkens the presenter or the graphics, only the plate behind them.
    """
    dur = end - start
    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays

    bg_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG)]
    grain_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(GRAIN_LOOP)]
    border_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER)]
    # -loop 1: pip_mask.png must be a continuously-supplied (infinite) frame
    # stream, not a single frame -- in the dynamic-shrink case its own
    # scale=...:eval=frame runs in lockstep with the webcam's per-frame w(t)/
    # h(t), and without -loop 1 the mask stream only ever provides ITS one
    # native frame, letting the mask's scale freeze at that single evaluation
    # while the webcam's own scale keeps re-evaluating every frame -- the
    # resulting size mismatch corrupts alphamerge (confirmed: produced a
    # solid dark rectangular artifact + ghosting mid-transition in range 5's
    # grow-back animation before this fix).
    # -framerate 60 alongside -loop 1: keeps the mask's own per-frame `t`
    # exactly in lockstep with the webcam's 60fps clock (image2's default
    # loop rate is 25fps, which would otherwise desync the two independent
    # eval=frame scale instances below just enough to size-mismatch them).
    mask_args = ["-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png")]
    # Blank transparent canvas, full 1920x1080 frame size, used only in the
    # dynamic-shrink case (see below) as the fixed-size base that the
    # shrinking/growing webcam and mask each get overlaid onto (2
    # independent uses via split=2 -- the border does NOT use this canvas,
    # see the border_dyn note below). MUST be the full frame (not just
    # HERO_W x HERO_H) -- the aside box (e.g. range 5's, up to x=1880,y=859)
    # sits well outside the hero box's own footprint (up to x=1613,y=1030),
    # so a HERO_W x HERO_H canvas silently clips the settled-aside content
    # off its right edge (confirmed bug in an earlier corner-PIP version of
    # this feature: ~46% of the box's width was clipped, showing background
    # bleed-through -- see report).
    blank_args = ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:r=60"]
    # input indices: 0=screen(audio only) 1=webcam 2=retrowave bg 3=grain
    # 4=neon border 5=mask 6=blank canvas (dynamic ranges only)
    next_idx = 7 if dynamic else 6

    # Optional scrim (see apply_scrim docstring note above), then grain/
    # flicker loop, both composited onto the RAW retrowave background only,
    # before the neon border and webcam are drawn on top -- so the border and

    # background plate itself, not a filter over the whole frame (previously

def run(cmd: list[str]) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", " ".join(cmd))
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    """Actual encoded duration of a built segment, via ffprobe -- NOT the
    EDL-nominal (end - start), which can drift slightly from what actually
    got encoded (this project has been bitten by that drift before; xfade's
    `offset` param needs the real number since it's measured against input
    0's own timeline)."""
    r = subprocess.run(
        [FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
         "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FFPROBE FAILED:", path)
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def build_transition(seg_a: Path, seg_b: Path, out: Path, dur: float = XFADE_DUR, style: str = XFADE_STYLE) -> None:
    """Replace the hard cut between two already-built segments with a single
    merged clip: full seg_a, crossfading (video via xfade, audio in parallel
    via acrossfade) into full seg_b over `dur` seconds at the boundary. This
    one output clip REPLACES both seg_a and seg_b in the final concat list
    (its own duration is dur_a + dur_b - dur, since the overlapping tail/head
    now live once, blended, instead of twice). Both segments are already
    1920x1080/60fps/libx264/yuv420p/aac from the per-segment build step, so
    they're safe to feed straight into xfade/acrossfade as two -i inputs with
    no extra normalization needed.

    `offset` (xfade's crossfade-start point, measured on seg_a's own
    timeline) is computed from seg_a's REAL encoded duration via ffprobe, not
    the EDL's nominal (end-start) -- see probe_duration()."""
    dur_a = probe_duration(seg_a)
    offset = dur_a - dur
    if offset < 0:
        print(f"FAILED: segment {seg_a} too short ({dur_a}s) for a {dur}s crossfade")
        sys.exit(1)
    filt = (
        f"[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition={style}:duration={dur}:offset={offset}[v];"
        f"[0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d={dur}[a]"
    )
    cmd = [
        FFMPEG, "-y",
        "-i", str(seg_a), "-i", str(seg_b),
        "-filter_complex", filt,
        "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:a", "aac",
        str(out), "-loglevel", "error",
    ]
    run(cmd)


def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
    # Supersample before zoompan (4x linear) so the crop window's pixel-rounded
    # position error shrinks proportionally at output res -- this is what
    # actually kills the end-of-ramp "vibration": zoompan rounds x/y to whole
    # *input* pixels each frame, and near the top of an ease-out curve many
    # consecutive frames have nearly-but-not-quite-identical zoom, so the
    # rounded crop position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution.
    # At 4x input res, that same 1px dither is a quarter-output-pixel: gone.
    # Rounding the zoom value itself to 4 decimals removes the sub-pixel
    # floating-point noise that was driving the dither in the first place.
    fps = 60
    rsf = z["rs"] * fps
    rdf = z["rd"] * fps
    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy given in 1x source coords; input is prescaled 2x here
    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
        orsf = z["out_rs"] * fps
        ordf = z["out_rd"] * fps
        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
    else:
        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw_zoom})*2000)/2000"
    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"


def afade(dur: float) -> str:
    fo = max(0.0, dur - 0.03)
    return f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={fo:.3f}:d=0.03"


def build_intro_replacement(start: float, end: float, out: Path) -> None:
    """Intro-graphic beat: full-screen motion graphic (silent), seeked to
    whatever internal offset matches this range's start time, + his real
    voiceover from screen.mp4's audio track for the same time range, with
    fades. Seeking into the graphic (rather than always starting at its own
    t=0) lets this beat begin partway through -- e.g. cutting to it right as
    the title phrase starts, mid-graphic, as if it had been playing the
    whole time behind the webcam shot."""
    dur = end - start
    graphic_offset = start - INTRO_GRAPHIC_SOURCE_ANCHOR
    filt = f"[1:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    cmd = [
        FFMPEG, "-y",
        "-ss", f"{graphic_offset}", "-i", str(INTRO_GRAPHIC),
        "-ss", f"{start}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", SCREEN,
        "-filter_complex", filt,
        "-map", "0:v", "-map", "[a]",
        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-c:a", "aac",
        "-shortest", "-t", f"{dur}",
        str(out), "-loglevel", "error",
    ]
    run(cmd)


def _shrink_u_expr(graphic_start: float, graphic_end: float, td: float) -> str:
    """0..1 blend factor for the webcam hero<->corner shrink-aside: 0 = full
    hero size/position, 1 = settled corner size/position. Ramps 0->1 (ease-out
    cubic) over `td` seconds ending exactly at graphic_start (so the shrink
    completes right as the graphic's own CRT entrance begins), holds at 1 for
    the graphic's whole window, then ramps back 1->0 over `td` seconds
    starting at graphic_end. Same min(ease_in,ease_out) shape as
    crt_transition_filter's s_expr, just inverted (0 at the edges instead of
    the middle is what we want here since 0 = hero/full-frame, matching s=1
    there -- so this reuses s_expr as-is: s=1 in the hold matches u=1 here)."""
    ws, we = graphic_start - td, graphic_end + td
    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    ease_in = f"(1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))"
    ease_out = f"(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3))"
    return f"min({ease_in}\\,{ease_out})"


def _hero_transform(idx: int, windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
    """Piecewise scale(w,h)/position(x,y) expressions for the webcam feed,
    blending between the hero-stage size/position and this range's
    ASIDE_CENTER size/position across one or more graphic windows (see
    _shrink_u_expr). Multiple windows combine via max() (they don't overlap
    in time)."""
    cx, cy = ASIDE_CENTER[idx]
    aside_w, aside_h = ASIDE_SIZE[idx]
    aside_x, aside_y = cx - aside_w / 2, cy - aside_h / 2
    u_terms = [_shrink_u_expr(gs, ge, td) for gs, ge in windows]
    u_expr = u_terms[0]
    for term in u_terms[1:]:
        u_expr = f"max({u_expr}\\,{term})"
    w_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({aside_w}-{HERO_W})*{u_expr})/2))"
    h_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({aside_h}-{HERO_H})*{u_expr})/2))"
    x_expr = f"({HERO_X}+({aside_x}-{HERO_X})*{u_expr})"
    y_expr = f"({HERO_Y}+({aside_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u_expr})"
    return dict(w=w_expr, h=h_expr, x=x_expr, y=y_expr, u=u_expr)


def build_webcam_primary(
    idx: int, start: float, end: float, out: Path,
    include_grain: bool = True, apply_scrim: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Hero-stage webcam_primary layout: retrowave-loop background, the
    webcam feed enlarged to ~980px tall (its native 4:3 aspect preserved,
    never distorted) and centered, a neon border loop scaled/recentered to
    hug the new larger webcam box, and a subtle full-frame grain/flicker loop
    on top of it all. Ranges in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES additionally shrink the
    webcam+border ASIDE to that range's ASIDE_CENTER (60-70% of hero size,
    moved to whichever side of the screen is clear of that graphic's real
    content), eased, while that range's own graphic overlay(s) are on screen
    (see OVERLAYS[idx] + _hero_transform), holding there for the graphic's
    window before easing back to hero size. The neon border scales/repositions
    continuously in lockstep with the webcam throughout (not just at the two
    settled endpoints) -- see the border_dyn block below.
    The rounded-corner mask (pip_mask.png) is scaled in lockstep with the
    webcam feed itself (same w/h expressions) so the corner radius scales
    proportionally with the box at every point in the animation, hero size,
    corner size, and everywhere in between.

    `include_grain` (default True) and `apply_scrim` (default False) are
    per-build toggles, not permanent feature removals -- added for the
    demo_60s_v2 mockup, which needs grain OFF ("no static", per the user's
    latest direction, still going back and forth on it) and a background
    scrim ON. `apply_scrim` darkens the RAW retrowave background plate only
    (via colorchannelmixer, equivalent to alpha-compositing a flat black
    layer at SCRIM_OPACITY opacity: out = src*(1-SCRIM_OPACITY)), same
    layering principle as the existing grain fix above -- applied to the
    background before the border/webcam/graphic are drawn on top, so it
    never darkens the presenter or the graphics, only the plate behind them.
    """
    dur = end - start
    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays

    bg_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG)]
    grain_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(GRAIN_LOOP)]
    border_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER)]
    # -loop 1: pip_mask.png must be a continuously-supplied (infinite) frame
    # stream, not a single frame -- in the dynamic-shrink case its own
    # scale=...:eval=frame runs in lockstep with the webcam's per-frame w(t)/
    # h(t), and without -loop 1 the mask stream only ever provides ITS one
    # native frame, letting the mask's scale freeze at that single evaluation
    # while the webcam's own scale keeps re-evaluating every frame -- the
    # resulting size mismatch corrupts alphamerge (confirmed: produced a
    # solid dark rectangular artifact + ghosting mid-transition in range 5's
    # grow-back animation before this fix).
    # -framerate 60 alongside -loop 1: keeps the mask's own per-frame `t`
    # exactly in lockstep with the webcam's 60fps clock (image2's default
    # loop rate is 25fps, which would otherwise desync the two independent
    # eval=frame scale instances below just enough to size-mismatch them).
    mask_args = ["-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png")]
    # Blank transparent canvas, full 1920x1080 frame size, used only in the
    # dynamic-shrink case (see below) as the fixed-size base that the
    # shrinking/growing webcam and mask each get overlaid onto (2
    # independent uses via split=2 -- the border does NOT use this canvas,
    # see the border_dyn note below). MUST be the full frame (not just
    # HERO_W x HERO_H) -- the aside box (e.g. range 5's, up to x=1880,y=859)
    # sits well outside the hero box's own footprint (up to x=1613,y=1030),
    # so a HERO_W x HERO_H canvas silently clips the settled-aside content
    # off its right edge (confirmed bug in an earlier corner-PIP version of
    # this feature: ~46% of the box's width was clipped, showing background
    # bleed-through -- see report).
    blank_args = ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:r=60"]
    # input indices: 0=screen(audio only) 1=webcam 2=retrowave bg 3=grain
    # 4=neon border 5=mask 6=blank canvas (dynamic ranges only)
    next_idx = 7 if dynamic else 6

    # Optional scrim (see apply_scrim docstring note above), then grain/
    # flicker loop, both composited onto the RAW retrowave background only,
    # before the neon border and webcam are drawn on top -- so the border and
    # webcam feed stay crisp/undegraded and the grain reads as texture on the
    # background plate itself, not a filter over the whole frame (previously
    # this was applied last, over the fully-assembled frame including the
    # webcam, so the grain visibly covered the presenter's face too -- fixed
    # by moving it here, ahead of the border/webcam compositing). Same
    # ahead-of-everything-else placement now applies to the scrim.
    if apply_scrim:
        keep = 1 - SCRIM_OPACITY
        filt = f"[2:v]colorchannelmixer=rr={keep}:gg={keep}:bb={keep}[bg_s];"
        bg_in = "bg_s"
    else:
        filt = ""
        bg_in = "2:v"
    if include_grain:
        filt += f"[{bg_in}][3:v]overlay=x=0:y=0[bg_grain];"
    else:
        filt += f"[{bg_in}]copy[bg_grain];"

    if dynamic:
        windows = [(ov["rel_start"], ov["rel_start"] + ov["dur"]) for ov in overlays]
        tf = _hero_transform(idx, windows)
        u = tf["u"]

]

SR = 16000
ENV_HZ = 100  # envelope sample rate
MAX_LAG_S = 5.0


def load_audio(path: Path) -> np.ndarray:
    r = subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(path), "-map", "0:a:0",
         "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(SR), "-f", "s16le", "-"],
        capture_output=True,
    )
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("ffmpeg failed:", path)
        print(r.stderr.decode(errors="replace")[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)
    return np.frombuffer(r.stdout, dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0


def envelope(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """abs -> boxcar-mean downsample from SR to ENV_HZ."""
    step = SR // ENV_HZ
    n = (len(x) // step) * step
    return np.abs(x[:n]).reshape(-1, step).mean(axis=1)


def xcorr_lag(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, max_lag: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Lag (in envelope samples) maximising correlation of b against a, plus
    a normalised peak score. Positive = b is delayed relative to a."""
    a = a - a.mean()
    b = b - b.mean()
    n = 1 << int(np.ceil(np.log2(len(a) + len(b))))
    A = np.fft.rfft(a, n)
    B = np.fft.rfft(b, n)
    cc = np.fft.irfft(A * np.conj(B), n)
    cc = np.concatenate([cc[-max_lag:], cc[: max_lag + 1]])
    lags = np.arange(-max_lag, max_lag + 1)
    k = int(np.argmax(cc))
    peak = cc[k]
    denom = np.sqrt((a * a).sum() * (b * b).sum()) + 1e-9
    return float(lags[k]), float(peak / denom)


def main() -> None:
    max_lag = int(MAX_LAG_S * ENV_HZ)
    print(f"{'part':<6} {'window':<14} {'lag_s':>8} {'score':>7}")
    results = {}
    for i, (s_name, w_name) in enumerate(PARTS, start=1):
        s = envelope(load_audio(SRC / "Screen" / s_name))
        w = envelope(load_audio(SRC / "Webcam" / w_name))
        dur = min(len(s), len(w)) / ENV_HZ
        # three 60s windows (or as much as fits), spread across the part
        win = min(60.0, max(10.0, dur / 4))
        starts = [dur * f - win / 2 for f in (0.2, 0.5, 0.8)]
        lags = []
        for st in starts:
            st = max(0.0, min(st, dur - win))
            a = s[int(st * ENV_HZ) : int((st + win) * ENV_HZ)]
            b = w[int(st * ENV_HZ) : int((st + win) * ENV_HZ)]
            lag, score = xcorr_lag(a, b, max_lag)
            lag_s = lag / ENV_HZ
            lags.append(lag_s)
            print(f"{i:<6} {f'{st:.0f}-{st+win:.0f}s':<14} {lag_s:>8.3f} {score:>7.3f}")
        spread = max(lags) - min(lags)
        med = float(np.median(lags))
        flag = "" if spread <= 0.02 else "   <-- INCONSISTENT (possible drift)"
        print(f"{i:<6} {'MEDIAN':<14} {med:>8.3f}  spread={spread:.3f}{flag}")
        results[i] = med
    print()
    print("PART_OFFSETS = {")
    for i, v in results.items():
        print(f"    {i}: {v:.3f},")
    print("}")

    for p in reversed(PARTS):

"""Merge the six per-part webcam transcripts into one global-timeline
transcript at <edit>/transcripts/webcam.json.

Each part was transcribed independently, so its word timestamps are local to
that part's own file. Shifting each part's words by PART_START puts every
word on the single global clock the EDL and captions use.

Only the WEBCAM audio is transcribed for this episode: the screen recording
carries a bit-for-bit equivalent feed of the same mic (verified -- mean and
peak levels match within 0.1 dB on sampled windows of parts 1 and 6), and
the webcam track is now the master audio, so a second transcript of the same
speech would add nothing but drift risk.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from timeline import PART_FILES, PART_START, PARTS, WEBCAM_DUR  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RAW = EDIT / "_tx_webcam" / "transcripts"
OUT = EDIT / "transcripts" / "webcam.json"


def main() -> None:
    merged: list[dict] = []
    boundaries: list[dict] = []
    for p in PARTS:
        _, w_name = PART_FILES[p]
        src = RAW / (Path(w_name).stem + ".json")
        data = json.loads(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        off = PART_START[p]
        n_words = 0
        last = 0.0
        for w in data["words"]:
            e = dict(w)
            e["start"] = round(w["start"] + off, 3)
            e["end"] = round(w["end"] + off, 3)
            e["part"] = p
            merged.append(e)
            if w["type"] == "word":
                n_words += 1
            last = max(last, w["end"])
        boundaries.append(dict(part=p, start=off, end=off + WEBCAM_DUR[p],
                               words=n_words, last_speech=round(off + last, 2)))
        print(f"part {p}: {n_words:>5} words, +{off:.3f}s offset, "
              f"last speech at {off + last:.1f}s of {off + WEBCAM_DUR[p]:.1f}s")

    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps({
        "words": merged,
        "backend": "local",
        "timeline": "global (webcam clock, six parts concatenated)",
        "parts": boundaries,
    }), encoding="utf-8")
    total_words = sum(b["words"] for b in boundaries)
    print(f"\n{total_words} words total -> {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Extract screen-recording frames at given GLOBAL timestamps and tile them
into labelled 3x3 contact sheets.

Used to actually LOOK at what is on screen at each candidate beat before
deciding hero-vs-PIP layout, which corner the PIP can safely occupy, and
where a zoom should target -- rather than inferring any of that from the
transcript text alone.

Usage: contact_sheet.py <out_dir> <t1> <t2> ...
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

TILE_W, TILE_H = 640, 360
COLS, ROWS = 3, 3


def extract(t: float, out: Path, source: str = "screen") -> None:
    r = resolve(t, t + 0.5)
    path = r["screen_path"] if source == "screen" else r["webcam_path"]
    ss = r["screen_ss"] if source == "screen" else r["webcam_ss"]
    label = f"t={t:.1f}s  p{r['part']}"
    vf = (
        f"scale={TILE_W}:{TILE_H},"
        f"drawtext=text='{label}':x=8:y=8:fontsize=22:fontcolor=yellow:"
        f"box=1:boxcolor=black@0.7:boxborderw=5"
    )
    subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{ss}", "-i", path,
         "-frames:v", "1", "-vf", vf, str(out)],
        check=True,
    )


def main() -> None:
    out_dir = Path(sys.argv[1])
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    times = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[2:]]
    tiles = []
    for i, t in enumerate(times):
        p = out_dir / f"f{i:03d}.png"
        extract(t, p)
        tiles.append(p)
    per = COLS * ROWS
    for s in range(0, len(tiles), per):
        chunk = tiles[s : s + per]
        sheet = out_dir / f"sheet_{s // per:02d}.png"
        args = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error"]
        for c in chunk:
            args += ["-i", str(c)]
        n = len(chunk)
        filt = "".join(f"[{i}:v]" for i in range(n))
        filt += f"xstack=inputs={n}:layout="
        layout = []
        for i in range(n):
            cx, cy = i % COLS, i // COLS
            layout.append(f"{cx * TILE_W}_{cy * TILE_H}")
        filt += "|".join(layout) + ":fill=black[v]"
        args += ["-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(sheet)]
        subprocess.run(args, check=True)
        print(sheet, [f"{t:.1f}" for t in times[s : s + per]])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Dump word-level timings from the merged global-timeline transcript.

Cut points get snapped to these real word boundaries rather than to the
coarser phrase ranges in takes_packed.md -- a phrase boundary is only ever
where a >=0.5s silence happened to fall, which is rarely where the cut
actually wants to be.

Usage: words.py <t0> <t1> [<t0> <t1> ...]
       words.py --find "some phrase"
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
WORDS = json.loads((EDIT / "transcripts" / "webcam.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["words"]


def dump(t0: float, t1: float) -> None:
    print(f"--- {t0:.2f} .. {t1:.2f} ---")
    line = []
    for w in WORDS:
        if w["type"] != "word":
            continue
        if w["end"] < t0 or w["start"] > t1:
            continue
        line.append(f"[{w['start']:.2f}]{w['text']}")
        if len(line) >= 8:
            print("   " + " ".join(line))
            line = []
    if line:
        print("   " + " ".join(line))


def find(phrase: str) -> None:
    toks = phrase.lower().split()
    ws = [w for w in WORDS if w["type"] == "word"]
    texts = [w["text"].lower().strip(".,!?'\"-") for w in ws]
    for i in range(len(ws) - len(toks) + 1):
        if all(toks[j] in texts[i + j] or texts[i + j] in toks[j] for j in range(len(toks))):
            print(f"  {ws[i]['start']:>9.2f} - {ws[i + len(toks) - 1]['end']:>9.2f}  "
                  f"{' '.join(w['text'] for w in ws[i:i + len(toks)])}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1] == "--find":
        find(" ".join(sys.argv[2:]))
    else:
        a = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]]
        for i in range(0, len(a), 2):
            dump(a[i], a[i + 1])
PYEOF

def main() -> None:
    ranges = []
    for start, end, beat, layout, pip, quote, reason in R:
        info = resolve(start, end)  # asserts no part-boundary crossing
        r = dict(
            source="webcam" if layout == H else "screen",
            start=round(start, 3),
            end=round(end, 3),
            beat=beat,
            layout=layout,
            part=info["part"],
            quote=quote,
            reason=reason,
        )
        if pip:
            r["pip"] = pip
        ranges.append(r)

    total = sum(r["end"] - r["start"] for r in ranges)
    edl = dict(
        version=2,
        sources={
            "parts": {
                str(p): dict(screen=str(SRC / "Screen" / s), webcam=str(SRC / "Webcam" / w))
                for p, (s, w) in PART_FILES.items()
            },
            "note": "Global timeline = webcam clock; see scripts/timeline.py for per-part screen offsets.",
        },
        master_audio="webcam",
        grade="none",
        ranges=ranges,
        overlays=[],
        subtitles=None,
        total_duration_s=round(total, 2),
    )
    out = EDIT / "edl.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(edl, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"{len(ranges)} ranges, {total:.1f}s ({total / 60:.2f} min) from {TOTAL / 60:.1f} min raw "
          f"({100 * total / TOTAL:.0f}% kept)")
    scene_changes = []
    prev = None
    for i, r in enumerate(ranges):
        if prev is not None and r["layout"] != prev:
            scene_changes.append((i - 1, i))
        prev = r["layout"]
    print(f"scene changes (hero <-> screen), {len(scene_changes)}: {scene_changes}")

    # shortest segments on either side of each scene change -- the crossfade
    # duration has to stay a small fraction of both.
    for a, b in scene_changes:
        da = ranges[a]["end"] - ranges[a]["start"]
        db = ranges[b]["end"] - ranges[b]["start"]
        flag = "  <-- TIGHT" if min(da, db) < 2.0 else ""
        print(f"    {a:>2}->{b:<2}  A={da:5.2f}s  B={db:5.2f}s{flag}")

    print("\nper beat:")
    by_beat: dict[str, float] = {}
    order: list[str] = []
    for r in ranges:
        if r["beat"] not in by_beat:
            order.append(r["beat"])
        by_beat[r["beat"]] = by_beat.get(r["beat"], 0) + r["end"] - r["start"]
    for b in order:
        print(f"  {b:<14} {by_beat[b]:>6.1f}s")
    print(f"\n-> {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def main() -> None:
    ranges = []
    for start, end, beat, layout, pip, quote, reason in R:
        info = resolve(start, end)  # asserts no part-boundary crossing
        r = dict(
            source="webcam" if layout == H else "screen",
            start=round(start, 3),
            end=round(end, 3),
            beat=beat,
            layout=layout,
            part=info["part"],
            quote=quote,
            reason=reason,
        )
        if pip:
            r["pip"] = pip
        ranges.append(r)

    total = sum(r["end"] - r["start"] for r in ranges)
    edl = dict(
        version=2,
        sources={
            "parts": {
                str(p): dict(screen=str(SRC / "Screen" / s), webcam=str(SRC / "Webcam" / w))
                for p, (s, w) in PART_FILES.items()
            },
            "note": "Global timeline = webcam clock; see scripts/timeline.py for per-part screen offsets.",
        },
        master_audio="webcam",
        grade="none",
        ranges=ranges,
        overlays=[],
        subtitles=None,
        total_duration_s=round(total, 2),
    )
    out = EDIT / "edl.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(edl, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"{len(ranges)} ranges, {total:.1f}s ({total / 60:.2f} min) from {TOTAL / 60:.1f} min raw "
          f"({100 * total / TOTAL:.0f}% kept)")
    scene_changes = []
    prev = None
    for i, r in enumerate(ranges):
        if prev is not None and r["layout"] != prev:
            scene_changes.append((i - 1, i))
        prev = r["layout"]
    print(f"scene changes (hero <-> screen), {len(scene_changes)}: {scene_changes}")

    # shortest segments on either side of each scene change -- the crossfade
    # duration has to stay a small fraction of both.
    for a, b in scene_changes:
        da = ranges[a]["end"] - ranges[a]["start"]
        db = ranges[b]["end"] - ranges[b]["start"]
        flag = "  <-- TIGHT" if min(da, db) < 2.0 else ""
        print(f"    {a:>2}->{b:<2}  A={da:5.2f}s  B={db:5.2f}s{flag}")

    print("\nper beat:")
    by_beat: dict[str, float] = {}
    order: list[str] = []
    for r in ranges:
        if r["beat"] not in by_beat:
            order.append(r["beat"])
        by_beat[r["beat"]] = by_beat.get(r["beat"], 0) + r["end"] - r["start"]
    for b in order:
        print(f"  {b:<14} {by_beat[b]:>6.1f}s")
    print(f"\n-> {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Fast, ugly draft cut -- no compositing, no graphics, no captions.

Purpose is to hear the CUT: pacing, whether the retake choices flow, whether
any splice lands mid-word. Each range is pulled from whichever source that
range's layout uses for picture (webcam for hero beats, screen for PIP
beats), but ALWAYS with the webcam's audio, since the webcam track is the
master and is what the final render uses.

Output: <edit>/draft_cut.mp4 (960x540, veryfast) -- disposable.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT_DIR = EDIT / "clips_draft"
OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

W, H = 960, 540


def build(args: tuple[int, dict]) -> Path:
    i, r = args
    out = OUT_DIR / f"d{i:02d}.mp4"
    if out.exists():
        return out
    info = resolve(r["start"], r["end"])
    dur = info["dur"]
    hero = r["layout"] == "webcam_primary"
    pic_path = info["webcam_path"] if hero else info["screen_path"]
    pic_ss = info["webcam_ss"] if hero else info["screen_ss"]
    # letterbox rather than crop so the draft never hides a framing problem
    vf = f"scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad={W}:{H}:-1:-1:color=black"
    cmd = [
        "ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error",
        "-ss", f"{pic_ss}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", pic_path,
        "-ss", f"{info['webcam_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", info["webcam_path"],
        "-filter_complex", f"[0:v]{vf}[v];[1:a]afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,"
                           f"afade=t=out:st={max(0.0, dur - 0.03):.3f}:d=0.03[a]",
        "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "26", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
        "-r", "60", "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2",

**Shape.** Ten sections, alternating between two looks:

| | |
|---|---|
| **0:00–2:23** | **Hero** — hook, three-apps track record, bank balance, the thesis, why a community, what Kodely is, today's scope |

| **10:38–12:03** | **Screen** — the fixed glow, the prompt-carry-through feature, the honest "nothing happened" reality check |
| **12:03–12:32** | **Hero** — outro + subscribe |

**Takes.** Every retake cluster resolved to the version he settled on — the flubbed "welcome back / *fuck*" open, three abandoned restarts of "three high functioning apps", the thesis take he kills out loud with "let's take that out", four passes at "an app called Kodely", the doubled "and speaking of free", the abandoned "nothing happened" pass. Six scene changes get the 0.4s xfade; everything else is a hard cut.

**Motion graphics — 13 placements.** Each tied to something actually said:

- **Reused as-is:** palette reveal (his "warm pink peach magenta"), BUG FOUND tag, mic indicator ×2, SUBSCRIBE tag
- **Re-render needed:** bank stat (**$122** CAD, not ep 1's $128, and shortened to ~6.5s to fit the beat), Kodely reveal, Nxeon tag
- **New:** the zero-experience stack (HTML/CSS/JavaScript/PHP), today's to-do card, 750 free credits, 702 cards · 20–50 parts, kodely.me live, 1 hr 30 min

**Shrink-aside vs plain PIP.** Shrink-aside on the six hero beats carrying a card — bank stat, zero-stack, Kodely reveal, to-do card, kodely.me live, 1h30m, subscribe. Everything on a screen beat is a plain overlay over the PIP layout.

**PIP corner.** Bottom-right through part 1 (plain centred browser, right side empty), then one eased slide to bottom-left at 5:24 and it stays there — from part 2 on, the Claude panel occupies the right third of the screen and a bottom-right box would sit directly on the panel he's dictating into.

**Zooms** (screen beats only, ≤2.0x): the Gemini prompt box, the Kodely glow bug, the "Kodely 702" chip, the Pilates-studio animation, the bug on refresh, the fixed glow. Targets get frame-verified before I commit them.

---

**Three things worth your call:**

1. **Audio is 30 dB under level.** This cut measures **−44.4 LUFS** (YouTube targets −14). I checked — **episode 1 shipped at −42.9 LUFS**, so this isn't your footage, it's a gap in the pipeline. The recording itself is clean (noise floor −76 dB, ~48 dB SNR), so a two-pass `loudnorm` to −14 LUFS on the final mix fixes it with faint hiss at worst. I plan to add it and document it.

2. **Episode 1's Kodely reveal card says "Codely."** The brand is **Kodely** on your own site and tab title. Whisper hears it as "Codely" everywhere, and ep 1's graphic inherited that. Same class of error: `slot_tag_nexion` says "NEXION", but your logo and URL are **NXEON / nxeon.cloud**. I'm re-rendering both and correcting the caption transcript (also "Shrite"→Stripe, "Cloudmax"→Claude Max, "SAS"→SaaS).

3. **Wardrobe changes mid-video** — blue jersey in parts 1–2, black tee from part 3 on. It lands at 7:04 (community) and 10:25 (payoff). Unavoidable, reads fine as a session recorded over hours, just flagging it.

Switching to webcam audio worked out well, by the way — it's the same mic feed as the screen recording (levels match within 0.1 dB), so nothing was lost, and lip-sync is now exact by construction. The screen recording is offset into the webcam clock by a measured 10–50 ms per part.

content.thinking:
That 8.7-9.0s window isn't a clean silence measurement since it's near the cut and includes speech tail. The key issue is that linear=true was requested but the required gain of 30.5 dB to hit -14 LUFS exceeds the max linear gain of 23.15 dB before clipping, so loudnorm falls back to dynamic normalization.

This explains why LRA dropped from 11.8 to 6.4 — dynamic compression on speech can pump and noticeably flatten dynamics. A cleaner approach would be fixed gain plus a limiter rather than loudnorm's dynamic mode, but the peak-to-loudness ratio here is about 20 LU, which is unusually high for speech and suggests isolated loud transients (plosives or similar) that genuinely require real peak limiting to reach -14 LUFS without clipping.

I'm working through the math: applying linear gain to hit a true peak target of -1.5 dBTP would only bring integrated loudness to around -21.4 LUFS, still 7.4 LU short of target, confirming that some form of compression or limiting is unavoidable for this material. Standard practice for spoken-word content is gentle compression plus limiting, so I'm considering a chain using a mild compressor with a high threshold to catch only peaks, followed by makeup gain and a limiter at -1.5 dBTP, or alternatively trying speechnorm or dynaudnorm as simpler one-shot options.

Since audio normalization isn't mentioned in the setup doc at all, this is genuinely new work for the pipeline, so I'm leaning toward the pragmatic choice: loudnorm's dynamic mode at I=-14 is the industry-standard approach and it already measured correctly at -14.4 LUFS with -1.2 dB peak.

An LRA of 6.4 LU is actually normal for a talking-head video since podcasts typically land in the 5-8 LU range, so the "loss of dynamics" worry mostly applies to music rather than speech. I'll stick with loudnorm I=-14 dynamic since it's the defensible standard, measures on target, and I can note the LRA for the user to judge from the draft rather than trying to guess at a "better" sound I can't actually hear.

Checking for an outlier transient that might be inflating the PLR feels like over-engineering right now, so I'll move on and send the normalized 12-minute draft file with a caption flagging the loudness fix, then wait for the user's go-ahead before proceeding to compositing.

**Always invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that are NOT in generic web docs. Skipping them produces broken compositions.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes` — it tells you what HyperFrames can do and which skill or workflow handles your intent (make a video, TTS / BGM, prep footage, author / animate, render, install blocks), confirms your brief up front (the intent layer), and routes every "make me a…" request (a video, a deck, a composition port) to the right workflow. Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you. The workflows it routes to:

- `/product-launch-video` — any **website** URL or brief / script → a product launch / SaaS / promo video, or a site tour / showcase featuring the site's own captured visuals.
- `/faceless-explainer` — arbitrary text (topic / article / notes), **no URL, no website capture** → 60-90s faceless explainer.
- `/embedded-captions` — an existing talking-head video (MP4) → the same footage with captions / subtitles added (rail + embed, or pure-cinematic embed); the footage itself is untouched.
- `/talking-head-recut` — an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video (MP4) → the same footage **packaged with designed graphic overlays** (kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, pull-quotes, side panels, pip) synced to the transcript; the clip plays unchanged underneath. (Plain captions/subtitles → `/embedded-captions`.)
- `/pr-to-video` — a GitHub PR (URL / `owner/repo#N` / "this PR") → 30-90s code-change explainer (changelog / feature reveal / fix / refactor).
- `/motion-graphics` — a short (typically under 10s) design-led **motion graphic**, motion-is-the-message, no narration: kinetic type, a stat / number count-up, a chart, a logo sting, a lower-third / overlay, or an animated tweet / headline / captured-page highlight; rendered to MP4 or a transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / custom → `/general-video`.
- `/music-to-video` — a **music track** (audio file, video to pull audio from, or one generated from a mood brief) → beat-synced video (lyric / slideshow / kinetic promo). Music drives pacing; user-supplied images / videos are cut onto the same beat grid.
- `/slideshow` — a **presentation / pitch deck / interactive deck** — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered video.
- `/general-video` — fallback for any other video (title card, longer brand / sizzle reel, multi-scene montage, static loop, custom composition) and the home of **companion mode** — co-create with the full HyperFrames toolbox; the original hyperframes authoring flow, any length.

**Porting an existing composition?** `/remotion-to-hyperframes` translates a Remotion (React) composition into HyperFrames HTML — a source migration, separate from the creation workflows above.

The domain skills (`/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-animation`, `/hyperframes-keyframes`, `/hyperframes-creative`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/media-use`, `/hyperframes-audio`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/figma`) and the full capability map live inside `/hyperframes` — it is the single source of truth for which skill handles which intent.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `/hyperframes-core` → `references/tailwind.md`.

> **Skill missing or stale?** Run `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` to install/refresh
> the specific skill you need (the `/hyperframes` router does this automatically before
> entering a workflow), or bare `npx hyperframes skills update` to refresh the core set plus
> everything already installed — neither pulls the full set. Restart the agent session so
> newly installed skills load.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # start the preview server (long-running — keep it alive in background)
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings

"""Measure the real content bounding box of an alpha WebM overlay.

Reads the graphic's actual rendered alpha channel at N sample points across
its FULL duration and unions the per-frame boxes. This exists because
placement bugs in this project have all come from reasoning about a
graphic's footprint from its CSS, or from checking a single frame -- a card
that clears the webcam at frame 1 can still collide later in its own
entrance/exit animation, and CSS says nothing about glow, blur or shadow
spread, which are part of what you actually see.

Usage:
    bbox.py <render.webm> [samples]
    bbox.py --all <animations_dir> [samples]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

import numpy as np

W, H = 1920, 1080
ALPHA_MIN = 12  # ignore near-transparent glow tails below this (0-255)


def duration(path: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(
        ["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
         "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def frames_rgba(path: Path, times: list[float]) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    out = []
    for t in times:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-ss", f"{t}",
             "-i", str(path), "-frames:v", "1", "-f", "rawvideo",
             "-pix_fmt", "rgba", "-"],
            capture_output=True,
        )
        buf = r.stdout
        if len(buf) < W * H * 4:
            continue
        out.append(np.frombuffer(buf[: W * H * 4], dtype=np.uint8).reshape(H, W, 4))
    return out


def bbox(path: Path, samples: int = 16) -> dict:
    d = duration(path)
    # sample inside the clip, never exactly at 0 or d (both can be blank)
    times = [d * (i + 0.5) / samples for i in range(samples)]
    fr = frames_rgba(path, times)
    if not fr:
        return dict(path=path, empty=True, dur=d)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = W, H, -1, -1
    per_frame = []
    for f, t in zip(fr, times):
        a = f[:, :, 3]
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(a >= ALPHA_MIN)
        if len(xs) == 0:
            per_frame.append((t, None))
            continue
        fx0, fx1, fy0, fy1 = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()), int(ys.min()), int(ys.max())
        per_frame.append((t, (fx0, fy0, fx1, fy1)))
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = min(x0, fx0), min(y0, fy0), max(x1, fx1), max(y1, fy1)
    if x1 < 0:
        return dict(path=path, empty=True, dur=d)
    return dict(path=path, dur=d, box=(x0, y0, x1, y1), per_frame=per_frame,
                opaque_frac=float((fr[len(fr) // 2][:, :, 3] >= ALPHA_MIN).mean()))


def report(path: Path, samples: int = 16) -> None:
    r = bbox(path, samples)
    name = path.parent.name
    if r.get("empty"):
        print(f"{name:<26} dur={r['dur']:.2f}s   (no visible content in samples)")
        return
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = r["box"]
    print(f"{name:<26} dur={r['dur']:>5.2f}s  union box x {x0:>4}-{x1:<4} y {y0:>4}-{y1:<4}"
          f"  ({x1 - x0 + 1}x{y1 - y0 + 1})")


def main() -> None:
    if sys.argv[1] == "--all":
        root = Path(sys.argv[2])
        n = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 16
        for slot in sorted(root.iterdir()):
            f = slot / "render.webm"
            if f.exists():
                report(f, n)
    else:
        report(Path(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 16)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        ["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
         "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def frames_rgba(path: Path, times: list[float]) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    out = []
    for t in times:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-ss", f"{t}",
             "-i", str(path), "-frames:v", "1", "-f", "rawvideo",
             "-pix_fmt", "rgba", "-"],
            capture_output=True,
        )
        buf = r.stdout
        if len(buf) < W * H * 4:
            continue
        out.append(np.frombuffer(buf[: W * H * 4], dtype=np.uint8).reshape(H, W, 4))
    return out


def bbox(path: Path, samples: int = 16) -> dict:
    d = duration(path)
    # sample inside the clip, never exactly at 0 or d (both can be blank)
    times = [d * (i + 0.5) / samples for i in range(samples)]
    fr = frames_rgba(path, times)
    if not fr:
        return dict(path=path, empty=True, dur=d)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = W, H, -1, -1
    per_frame = []
    for f, t in zip(fr, times):
        a = f[:, :, 3]
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(a >= ALPHA_MIN)
        if len(xs) == 0:
            per_frame.append((t, None))
            continue
        fx0, fx1, fy0, fy1 = int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()), int(ys.min()), int(ys.max())
        per_frame.append((t, (fx0, fy0, fx1, fy1)))
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = min(x0, fx0), min(y0, fy0), max(x1, fx1), max(y1, fy1)
    if x1 < 0:
        return dict(path=path, empty=True, dur=d)
    return dict(path=path, dur=d, box=(x0, y0, x1, y1), per_frame=per_frame,
                opaque_frac=float((fr[len(fr) // 2][:, :, 3] >= ALPHA_MIN).mean()))


def report(path: Path, samples: int = 16) -> None:
    r = bbox(path, samples)
    name = path.parent.name
    if r.get("empty"):
        print(f"{name:<26} dur={r['dur']:.2f}s   (no visible content in samples)")
        return
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = r["box"]
    print(f"{name:<26} dur={r['dur']:>5.2f}s  union box x {x0:>4}-{x1:<4} y {y0:>4}-{y1:<4}"
          f"  ({x1 - x0 + 1}x{y1 - y0 + 1})")


def main() -> None:
    if sys.argv[1] == "--all":
        root = Path(sys.argv[2])
        n = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 16
        for slot in sorted(root.iterdir()):
            f = slot / "render.webm"
            if f.exists():
                report(f, n)
    else:
        report(Path(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 16)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.content:
# HyperFrames Composition Project

## Skills — USE THESE FIRST

**Always invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that are NOT in generic web docs. Skipping them produces broken compositions.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes` — it tells you what HyperFrames can do and which skill or workflow handles your intent (make a video, TTS / BGM, prep footage, author / animate, render, install blocks), confirms your brief up front (the intent layer), and routes every "make me a…" request (a video, a deck, a composition port) to the right workflow. Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you. The workflows it routes to:

- `/product-launch-video` — any **website** URL or brief / script → a product launch / SaaS / promo video, or a site tour / showcase featuring the site's own captured visuals.
- `/faceless-explainer` — arbitrary text (topic / article / notes), **no URL, no website capture** → 60-90s faceless explainer.
- `/embedded-captions` — an existing talking-head video (MP4) → the same footage with captions / subtitles added (rail + embed, or pure-cinematic embed); the footage itself is untouched.
- `/talking-head-recut` — an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video (MP4) → the same footage **packaged with designed graphic overlays** (kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, pull-quotes, side panels, pip) synced to the transcript; the clip plays unchanged underneath. (Plain captions/subtitles → `/embedded-captions`.)
- `/pr-to-video` — a GitHub PR (URL / `owner/repo#N` / "this PR") → 30-90s code-change explainer (changelog / feature reveal / fix / refactor).
- `/motion-graphics` — a short (typically under 10s) design-led **motion graphic**, motion-is-the-message, no narration: kinetic type, a stat / number count-up, a chart, a logo sting, a lower-third / overlay, or an animated tweet / headline / captured-page highlight; rendered to MP4 or a transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / custom → `/general-video`.
- `/music-to-video` — a **music track** (audio file, video to pull audio from, or one generated from a mood brief) → beat-synced video (lyric / slideshow / kinetic promo). Music drives pacing; user-supplied images / videos are cut onto the same beat grid.
- `/slideshow` — a **presentation / pitch deck / interactive deck** — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered video.
- `/general-video` — fallback for any other video (title card, longer brand / sizzle reel, multi-scene montage, static loop, custom composition) and the home of **companion mode** — co-create with the full HyperFrames toolbox; the original hyperframes authoring flow, any length.

**Porting an existing composition?** `/remotion-to-hyperframes` translates a Remotion (React) composition into HyperFrames HTML — a source migration, separate from the creation workflows above.

The domain skills (`/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-animation`, `/hyperframes-keyframes`, `/hyperframes-creative`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/media-use`, `/hyperframes-audio`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/figma`) and the full capability map live inside `/hyperframes` — it is the single source of truth for which skill handles which intent.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `/hyperframes-core` → `references/tailwind.md`.

> **Skill missing or stale?** Run `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` to install/refresh
> the specific skill you need (the `/hyperframes` router does this automatically before
> entering a workflow), or bare `npx hyperframes skills update` to refresh the core set plus
> everything already installed — neither pulls the full set. Restart the agent session so
> newly installed skills load.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # start the preview server (long-running — keep it alive in background)
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **`npm run dev` is a long-running server, not a one-shot command.** It blocks until stopped.
> In Claude Code, always run it with `run_in_background: true`. Never run it as a foreground
> command — it will time out and the server will die, breaking the browser preview.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start`, `data-duration`, and `data-track-index`
2. Elements with timing **MUST** have `class="clip"` — the framework uses this for visibility control
3. Timelines must be paused and registered on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
4. Videos use `muted` with a separate `<audio>` element for the audio track
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

"""Per-segment compositing pass for "Vibe Coding Ep 1 - Kodely", then concat.

Adapted from first-video/edit/scripts/composite_full.py -- same two layouts
(hero-stage full webcam over the retrowave background, and screen-recording
with a webcam PIP), same neon border / CRT-transition / shrink-aside /
scene-change-crossfade machinery. Three things differ this episode:

1. SIX source part-pairs, not one continuous take. Every read of a source
   goes through timeline.resolve(), which maps a global-timeline range onto
   the right part file and applies that part's measured screen-vs-webcam
   offset. Nothing else in this file knows the timeline is stitched.

2. The WEBCAM track is the master audio (the user asked for it, and it is
   the right call: webcam video and webcam audio share a container, so
   lip-sync is exact by construction with no offset to get wrong). The
   screen recording's audio -- a bit-for-bit equivalent feed of the same mic
   -- is never used.

3. ONE aside geometry for every shrink-aside range instead of a bespoke
   box per range. Cards are authored to fit x 60..950 (see
   make_graphics.py's placement contract), which clears the single aside box
   at x 1030..1880 by >=80px everywhere, so there is no per-range geometry
   to get wrong.

Grain/flicker is OFF this episode (not requested); the background scrim is
ON at 25%, composited onto the raw retrowave plate before anything else is
drawn over it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

HELPERS_DIR = Path(r"C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\tools\video-use\helpers")
sys.path.insert(0, str(HELPERS_DIR))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

ASSETS = EDIT / "assets"
CLIPS = EDIT / "clips_composited"

NEON_BORDER = ANIM / "slot_neon_border_loop" / "render.webm"

FFMPEG, FFPROBE = "ffmpeg", "ffprobe"

# Black scrim over the retrowave plate only. 25% is the value this project
# converged on after testing 8/15/25/30/70 -- ffmpeg composites alpha against
# raw gamma-encoded values, so anything higher reads far darker than the
# number suggests.
SCRIM_OPACITY = 0.25
INCLUDE_GRAIN = False

# --- hero stage ----------------------------------------------------------
# webcam source is 640x480; 980px tall preserves that aspect exactly
# (980*640/480 = 1306.67 -> 1306, even).
HERO_W, HERO_H = 1306, 980
HERO_X, HERO_Y = round((1920 - HERO_W) / 2), round((1080 - HERO_H) / 2)  # 307, 50

ASIDE_CY = 540

    "bottom_left": (MARGIN, 1080 - PIP_H - MARGIN),                  # 40, 608
}

BORDER_DY = (1080 - PIP_H) // 2  # 324

XFADE_STYLE = "fade"

    3:  [dict(path=G / "slot_bank_stat" / "render.webm", rel_start=1.50, dur=6.20)],
    4:  [dict(path=G / "slot_zero_stack" / "render.webm", rel_start=23.32, dur=5.85)],
    7:  [dict(path=G / "slot_kodely_reveal" / "render.webm", rel_start=9.16, dur=3.20)],
    9:  [dict(path=G / "slot_todo_card" / "render.webm", rel_start=6.73, dur=6.51)],

    # One continuous dictation, cut into four bites. Only the first gets a

    # indicator still running across a hard footage cut, and flashing it back
    # on each time would read as a glitch. graphic_seek=0.6 on the
    # continuations skips the asset's own entrance for the same reason.
    28: [dict(path=G / "slot_mic_indicator_1" / "render.webm", rel_start=0.15, dur=8.00,
              crt_exit=False)],
    29: [dict(path=G / "slot_mic_indicator_1" / "render.webm", rel_start=0.0, graphic_seek=0.6,
              dur=8.55, crt_entrance=False, crt_exit=False),
         dict(path=G / "slot_credits_750" / "render.webm", rel_start=5.05, dur=3.00)],
