    31: [dict(path=G / "slot_mic_indicator_1" / "render.webm", rel_start=0.0, graphic_seek=0.6,
              dur=5.73, crt_entrance=False)],
    34: [dict(path=G / "slot_tag_nxeon" / "render.webm", rel_start=10.00, dur=2.60)],
    36: [dict(path=G / "slot_board_stat" / "render.webm", rel_start=2.80, dur=15.10)],
    39: [dict(path=G / "slot_kodely_live" / "render.webm", rel_start=13.75, dur=6.15)],
    # Second dictation stretch, same continuation rule across its own cut.
    47: [dict(path=G / "slot_mic_indicator_1" / "render.webm", rel_start=0.15, dur=18.70,
              crt_exit=False)],
    48: [dict(path=G / "slot_mic_indicator_1" / "render.webm", rel_start=0.0, graphic_seek=0.6,
              dur=11.30, crt_entrance=False)],
    52: [dict(path=G / "slot_time_90" / "render.webm", rel_start=2.71, dur=5.85)],
    59: [dict(path=G / "slot_tag_subscribe" / "render.webm", rel_start=3.89, dur=2.60)],
}

# Hero-stage ranges whose graphic would otherwise be drawn over the
# presenter: the webcam eases down to the aside box and back instead.
DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES = {3, 4, 7, 9, 39, 52, 59}


def run(cmd: list[str]) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", " ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:2000])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    """Real encoded duration -- xfade's offset is measured on input 0's own
    timeline, and nominal (end-start) drifts from what actually got encoded."""
    r = subprocess.run(
        [FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
         "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FFPROBE FAILED:", path, r.stderr[-1500:])
        sys.exit(1)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def afade(dur: float) -> str:
    fo = max(0.0, dur - 0.03)
    return f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={fo:.3f}:d=0.03"


def overlay_chain(label_in: str, overlays: list[dict], next_input_idx: int):
    """Composite N alpha-webm graphics onto [label_in], each windowed to its
    own (rel_start, rel_start+dur) and each wrapped in the CRT power-on/
    power-off squash+flash unless that edge is disabled."""
    CRT_DUR = 0.18
    frag, extra_args, label, idx = "", [], label_in, next_input_idx
    for i, ov in enumerate(overlays):
        seek = ov.get("graphic_seek", 0)
        # -c:v libvpx-vp9 is required: the native vp9 decoder silently drops
        # the alpha channel here and renders the card as an opaque box.
        extra_args += ["-itsoffset", f"{ov['rel_start']}", "-ss", f"{seek}",
                       "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(ov["path"])]
        start = ov["rel_start"]
        end = start + ov["dur"]
        crt = crt_transition_filter(
            entrance_dur=CRT_DUR if ov.get("crt_entrance", True) else 0.0,
            exit_dur=CRT_DUR if ov.get("crt_exit", True) else 0.0,
            window_start=start, window_end=end,
        )
        frag += f"[{idx}:v]{crt}[go{i}crt];"
        frag += (f"[{label}][go{i}crt]overlay=x=0:y=0:"
                 f"enable='between(t\\,{start}\\,{end})'[go{i}];")
        label = f"go{i}"
        idx += 1
    return frag, extra_args, label, idx


def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
    """Ken-Burns push-in. Supersamples 2x before zoompan so the crop window's
    per-frame pixel rounding lands at a quarter-output-pixel instead of
    dithering visibly at the top of the ease."""
    fps = 60
    rsf, rdf = z["rs"] * fps, z["rd"] * fps
    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy are 1x source coords
    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
        orsf, ordf = z["out_rs"] * fps, z["out_rd"] * fps
        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
        raw = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
    else:
        raw = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw})*2000)/2000"
    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"


def _shrink_u_expr(gs: float, ge: float, td: float) -> str:
    """0..1 blend: 0 = hero size/position, 1 = settled aside. Eases 0->1 over
    `td` ending exactly as the graphic appears, holds, then eases back."""
    ws, we = gs - td, ge + td
    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    return f"min((1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))\\,(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3)))"


def _hero_transform(windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
    aside_x, aside_y = ASIDE_CX - ASIDE_W / 2, ASIDE_CY - ASIDE_H / 2
    u = _shrink_u_expr(*windows[0], td)
    for w in windows[1:]:
        u = f"max({u}\\,{_shrink_u_expr(*w, td)})"
    return dict(
        w=f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({ASIDE_W}-{HERO_W})*{u})/2))",
        h=f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({ASIDE_H}-{HERO_H})*{u})/2))",
        x=f"({HERO_X}+({aside_x}-{HERO_X})*{u})",
        y=f"({HERO_Y}+({aside_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u})",
        u=u,
    )


def build_webcam_primary(idx: int, r: dict, out: Path) -> None:
    """Hero stage: scrimmed retrowave plate, neon border, big webcam, then any
    graphics. Ranges in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES ease the webcam+border down to
    the aside box for their graphic's window and back."""
    src = resolve(r["start"], r["end"])
    dur = src["dur"]
    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays

    # inputs: 0=webcam(v+a) 1=retrowave 2=neon border 3=mask [4=blank canvas]
    inputs = [
        "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
        "-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG),
        "-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER),
        # -loop 1 + -framerate 60: the mask must be an infinite 60fps stream so
        # its own eval=frame scale stays in lockstep with the webcam's. A single
        # still frame freezes the mask's scale while the webcam's keeps
        # re-evaluating, and the size mismatch corrupts alphamerge.
        "-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png"),
    ]
    next_idx = 4
    if dynamic:
        inputs += ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", "color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:r=60"]
        next_idx = 5

    keep = 1 - SCRIM_OPACITY
    filt = f"[1:v]colorchannelmixer=rr={keep}:gg={keep}:bb={keep}[bg];"

    if dynamic:
        windows = [(o["rel_start"], o["rel_start"] + o["dur"]) for o in overlays]
        tf = _hero_transform(windows)
        wc_cx = f"(({tf['x']})+({tf['w']})/2)"
        wc_cy = f"(({tf['y']})+({tf['h']})/2)"
        s = f"({NEON_SCALE_HERO}+({NEON_SCALE_ASIDE}-{NEON_SCALE_HERO})*{tf['u']})"
        bw, bh = f"(2*round((1920*{s})/2))", f"(2*round((1080*{s})/2))"
        # alphamerge needs constant-size inputs every frame, and pad's x/y
        # expressions do not expose `t`. So: scale to the frame-varying box,
        # then overlay that onto a constant-size FULL-FRAME transparent canvas
        # at the box's absolute x(t)/y(t). The canvas must be 1920x1080 -- a
        # hero-sized one clips the aside box, which sits outside the hero
        # box's own footprint.
        filt += (
            f"[0:v]scale=w='{tf['w']}':h='{tf['h']}':eval=frame:flags=bilinear[wcs];"
            f"[3:v]scale=w='{tf['w']}':h='{tf['h']}':eval=frame:flags=bilinear[mks];"
            f"[4:v]split=2[bl1][bl2];"
            f"[bl1][wcs]overlay=x='{tf['x']}':y='{tf['y']}'[wc];"
            f"[bl2][mks]overlay=x='{tf['x']}':y='{tf['y']}'[mk];"
            f"[wc][mk]alphamerge[wcr];"
            # The border does NOT go through the blank-canvas detour: it has no
            # alphamerge step, and routing it through a second overlay drops its
            # alpha and paints an opaque black frame over the background.
            f"[2:v]scale=w='{bw}':h='{bh}':eval=frame:flags=bilinear[nbs];"
            f"[bg][nbs]overlay=x='(({wc_cx})-({bw})/2)':y='(({wc_cy})-({bh})/2)'[bgb];"
            f"[bgb][wcr]overlay=x=0:y=0[base];"
        )
    else:
        filt += (
            f"[0:v]scale={HERO_W}:{HERO_H}[wc];"
            f"[3:v]scale={HERO_W}:{HERO_H}[mk];"
            f"[wc][mk]alphamerge[wcr];"
            f"[2:v]scale=w='iw*{NEON_SCALE_HERO}':h='ih*{NEON_SCALE_HERO}',"
            f"crop=1920:1080:(iw-1920)/2:(ih-1080)/2[bh];"
            f"[bg][bh]overlay=x=0:y=0[bgb];"
            f"[bgb][wcr]overlay=x={HERO_X}:y={HERO_Y}[base];"
        )

    filt += f"[0:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    extra, final = [], "base"
    if overlays:
        frag, extra, final, _ = overlay_chain("base", overlays, next_idx)
        filt += ";" + frag

    run([FFMPEG, "-y", *inputs, *extra, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", f"[{final}]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", "-r", "60", "-t", f"{dur}",
         str(out), "-loglevel", "error"])


def build_screen_primary(idx: int, r: dict, prev_pos: str | None, out: Path) -> None:
    src = resolve(r["start"], r["end"])
    dur = src["dur"]
    pos_key = r.get("pip", "bottom_right")
    px, py = POS[pos_key]

    if prev_pos is not None and prev_pos != pos_key:
        ppx, _ = POS[prev_pos]
        ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max(t/{SLIDE_DUR}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
        x_expr = f"'{ppx}+({px}-{ppx})*{ease}'"
        shx = f"'{ppx - SHADOW_MARGIN}+({px}-{ppx})*{ease}'"
        bx = f"'{ppx - BORDER_DX}+({px}-{ppx})*{ease}'"
    else:
        x_expr, shx, bx = f"{px}", f"{px - SHADOW_MARGIN}", f"{px - BORDER_DX}"

    base = zoom_filter(ZOOMS[idx]) if idx in ZOOMS else "scale=1920:1080"
    # back to front: base -> shadow -> neon border -> masked webcam
    filt = (
        f"[0:v]{base}[bs];"
        f"[1:v]scale={PIP_W}:{PIP_H}[wc];"
        f"[wc][2:v]alphamerge[wcr];"
        f"[bs][3:v]overlay=x={shx}:y={py - SHADOW_MARGIN}[b1];"
        f"[b1][4:v]overlay=x={bx}:y={py - BORDER_DY}[b2];"
        f"[b2][wcr]overlay=x={x_expr}:y={py}[vout];"
        f"[1:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    )
    extra, final = [], "vout"
    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
    if overlays:
        frag, extra, final, _ = overlay_chain("vout", overlays, 5)
        filt += ";" + frag

    run([FFMPEG, "-y",
         "-ss", f"{src['screen_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["screen_path"],
         "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
         "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png"),
         "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_shadow.png"),
         "-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER),
         *extra, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", f"[{final}]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", "-r", "60", "-t", f"{dur}",
         str(out), "-loglevel", "error"])


def build_transition(a: Path, b: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    """Replace a hard cut with one merged clip: all of A crossfading into all
    of B. -pix_fmt yuv420p is forced explicitly -- left to negotiate, xfade
    drifts to yuv444p, which passes ffmpeg's own decode check but breaks
    playback partway through once concatenated with yuv420p segments."""
    dur_a = probe_duration(a)
    offset = dur_a - XFADE_DUR
    if offset < 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {a} ({dur_a}s) too short for a {XFADE_DUR}s crossfade")
        sys.exit(1)
    filt = (f"[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition={XFADE_STYLE}:duration={XFADE_DUR}:offset={offset}[v];"
            f"[0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d={XFADE_DUR}[a]")
    run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-i", str(a), "-i", str(b), "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out), "-loglevel", "error"])


def main() -> None:
    edl = json.loads((EDIT / "edl.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ranges = edl["ranges"]

    prev_pos = None
    clip_paths = []
    for i, r in enumerate(ranges):
        out = CLIPS / f"seg_{i:02d}.mp4"
        clip_paths.append(out)
        hero = r["layout"] == "webcam_primary"
        if out.exists():
            print(f"[{i:02d}] cached")
            if not hero:
                prev_pos = r.get("pip", "bottom_right")
            continue
        if hero:
            build_webcam_primary(i, r, out)
            extra = "  +shrink-aside" if i in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES else ""
            g = f"  +{len(OVERLAYS[i])}gfx" if i in OVERLAYS else ""
            print(f"[{i:02d}] hero    {r['start']:>8.2f}-{r['end']:<8.2f} {r['beat']}{g}{extra}")
        else:
            build_screen_primary(i, r, prev_pos, out)
            slide = "  +slide" if prev_pos and prev_pos != r.get("pip") else ""
            z = "  +zoom" if i in ZOOMS else ""
            g = f"  +{len(OVERLAYS[i])}gfx" if i in OVERLAYS else ""
            print(f"[{i:02d}] screen  {r['start']:>8.2f}-{r['end']:<8.2f} {r['beat']}  "
                  f"{r.get('pip')}{z}{g}{slide}")
            prev_pos = r.get("pip", "bottom_right")

    # --- scene-change crossfades ----------------------------------------
    # Boundaries where the layout genuinely changes scene type. Consecutive
    # boundaries that share a segment (here 51->52->53, a hero beat sandwiched
    # between two screen beats) are folded into ONE chain and merged left to
    # right; treating them as two independent pairs would emit segment 52
    # twice in the concat list.
    bounds = []
    for i in range(1, len(ranges)):
        if ranges[i]["layout"] != ranges[i - 1]["layout"]:
            bounds.append((i - 1, i))
    chains: list[list[int]] = []
    for a, b in bounds:
        if chains and chains[-1][-1] == a:
            chains[-1].append(b)
        else:
            chains.append([a, b])

    TRANS = EDIT / "clips_transitions"
    TRANS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    merged: dict[int, Path] = {}
    skip: set[int] = set()
    for chain in chains:
        cur = clip_paths[chain[0]]
        for n, nxt in enumerate(chain[1:], start=1):
            tag = "_".join(f"{c:02d}" for c in chain[: n + 1])
            t_out = TRANS / f"trans_{tag}.mp4"
            if t_out.exists():
                print(f"[trans {tag}] cached")
            else:
                build_transition(cur, clip_paths[nxt], t_out)
                print(f"[trans {tag}] built ({XFADE_DUR}s {XFADE_STYLE})")
            cur = t_out
            skip.add(nxt)
        merged[chain[0]] = cur

    final_paths = []
    for i, p in enumerate(clip_paths):
        if i in merged:
            final_paths.append(merged[i])
        elif i in skip:
            continue
        else:
            final_paths.append(p)

    list_path = EDIT / "concat_list.txt"
    list_path.write_text("\n".join(f"file '{p.as_posix()}'" for p in final_paths),
                         encoding="utf-8")
    out_path = EDIT / "composited_draft.mp4"
    run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", str(list_path),
         "-c", "copy", str(out_path), "-loglevel", "error"])
    d = probe_duration(out_path)
    print(f"\ndone: {out_path}  ({d:.1f}s = {d / 60:.2f} min)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Per-segment compositing pass for "Vibe Coding Ep 1 - Kodely", then concat.

Adapted from first-video/edit/scripts/composite_full.py -- same two layouts
(hero-stage full webcam over the retrowave background, and screen-recording
with a webcam PIP), same neon border / CRT-transition / shrink-aside /
scene-change-crossfade machinery. Three things differ this episode:

1. SIX source part-pairs, not one continuous take. Every read of a source
   goes through timeline.resolve(), which maps a global-timeline range onto
   the right part file and applies that part's measured screen-vs-webcam
   offset. Nothing else in this file knows the timeline is stitched.

2. The WEBCAM track is the master audio (the user asked for it, and it is
   the right call: webcam video and webcam audio share a container, so
   lip-sync is exact by construction with no offset to get wrong). The
   screen recording's audio -- a bit-for-bit equivalent feed of the same mic
   -- is never used.

3. ONE aside geometry for every shrink-aside range instead of a bespoke
   box per range. Cards are authored to fit x 60..950 (see
   make_graphics.py's placement contract), which clears the single aside box
   at x 1030..1880 by >=80px everywhere, so there is no per-range geometry
   to get wrong.

Grain/flicker is OFF this episode (not requested); the background scrim is
ON at 25%, composited onto the raw retrowave plate before anything else is
drawn over it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

HELPERS_DIR = Path(r"C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\tools\video-use\helpers")
sys.path.insert(0, str(HELPERS_DIR))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from crt_transition import crt_transition_filter  # noqa: E402
from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ANIM = EDIT / "animations"
ASSETS = EDIT / "assets"
CLIPS = EDIT / "clips_composited"
CLIPS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

RETROWAVE_BG = ANIM / "slot_retrowave_bg_loop" / "render.mp4"
NEON_BORDER = ANIM / "slot_neon_border_loop" / "render.webm"

FFMPEG, FFPROBE = "ffmpeg", "ffprobe"

# Black scrim over the retrowave plate only. 25% is the value this project
# converged on after testing 8/15/25/30/70 -- ffmpeg composites alpha against
# raw gamma-encoded values, so anything higher reads far darker than the
# number suggests.
SCRIM_OPACITY = 0.25
INCLUDE_GRAIN = False

# --- hero stage ----------------------------------------------------------
# webcam source is 640x480; 980px tall preserves that aspect exactly
# (980*640/480 = 1306.67 -> 1306, even).
HERO_W, HERO_H = 1306, 980
HERO_X, HERO_Y = round((1920 - HERO_W) / 2), round((1080 - HERO_H) / 2)  # 307, 50

# Shrink-aside resting box: 65% of hero, right-hand side, 40px in from the
# frame edge -> x 1030..1880, y 221..859.
ASIDE_W, ASIDE_H = 850, 638
ASIDE_MARGIN = 40
ASIDE_CX = 1920 - ASIDE_MARGIN - ASIDE_W // 2  # 1455
ASIDE_CY = 540
SHRINK_DUR = 0.5

# The neon border loop is authored as a 576x432 rounded rail centred on its
# own 1920x1080 frame, so scaling the whole frame by (box height / 432)
# grows the rail to exactly the box in play. Both boxes are ~4:3, same as the
# rail, so one scalar covers both axes.
PIP_W, PIP_H = 576, 432
NEON_SCALE_HERO = HERO_H / PIP_H     # 2.2685
NEON_SCALE_ASIDE = ASIDE_H / PIP_H   # 1.4769

MARGIN = 40
SHADOW_MARGIN = 60
POS = {
    "bottom_right": (1920 - PIP_W - MARGIN, 1080 - PIP_H - MARGIN),  # 1304, 608
    "bottom_left": (MARGIN, 1080 - PIP_H - MARGIN),                  # 40, 608

def run(cmd: list[str]) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", " ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:2000])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    """Real encoded duration -- xfade's offset is measured on input 0's own
    timeline, and nominal (end-start) drifts from what actually got encoded."""
    r = subprocess.run(
        [FFPROBE, "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
         "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FFPROBE FAILED:", path, r.stderr[-1500:])
        sys.exit(1)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def afade(dur: float) -> str:
    fo = max(0.0, dur - 0.03)
    return f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={fo:.3f}:d=0.03"


def overlay_chain(label_in: str, overlays: list[dict], next_input_idx: int):
    """Composite N alpha-webm graphics onto [label_in], each windowed to its
    own (rel_start, rel_start+dur) and each wrapped in the CRT power-on/
    power-off squash+flash unless that edge is disabled."""
    CRT_DUR = 0.18
    frag, extra_args, label, idx = "", [], label_in, next_input_idx
    for i, ov in enumerate(overlays):
        seek = ov.get("graphic_seek", 0)
        # -c:v libvpx-vp9 is required: the native vp9 decoder silently drops
        # the alpha channel here and renders the card as an opaque box.
        extra_args += ["-itsoffset", f"{ov['rel_start']}", "-ss", f"{seek}",
                       "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(ov["path"])]
        start = ov["rel_start"]
        end = start + ov["dur"]
        crt = crt_transition_filter(
            entrance_dur=CRT_DUR if ov.get("crt_entrance", True) else 0.0,
            exit_dur=CRT_DUR if ov.get("crt_exit", True) else 0.0,
            window_start=start, window_end=end,
        )
        frag += f"[{idx}:v]{crt}[go{i}crt];"
        frag += (f"[{label}][go{i}crt]overlay=x=0:y=0:"
                 f"enable='between(t\\,{start}\\,{end})'[go{i}];")
        label = f"go{i}"
        idx += 1
    return frag, extra_args, label, idx


def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
    """Ken-Burns push-in. Supersamples 2x before zoompan so the crop window's
    per-frame pixel rounding lands at a quarter-output-pixel instead of
    dithering visibly at the top of the ease."""
    fps = 60
    rsf, rdf = z["rs"] * fps, z["rd"] * fps
    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy are 1x source coords
    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
        orsf, ordf = z["out_rs"] * fps, z["out_rd"] * fps
        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
        raw = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
    else:
        raw = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw})*2000)/2000"
    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"


def _shrink_u_expr(gs: float, ge: float, td: float) -> str:
    """0..1 blend: 0 = hero size/position, 1 = settled aside. Eases 0->1 over
    `td` ending exactly as the graphic appears, holds, then eases back."""
    ws, we = gs - td, ge + td
    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
    return f"min((1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))\\,(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3)))"


def _hero_transform(windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
    aside_x, aside_y = ASIDE_CX - ASIDE_W / 2, ASIDE_CY - ASIDE_H / 2
    u = _shrink_u_expr(*windows[0], td)
    for w in windows[1:]:
        u = f"max({u}\\,{_shrink_u_expr(*w, td)})"
    return dict(
        w=f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({ASIDE_W}-{HERO_W})*{u})/2))",
        h=f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({ASIDE_H}-{HERO_H})*{u})/2))",
        x=f"({HERO_X}+({aside_x}-{HERO_X})*{u})",
        y=f"({HERO_Y}+({aside_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u})",
        u=u,
    )


def build_webcam_primary(idx: int, r: dict, out: Path) -> None:
    """Hero stage: scrimmed retrowave plate, neon border, big webcam, then any
    graphics. Ranges in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES ease the webcam+border down to
    the aside box for their graphic's window and back."""
    src = resolve(r["start"], r["end"])
    dur = src["dur"]
    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays

    # inputs: 0=webcam(v+a) 1=retrowave 2=neon border 3=mask [4=blank canvas]
    inputs = [
        "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
        "-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG),
        "-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER),
        # -loop 1 + -framerate 60: the mask must be an infinite 60fps stream so
        # its own eval=frame scale stays in lockstep with the webcam's. A single
        # still frame freezes the mask's scale while the webcam's keeps
        # re-evaluating, and the size mismatch corrupts alphamerge.
        "-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png"),
    ]
    next_idx = 4
    if dynamic:
        inputs += ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", "color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:r=60"]
        next_idx = 5

    keep = 1 - SCRIM_OPACITY
    filt = f"[1:v]colorchannelmixer=rr={keep}:gg={keep}:bb={keep}[bg];"

    if dynamic:
        windows = [(o["rel_start"], o["rel_start"] + o["dur"]) for o in overlays]
        tf = _hero_transform(windows)
        wc_cx = f"(({tf['x']})+({tf['w']})/2)"
        wc_cy = f"(({tf['y']})+({tf['h']})/2)"
        s = f"({NEON_SCALE_HERO}+({NEON_SCALE_ASIDE}-{NEON_SCALE_HERO})*{tf['u']})"
        bw, bh = f"(2*round((1920*{s})/2))", f"(2*round((1080*{s})/2))"
        # alphamerge needs constant-size inputs every frame, and pad's x/y
        # expressions do not expose `t`. So: scale to the frame-varying box,
        # then overlay that onto a constant-size FULL-FRAME transparent canvas
        # at the box's absolute x(t)/y(t). The canvas must be 1920x1080 -- a
        # hero-sized one clips the aside box, which sits outside the hero
        # box's own footprint.
        filt += (
            f"[0:v]scale=w='{tf['w']}':h='{tf['h']}':eval=frame:flags=bilinear[wcs];"
            f"[3:v]scale=w='{tf['w']}':h='{tf['h']}':eval=frame:flags=bilinear[mks];"
            f"[4:v]split=2[bl1][bl2];"
            f"[bl1][wcs]overlay=x='{tf['x']}':y='{tf['y']}'[wc];"
            f"[bl2][mks]overlay=x='{tf['x']}':y='{tf['y']}'[mk];"
            f"[wc][mk]alphamerge[wcr];"
            # The border does NOT go through the blank-canvas detour: it has no
            # alphamerge step, and routing it through a second overlay drops its
            # alpha and paints an opaque black frame over the background.
            f"[2:v]scale=w='{bw}':h='{bh}':eval=frame:flags=bilinear[nbs];"
            f"[bg][nbs]overlay=x='(({wc_cx})-({bw})/2)':y='(({wc_cy})-({bh})/2)'[bgb];"
            f"[bgb][wcr]overlay=x=0:y=0[base];"
        )
    else:
        filt += (
            f"[0:v]scale={HERO_W}:{HERO_H}[wc];"
            f"[3:v]scale={HERO_W}:{HERO_H}[mk];"
            f"[wc][mk]alphamerge[wcr];"
            f"[2:v]scale=w='iw*{NEON_SCALE_HERO}':h='ih*{NEON_SCALE_HERO}',"
            f"crop=1920:1080:(iw-1920)/2:(ih-1080)/2[bh];"
            f"[bg][bh]overlay=x=0:y=0[bgb];"
            f"[bgb][wcr]overlay=x={HERO_X}:y={HERO_Y}[base];"
        )

    filt += f"[0:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    extra, final = [], "base"
    if overlays:
        frag, extra, final, _ = overlay_chain("base", overlays, next_idx)
        filt += ";" + frag

    run([FFMPEG, "-y", *inputs, *extra, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", f"[{final}]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", "-r", "60", "-t", f"{dur}",
         str(out), "-loglevel", "error"])


def build_screen_primary(idx: int, r: dict, prev_pos: str | None, out: Path) -> None:
    src = resolve(r["start"], r["end"])
    dur = src["dur"]
    pos_key = r.get("pip", "bottom_right")
    px, py = POS[pos_key]

    if prev_pos is not None and prev_pos != pos_key:
        ppx, _ = POS[prev_pos]
        ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max(t/{SLIDE_DUR}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
        x_expr = f"'{ppx}+({px}-{ppx})*{ease}'"
        shx = f"'{ppx - SHADOW_MARGIN}+({px}-{ppx})*{ease}'"
        bx = f"'{ppx - BORDER_DX}+({px}-{ppx})*{ease}'"
    else:
        x_expr, shx, bx = f"{px}", f"{px - SHADOW_MARGIN}", f"{px - BORDER_DX}"

    base = zoom_filter(ZOOMS[idx]) if idx in ZOOMS else "scale=1920:1080"
    # back to front: base -> shadow -> neon border -> masked webcam
    filt = (
        f"[0:v]{base}[bs];"
        f"[1:v]scale={PIP_W}:{PIP_H}[wc];"
        f"[wc][2:v]alphamerge[wcr];"
        f"[bs][3:v]overlay=x={shx}:y={py - SHADOW_MARGIN}[b1];"
        f"[b1][4:v]overlay=x={bx}:y={py - BORDER_DY}[b2];"
        f"[b2][wcr]overlay=x={x_expr}:y={py}[vout];"
        f"[1:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    )
    extra, final = [], "vout"
    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
    if overlays:
        frag, extra, final, _ = overlay_chain("vout", overlays, 5)
        filt += ";" + frag

    run([FFMPEG, "-y",
         "-ss", f"{src['screen_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["screen_path"],
         "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
         "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png"),
         "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_shadow.png"),
         "-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER),
         *extra, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", f"[{final}]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", "-r", "60", "-t", f"{dur}",
         str(out), "-loglevel", "error"])


def build_transition(a: Path, b: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    """Replace a hard cut with one merged clip: all of A crossfading into all
    of B. -pix_fmt yuv420p is forced explicitly -- left to negotiate, xfade
    drifts to yuv444p, which passes ffmpeg's own decode check but breaks
    playback partway through once concatenated with yuv420p segments."""
    dur_a = probe_duration(a)
    offset = dur_a - XFADE_DUR
    if offset < 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {a} ({dur_a}s) too short for a {XFADE_DUR}s crossfade")
        sys.exit(1)
    filt = (f"[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition={XFADE_STYLE}:duration={XFADE_DUR}:offset={offset}[v];"
            f"[0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d={XFADE_DUR}[a]")
    run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-i", str(a), "-i", str(b), "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out), "-loglevel", "error"])


def main() -> None:
    edl = json.loads((EDIT / "edl.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ranges = edl["ranges"]

    prev_pos = None
    clip_paths = []
    for i, r in enumerate(ranges):
        out = CLIPS / f"seg_{i:02d}.mp4"
        clip_paths.append(out)
        hero = r["layout"] == "webcam_primary"
        if out.exists():
            print(f"[{i:02d}] cached")
            if not hero:
                prev_pos = r.get("pip", "bottom_right")
            continue
        if hero:
            build_webcam_primary(i, r, out)
            extra = "  +shrink-aside" if i in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES else ""
            g = f"  +{len(OVERLAYS[i])}gfx" if i in OVERLAYS else ""
            print(f"[{i:02d}] hero    {r['start']:>8.2f}-{r['end']:<8.2f} {r['beat']}{g}{extra}")
        else:
            build_screen_primary(i, r, prev_pos, out)
            slide = "  +slide" if prev_pos and prev_pos != r.get("pip") else ""
            z = "  +zoom" if i in ZOOMS else ""
            g = f"  +{len(OVERLAYS[i])}gfx" if i in OVERLAYS else ""
            print(f"[{i:02d}] screen  {r['start']:>8.2f}-{r['end']:<8.2f} {r['beat']}  "
                  f"{r.get('pip')}{z}{g}{slide}")
            prev_pos = r.get("pip", "bottom_right")

    # --- scene-change crossfades ----------------------------------------
    # Boundaries where the layout genuinely changes scene type. Consecutive
    # boundaries that share a segment (here 51->52->53, a hero beat sandwiched
    # between two screen beats) are folded into ONE chain and merged left to
    # right; treating them as two independent pairs would emit segment 52
    # twice in the concat list.
    bounds = []
    for i in range(1, len(ranges)):
        if ranges[i]["layout"] != ranges[i - 1]["layout"]:
            bounds.append((i - 1, i))
    chains: list[list[int]] = []
    for a, b in bounds:
        if chains and chains[-1][-1] == a:
            chains[-1].append(b)
        else:
            chains.append([a, b])

    TRANS = EDIT / "clips_transitions"
    TRANS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    merged: dict[int, Path] = {}
    skip: set[int] = set()
    for chain in chains:
        cur = clip_paths[chain[0]]
        for n, nxt in enumerate(chain[1:], start=1):
            tag = "_".join(f"{c:02d}" for c in chain[: n + 1])
            t_out = TRANS / f"trans_{tag}.mp4"
            if t_out.exists():
                print(f"[trans {tag}] cached")
            else:
                build_transition(cur, clip_paths[nxt], t_out)
                print(f"[trans {tag}] built ({XFADE_DUR}s {XFADE_STYLE})")
            cur = t_out
            skip.add(nxt)
        merged[chain[0]] = cur

    final_paths = []
    for i, p in enumerate(clip_paths):
        if i in merged:
            final_paths.append(merged[i])
        elif i in skip:
            continue
        else:
            final_paths.append(p)

    list_path = EDIT / "concat_list.txt"
    list_path.write_text("\n".join(f"file '{p.as_posix()}'" for p in final_paths),
                         encoding="utf-8")
    out_path = EDIT / "composited_draft.mp4"
    run([FFMPEG, "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", str(list_path),
         "-c", "copy", str(out_path), "-loglevel", "error"])
    d = probe_duration(out_path)
    print(f"\ndone: {out_path}  ({d:.1f}s = {d / 60:.2f} min)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Generate caption cues (output-timeline, per Hard Rule 5) from the EDL +
word-level transcript. Chunks into short word groups (glass-pill caption
style), breaking on punctuation or a silence gap, never spanning a cut.
Ranges with layout "intro_graphic" (or any layout you pass via
--skip-layout) are skipped -- assumed to carry their own on-screen kinetic
type, so this avoids double-captioning them.

Usage:
    python helpers/gen_caption_cues.py --edit-dir <dir> --source <name>
    python helpers/gen_caption_cues.py --edit-dir <dir> --source screen --max-chunk 6 --gap-break 0.5
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def gen_cues(edit_dir: Path, source: str, max_chunk: int, gap_break: float, skip_layouts: set[str]) -> list[dict]:
    edl = json.loads((edit_dir / "edl.json").read_text())
    words = json.loads((edit_dir / "transcripts" / f"{source}.json").read_text())["words"]
    words = sorted(words, key=lambda w: w["start"])

    cues: list[list[dict]] = []
    cum = 0.0
    for r in edl["ranges"]:
        dur = r["end"] - r["start"]
        if r.get("layout") in skip_layouts:
            cum += dur
            continue

        in_range = [w for w in words if w["type"] == "word" and r["start"] - 0.05 <= w["start"] < r["end"] + 0.05]

        chunk: list[dict] = []
        prev_end = None
        for w in in_range:
            gap = (w["start"] - prev_end) if prev_end is not None else 0
            if chunk and (gap >= gap_break or len(chunk) >= max_chunk):
                cues.append(chunk)
                chunk = []
            chunk.append(w)
            prev_end = w["end"]
            if w["text"].rstrip()[-1:] in ".!?" and len(chunk) >= 1:
                cues.append(chunk)
                chunk = []
        if chunk:
            cues.append(chunk)

def make_assets(
    out_dir: Path,
    pip_w: int = 576,
    pip_h: int = 432,
    radius: int = 28,
    border: int = 3,
    shadow_margin: int = 60,
    shadow_blur: int = 24,
    shadow_opacity: int = 130,
    neon_glow: bool = False,
    neon_colors: tuple = ((255, 122, 168), (255, 179, 122), (207, 63, 196)),  # liquid-glass brand gradient
    neon_margin: int = 50,
    neon_blur: int = 16,
    neon_opacity: int = 255,
) -> None:
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # 1. Alpha mask for the webcam video itself (rounded corners) -- fed into
    #    ffmpeg's alphamerge filter against the scaled webcam feed.
    mask = rounded_rect_mask(pip_w, pip_h, radius)
    mask.save(out_dir / "pip_mask.png")

    # 2. Glass-edge highlight ring (subtle translucent white border -- the
    #    "liquid glass" cue: light catching an angled edge).
    ring = Image.new("RGBA", (pip_w, pip_h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ring)
    d.rounded_rectangle(
        [border / 2, border / 2, pip_w - 1 - border / 2, pip_h - 1 - border / 2],
        radius=radius, outline=(255, 255, 255, 110), width=border,
    )
    ring.save(out_dir / "pip_ring.png")

    # 3. Soft drop shadow, oversized canvas so the blur has room -- placed
    #    centered-behind the PIP at (px - shadow_margin, py - shadow_margin)
    #    so the shadow peeks out symmetrically on all sides.
    canvas_w, canvas_h = pip_w + shadow_margin * 2, pip_h + shadow_margin * 2
    shadow = Image.new("RGBA", (canvas_w, canvas_h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(shadow)
    d.rounded_rectangle(
        [shadow_margin, shadow_margin + 6, shadow_margin + pip_w, shadow_margin + pip_h + 6],
        radius=radius, fill=(0, 0, 0, shadow_opacity),
    )
    shadow = shadow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(shadow_blur))
    shadow.save(out_dir / "pip_shadow.png")

    if neon_glow:
        # Colored rim-light halo just outside the PIP edge -- drawn as a
        # gradient-stroked rounded-rect (not a filled blob), then blurred, so
        # it reads as a glowing OUTLINE around the webcam rather than a
        # colored shadow blob behind it. Composite this BEHIND the webcam

    shadow_blur: int = 24,

    neon_colors: tuple = ((255, 122, 168), (255, 179, 122), (207, 63, 196)),  # liquid-glass brand gradient

    neon_blur: int = 16,
    neon_opacity: int = 255,

    #    ffmpeg's alphamerge filter against the scaled webcam feed.

    mask.save(out_dir / "pip_mask.png")

    # 2. Glass-edge highlight ring (subtle translucent white border -- the
    #    "liquid glass" cue: light catching an angled edge).
    ring = Image.new("RGBA", (pip_w, pip_h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ring)
    d.rounded_rectangle(
        [border / 2, border / 2, pip_w - 1 - border / 2, pip_h - 1 - border / 2],
        radius=radius, outline=(255, 255, 255, 110), width=border,
    )
    ring.save(out_dir / "pip_ring.png")

    # 3. Soft drop shadow, oversized canvas so the blur has room -- placed
    #    centered-behind the PIP at (px - shadow_margin, py - shadow_margin)
    #    so the shadow peeks out symmetrically on all sides.

    shadow = Image.new("RGBA", (canvas_w, canvas_h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(shadow)
    d.rounded_rectangle(

        radius=radius, fill=(0, 0, 0, shadow_opacity),
    )

"""Correct the ASR transcript, then build output-timeline caption cues.

Two jobs, in order:

1. FIX WHAT THE ASR HEARD. Burned-in captions make every mis-hearing
   permanent and on-brand-damaging: the app is Kodely, not "Codely"; the
   hosting product is Nxeon (nxeon.cloud), not "Nexion"; it's Claude Max and
   Stripe and SaaS. All of these were verified against what is actually on
   screen, not guessed. faster-whisper also emits hyphenated compounds as
   separate tokens ("high", "-functioning"), which a naive space-join renders
   as "high -functioning" -- those get merged back.

2. CHUNK INTO CUES on the output timeline, per the established style
   (5-7 words, break on punctuation or a real pause, never span a cut).

   Cues are SUPPRESSED inside CARD_BLACKOUTS. Those windows are when a large
   hero-stage card is on screen; the card is itself kinetic type carrying the
   same words, and the caption pill would land on top of it. This is the same
   principle as the upstream helper's --skip-layout, applied to a window
   rather than a whole range, because these cards occupy part of a range.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

MAX_CHUNK = 6
GAP_BREAK = 0.45

# Exact-token replacements. Keys are the raw ASR token; trailing punctuation
# is preserved automatically, so "Codely." -> "Kodely." without an entry.
FIXES = {
    "codely": "kodely",      # only ever appears inside "codely.me"
    "Codely": "Kodely",
    "Cloudmax": "Claude Max",
    "Nexion": "Nxeon",
    "Shrite": "Stripe",
    "SAS": "SaaS",
}

# Ambiguous tokens that are only wrong in specific places. "cloud" is genuine
# at 1361 ("VPS and cloud hosting") and inside "console.cloud.google.com" at
# 1640; at 1616 he is saying Claude.
FIXES_AT = {
    1616.51: "Claude",
}

# (start, end) on the raw source timeline for tokens that should be merged
# into a single word. "Code" + ".ly" is him pronouncing the domain.
MERGE_PAIRS = [(1435.50, 1435.78, "Kodely")]

# Output-timeline windows where a large hero card owns the lower half of the
# frame. Filled in from the EDL + composite_full's OVERLAYS at run time.
BLACKOUT_RANGES = {3, 4, 7, 9, 39, 52}


def apply_fixes(words: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    out: list[dict] = []
    n = 0
    skip_until = -1.0
    for w in words:
        if w["type"] != "word":
            continue
        if w["start"] <= skip_until:
            continue
        text = w["text"]

        merged = None
        for a, b, repl in MERGE_PAIRS:
            if abs(w["start"] - a) < 0.02:
                merged = (repl, b)
                break
        if merged:
            new = dict(w)
            new["text"] = merged[0]
            new["end"] = max(w["end"], merged[1] + 0.2)
            skip_until = merged[1]
            out.append(new)
            n += 1
            continue

        for t, repl in FIXES_AT.items():
            if abs(w["start"] - t) < 0.02:
                text = repl
                n += 1
                break
        else:
            core = text.rstrip(".,!?;:")
            tail = text[len(core):]
            if core in FIXES:
                text = FIXES[core] + tail
                n += 1

        # Merge a leading-hyphen continuation back onto the previous token.
        if text.startswith("-") and out:
            out[-1]["text"] += text
            out[-1]["end"] = w["end"]
            n += 1
            continue

        new = dict(w)
        new["text"] = text
        out.append(new)
    return out, n


def blackout_windows(edl: dict) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """Convert each blacked-out card's (range, rel_start, dur) into an
    output-timeline window."""
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    import composite_full as cf  # noqa: E402

    wins = []
    cum = 0.0
    for i, r in enumerate(edl["ranges"]):
        dur = r["end"] - r["start"]
        if i in BLACKOUT_RANGES:
            for ov in cf.OVERLAYS.get(i, []):
                s = cum + ov["rel_start"]
                # widen by the shrink ease on either side: the webcam is
                # already moving then, and a pill popping in over a card that
                # is still animating reads as a collision even if the boxes
                # clear by a few pixels.
                wins.append((s - 0.5, s + ov["dur"] + 0.5))
        cum += dur
    return wins


def main() -> None:
    edl = json.loads((EDIT / "edl.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    raw = json.loads((EDIT / "transcripts" / "webcam.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    words, nfix = apply_fixes(raw["words"])
    (EDIT / "transcripts" / "webcam_captions.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"words": words, "backend": raw.get("backend")}), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{nfix} token corrections applied -> transcripts/webcam_captions.json")

    words = sorted(words, key=lambda w: w["start"])
    cues: list[list[dict]] = []
    cum = 0.0
    for r in edl["ranges"]:
        dur = r["end"] - r["start"]
        in_range = [w for w in words
                    if r["start"] - 0.05 <= w["start"] < r["end"] + 0.05]
        made: list[list[dict]] = []
        chunk: list[dict] = []
        prev_end = None
        for w in in_range:
            gap = (w["start"] - prev_end) if prev_end is not None else 0.0
            if chunk and (gap >= GAP_BREAK or len(chunk) >= MAX_CHUNK):
                made.append(chunk)
                chunk = []
            chunk.append(w)
            prev_end = w["end"]
            if w["text"].rstrip()[-1:] in ".!?":
                made.append(chunk)
                chunk = []
        if chunk:
            made.append(chunk)
        for c in made:
            for w in c:
                w["_o0"] = w["start"] - r["start"] + cum
                w["_o1"] = w["end"] - r["start"] + cum
        cues.extend(made)
        cum += dur

    wins = blackout_windows(edl)
    out_cues, dropped = [], 0
    for c in cues:
        if not c:
            continue
        s, e = c[0]["_o0"], c[-1]["_o1"]
        if any(s < w1 and e > w0 for w0, w1 in wins):
            dropped += 1
            continue
        out_cues.append(dict(start=round(s, 3), end=round(e, 3),
                             text=" ".join(w["text"] for w in c)))

    out = EDIT / "caption_cues.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(out_cues, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(out_cues)} cues ({dropped} suppressed under {len(wins)} card windows) "
          f"-> {out}")
    print(f"total output timeline: {cum:.1f}s; last cue ends {out_cues[-1]['end']:.1f}s")
    longest = max(out_cues, key=lambda c: len(c["text"]))
    print(f"longest cue: {len(longest['text'])} chars -- {longest['text']!r}")
    for c in out_cues[:3]:
        print("   ", c)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

2	
3	Two jobs, in order:

6	   permanent and on-brand-damaging: the app is Kodely, not "Codely"; the
7	   hosting product is Nxeon (nxeon.cloud), not "Nexion"; it's Claude Max and
8	   Stripe and SaaS. All of these were verified against what is actually on
9	   screen, not guessed. faster-whisper also emits hyphenated compounds as
10	   separate tokens ("high", "-functioning"), which a naive space-join renders
11	   as "high -functioning" -- those get merged back.
12	
13	2. CHUNK INTO CUES on the output timeline, per the established style
14	   (5-7 words, break on punctuation or a real pause, never span a cut).
15	
16	   Cues are SUPPRESSED inside CARD_BLACKOUTS. Those windows are when a large
17	   hero-stage card is on screen; the card is itself kinetic type carrying the
18	   same words, and the caption pill would land on top of it. This is the same
19	   principle as the upstream helper's --skip-layout, applied to a window
20	   rather than a whole range, because these cards occupy part of a range.

51	    1616.51: "Claude",

55	# into a single word. "Code" + ".ly" is him pronouncing the domain.

66	    out: list[dict] = []
67	    n = 0
68	    skip_until = -1.0
69	    for w in words:
70	        if w["type"] != "word":
71	            continue
72	        if w["start"] <= skip_until:
73	            continue
74	        text = w["text"]
75	
76	        merged = None

81	        if merged:
82	            new = dict(w)

85	            skip_until = merged[1]
86	            out.append(new)
87	            n += 1
88	            continue

90	        for t, repl in FIXES_AT.items():
91	            if abs(w["start"] - t) < 0.02:
92	                text = repl

94	                break
95	        else:
96	            core = text.rstrip(".,!?;:")

98	            if core in FIXES:

101	
102	        # Merge a leading-hyphen continuation back onto the previous token.
103	        if text.startswith("-") and out:
104	            out[-1]["text"] += text

115	def blackout_windows(edl: dict) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:

132	                wins.append((s - 0.5, s + ov["dur"] + 0.5))

144	
145	    words = sorted(words, key=lambda w: w["start"])
146	    cues: list[list[dict]] = []
147	    cum = 0.0
148	    for r in edl["ranges"]:
149	        dur = r["end"] - r["start"]
150	        in_range = [w for w in words
151	                    if r["start"] - 0.05 <= w["start"] < r["end"] + 0.05]
152	        made: list[list[dict]] = []
153	        chunk: list[dict] = []
154	        prev_end = None
155	        for w in in_range:
156	            gap = (w["start"] - prev_end) if prev_end is not None else 0.0
157	            if chunk and (gap >= GAP_BREAK or len(chunk) >= MAX_CHUNK):
158	                made.append(chunk)
159	                chunk = []
160	            chunk.append(w)
161	            prev_end = w["end"]
162	            if w["text"].rstrip()[-1:] in ".!?":
163	                made.append(chunk)
164	                chunk = []
165	        if chunk:
166	            made.append(chunk)
167	        for c in made:
168	            for w in c:
169	                w["_o0"] = w["start"] - r["start"] + cum
170	                w["_o1"] = w["end"] - r["start"] + cum
171	        cues.extend(made)
172	        cum += dur

"""Extract labelled frames from a built segment and tile them.

Used to check compositing with real pixels -- multiple points ACROSS a
feature's active window, not just its first frame. Every positioning bug this
project has shipped came from checking one convenient timestamp.

Usage: seg_frames.py <seg_file> <out.png> <t> [<t> ...]
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

TW, TH, COLS = 640, 360, 3
FONT = "fontfile='C\\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf'"

def main() -> None:
    seg, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
    times = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[3:]]
    tmp = out.parent / "_t"
    tmp.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tiles = []
    for i, t in enumerate(times):
        p = tmp / f"{out.stem}_{i:02d}.png"
        vf = (f"scale={TW}:{TH},drawtext={FONT}:text='t={t:.2f}':x=8:y=8:fontsize=24:"
              f"fontcolor=yellow:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.75:boxborderw=5")
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{t}", "-i", str(seg),
                        "-frames:v", "1", "-vf", vf, str(p)], check=True)
        tiles.append(p)
    rows = (len(tiles) + COLS - 1) // COLS
    args = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error"]
    for p in tiles:
        args += ["-i", str(p)]
    layout = "|".join(f"{(i % COLS) * TW}_{(i // COLS) * TH}" for i in range(len(tiles)))
    args += ["-filter_complex",
             "".join(f"[{i}:v]" for i in range(len(tiles)))
             + f"xstack=inputs={len(tiles)}:layout={layout}:fill=black[v]",
             "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(out)]
    subprocess.run(args, check=True)
    print(f"{out}  ({len(tiles)} frames, {rows} rows)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Final pass: burn in captions and fix the audio level.

Input:  composited_draft.mp4 (segments + graphics + transitions, concatenated)
Output: final.mp4

Captions are a 1920x320 alpha strip (see make_captions_slot.py) overlaid at
y=760, which is why this is a video re-encode rather than a stream copy.

AUDIO: the source recordings sit around -44 LUFS -- roughly 30 dB under the
-14 LUFS streaming target, quiet enough that the previous episode shipped
close to inaudible (measured -42.9 LUFS). Loudness is normalised ONCE here on
the fully concatenated track, never per segment: per-segment normalisation
would pump the level at every cut.

The gain needed (~30 dB) exceeds the ~23 dB available before true peak hits
-1.5 dBTP, so loudnorm runs in its dynamic mode. That is expected for this
material -- its peak-to-loudness ratio is ~20 LU, i.e. a few isolated
transients sitting far above conversational level -- and is what every
speech-mastering chain does. It is measured in two passes so the result is
deterministic rather than loudnorm guessing from a single-pass estimate.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = EDIT / "composited_draft.mp4"
CAPTIONS = EDIT / "animations" / "slot_captions" / "render.webm"
OUT = EDIT / "final.mp4"

CAPTION_Y = 760
TARGET_I, TARGET_TP, TARGET_LRA = -14.0, -1.5, 11.0


def probe_duration(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run([
        "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
        "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def measure(p: Path) -> dict:
    print("pass 1/2: measuring loudness ...")
    r = subprocess.run([
        "ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
        "-af", f"loudnorm=I={TARGET_I}:TP={TARGET_TP}:LRA={TARGET_LRA}:print_format=json",
        "-f", "null", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = re.findall(r"\{[^{}]*\"input_i\"[^{}]*\}", r.stderr, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("could not parse loudnorm measurement:\n", r.stderr[-2500:])
        sys.exit(1)
    d = json.loads(m[-1])
    print(f"  measured: I={d['input_i']} LUFS  TP={d['input_tp']} dBTP  LRA={d['input_lra']}")
    return d


def main() -> None:
    if not SRC.exists():
        print(f"missing {SRC} -- run composite_full.py first")
        sys.exit(1)
    have_caps = CAPTIONS.exists()
    if not have_caps:
        print(f"WARNING: {CAPTIONS} not found -- rendering without captions")

    d = measure(SRC)
    af = (
        f"loudnorm=I={TARGET_I}:TP={TARGET_TP}:LRA={TARGET_LRA}"
        f":measured_I={d['input_i']}:measured_TP={d['input_tp']}"
        f":measured_LRA={d['input_lra']}:measured_thresh={d['input_thresh']}"
        f":offset={d['target_offset']}:linear=true,aresample=48000"
    )

    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-stats", "-i", str(SRC)]
    if have_caps:
        # libvpx-vp9 explicitly: the native vp9 decoder drops the alpha
        # channel here and the strip composites as an opaque black band.
        cmd += ["-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(CAPTIONS)]
        cmd += ["-filter_complex",
                f"[0:v][1:v]overlay=x=0:y={CAPTION_Y}:eof_action=pass[v];[0:a]{af}[a]",
                "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]"]
    else:
        cmd += ["-filter_complex", f"[0:a]{af}[a]", "-map", "0:v", "-map", "[a]"]
    cmd += ["-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "19",
            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-r", "60",
            "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2",
            "-movflags", "+faststart", str(OUT)]

    print("pass 2/2: overlaying captions + normalising ...")
    r = subprocess.run(cmd)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"\ndone: {OUT}  ({probe_duration(OUT):.1f}s)")
    v = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(OUT), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-af", "ebur128=peak=true", "-f", "null", "-"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
    for key in ("I:", "LRA:", "Peak:"):
        for line in v.splitlines()[-40:]:
            if line.strip().startswith(key):
                print("  ", line.strip())
                break


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.new_string:
- Pop-in (not slow reveal) per cue: quick `back.out` scale+opacity, ~0.04-0.08s -- a slow multi-second entrance looks laggy against fast speech cadence.
- Skip captioning any EDL range whose layout already carries its own on-screen kinetic type (e.g. an intro graphic) -- `gen_caption_cues.py --skip-layout` handles this, default skips `intro_graphic`.

### Caption width vs. the webcam PIP (the constraint that sets both)

A centred caption pill has to clear the PIP in **whichever corner that section uses**, and a video will usually use both. The clear centre band is `(1920 - 2*(MARGIN + PIP_W + border_glow))` wide -- with a 576px PIP that is only ~634px, which forces either an unreadably narrow pill or a ~17px gap. "Technically not touching" is not a gap.

Ep. 1 (Kodely) resolved this by **shrinking the PIP to 512x384**, which opens the band to ~768px and lets a 620px pill clear the neon border by ~54px on both sides. Verified by measuring the rendered pill's alpha box (x 624-1295) against both corner positions. 512x384 still reads as a substantial corner webcam; prefer it over narrowing the captions.

Consequence: the neon border must then be **scaled** in the PIP path too (`scale` the whole 1920x1080 border frame by `PIP_H / 432`, then offset by the scaled frame's own centred-rail origin). Keep the border's authored height (432) as its own constant -- in the first episode it happened to equal `PIP_H`, which made two different numbers look like one.

### Caption overlay: render a strip, not a full frame

The caption overlay is a pill in the bottom band; the rest of every frame is empty alpha that still costs full render time. Author the composition at **1920x320** and composite it at `y=760` (pill bottom then lands at y=988, same as a full-frame version). Measured on a 12.5-minute video: **~3.4x realtime instead of ~16x** -- 45 minutes instead of 3-4 hours, for an identical result.

### Caption blackout windows

`--skip-layout` skips a whole range, but a large card usually occupies only *part* of a range. Suppress cues whose output-timeline window overlaps a card's window (widened by the shrink-aside ease on either side) instead. Ep. 1 suppressed 36 of 441 cues this way -- every shrink-aside window plus one screen-stage card that sat 12px from the pill. The card is itself kinetic type carrying the same words, so nothing is lost.

### Fix the ASR before it becomes permanent

Burned-in captions make every mis-hearing permanent, and ASR reliably mangles brand names -- Kodely came through as "Codely" (the previous episode shipped a motion-graphic card with that spelling), Nxeon as "Nexion", Claude Max as "Cloudmax", Stripe as "Shrite", SaaS as "SAS". Run a correction pass over the transcript before generating cues, and **verify each spelling against what is actually on screen** (the site's own logo, the browser tab title, the URL) rather than guessing. faster-whisper also emits hyphenated compounds as separate tokens (`high`, `-functioning`), which a naive space-join renders as "high -functioning" -- merge any token starting with `-` onto the previous one.

## Full-frame / long overlay lesson (learned the hard way)

Any overlay graphic composited near a webcam PIP must clear the corner it might land in -- and since a PIP can be positioned in EITHER bottom corner depending on the segment (see `composite_pip.py`'s `pip_position` field), a graphic can't assume only one corner is at risk. ## Audio: normalise loudness (REQUIRED final pass)

**Check this on every video before calling it done.** OBS webcam/mic captures in this setup land around **-44 LUFS integrated** -- roughly 30 dB under the -14 LUFS streaming target. The first episode shipped at **-42.9 LUFS**, i.e. close to inaudible at a normal playback volume. It is not a footage problem (the recordings are clean: ~-76 dB noise floor, ~48 dB SNR), it is a missing pipeline step.

- Normalise **once, on the fully concatenated audio**, never per segment -- per-segment `loudnorm` re-levels each clip independently and pumps at every cut.
- Two-pass `loudnorm` (measure, then apply with `measured_*`), so the result is deterministic rather than a single-pass estimate: target `I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11`.
- Expect it to land in **dynamic mode**, not linear. This material has a peak-to-loudness ratio around 20 LU (a few isolated transients far above conversational level), so the ~30 dB of gain needed exceeds the ~23 dB available before true peak hits -1.5 dBTP. That is normal for speech and is what any speech-mastering chain does; it typically pulls LRA from ~12 to ~6 LU. If that reads as over-squashed, back off to a gentler gain-plus-limiter chain and accept a quieter master.
- The caption overlay pass re-encodes video anyway, so fold the normalisation into that same pass rather than adding another generation.
- Verify with `ffmpeg -af ebur128=peak=true -f null -` on the **final file**, not on an intermediate.

## Master audio: use the webcam recording, not the screen recording

When OBS records screen and webcam as two separate outputs, both carry the same mic. Take the master audio from the **webcam** file: its video and audio share a container, so lip-sync on the webcam PIP/hero shot is exact by construction and there is no offset left to get wrong. (Verified equivalent on ep. 1: mean and peak levels matched the screen recording within 0.1 dB, so nothing is lost.) The screen recording is then the track that gets aligned *into* the webcam's clock, and screen content is far more forgiving of a few frames of drift than lips are.

Corollary: only the webcam audio needs transcribing. Transcribing both doubles the cost for two transcripts of the same speech.

## Multi-part OBS footage: one global timeline

OBS often writes a session as several part-pairs (`Screen/part N`, `Webcam/part N`) rather than one take. Do **not** teach the EDL about parts -- keep a single global timeline (the concatenated **webcam** durations) and put all the part-awareness in one small module that maps a global range onto `(part, local_screen_t, local_webcam_t)`. See `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/scripts/timeline.py`. Everything downstream (EDL schema, caption cues, compositing) then looks identical to a single-take project.

- **Measure the screen-vs-webcam offset per part; never assume zero.** Amplitude-envelope cross-correlation over three separate windows spread across each part (`sync_parts.py`) gives both the offset and a drift check -- three windows rather than one, so genuine within-part drift shows up as three different lags instead of silently averaging. Ep. 1 measured 10-50ms per part, correlation 0.97-0.996, zero spread.
- **Never let a range span a part boundary** -- the two sides are different takes recorded minutes apart. Assert it in `resolve()`.
- Physically concatenating the parts is the wrong instinct: the screen parts each run ~0.5s longer than their webcam pair, so a naive concat accumulates a **~3.3s desync by part 6**.

## Verify overlay placement by measuring alpha, not by reading CSS

Every placement bug this project has shipped came from reasoning about a graphic's footprint from its source, or from checking one frame. CSS geometry says nothing about glow, blur or shadow spread -- a card authored at `left: 90px; width: 740px` measured **x 40-879** once rendered.

Use `bbox.py`: decode the alpha channel at N points across the graphic's **full duration** and union the per-frame boxes. Then check that union against the box it has to clear. Adopt a written placement contract so cards are authored to fit rather than fixed afterwards -- ep. 1 used "all hero-stage card content inside x 60..950", which clears the single aside box (x 1030..1880) by >=80px for every card, replacing the previous episode's per-range bespoke geometry.

## Cut boundaries: an ASR word `end` is not where the word ends

faster-whisper stretches the **last word of a phrase** to cover the silence after it -- `'GoDaddy.' [99.31-100.01]` is a 0.7s "word". Treating that as real makes every phrase-final OUT point look safe when it may still clip, and vice versa.

Cap the assumed real word length (~0.55s) and auto-pad each boundary outward off the word it lands in, clamped short of the neighbouring word. Only ever move outward, so a hand-chosen boundary that already has room is left alone, and keep an explicit exceptions list for boundaries that deliberately cut a word out (a self-correction, a dangling conjunction). On ep. 1 this moved 46 of 60 ranges and caught several genuine mid-word clips that the naive check had scored as fine.

## Scene-change crossfades: watch for chains

The "merge two segments into one crossfaded clip, then splice it in" approach breaks when two boundaries **share a segment** -- e.g. a short hero beat sandwiched between two screen beats (`51->52`, `52->53`). Handling those as two independent pairs emits segment 52 twice in the concat list. Group consecutive boundaries into a chain and fold left to right, feeding each merged clip in as the next `A`; `xfade`'s offset then comes from the *merged* clip's real probed duration.

1	# Liquid Glass style reference
2	
3	Reusable design tokens for the "liquid glass" (iOS 26) motion-graphics style,
4	established across the Kodely / Vibe Coding series. Reuse these values for
5	new graphics unless the video calls for a different brand explicitly.
6	
7	## Palette
8	
9	Warm pink → peach → magenta gradient (Kodely's own brand gradient):
10	
11	```css
12	--glass-accent-1: #ff7aa8; /* pink */
13	--glass-accent-2: #ffb37a; /* peach */
14	--glass-accent-3: #ff6fae; /* magenta-pink */
15	--glass-accent-4: #cf3fc4; /* magenta */
16	/* typical usage: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--glass-accent-1), var(--glass-accent-2), var(--glass-accent-4)) */
17	```
18	
19	## Glass panel recipe
20	
21	- Backdrop blur + saturation boost on whatever sits behind the panel (`backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.4)`).
22	- Translucent fill, not solid: low-alpha white/brand-tinted background (~10-20% opacity), not a flat card color.
23	- Rounded corners, 20-32px radius depending on card size.
24	- Subtle white edge-highlight catching light at an angle (a `border` or inset gradient-masked ring, ~2-3px, ~40% opacity) -- this is the single most important cue that reads as "glass" rather than "flat card."
25	- Soft drop shadow, low opacity, generous blur -- glass should feel like it's floating, not pasted on.
26	- Optional: a one-shot diagonal sheen sweep on entrance (a light gradient streak animating across the panel) reads well for a reveal moment; skip it for anything that holds on screen a while, it gets busy.
27	
28	## Motion
29	
30	- Never linear easing. Ease-out cubic (`power2.out`/`power3.out`) for reveals landing on a payoff; ease-in cubic (`power2.in`) for exits.
31	- Never reveal two new elements simultaneously -- stagger, one beat at a time.
32	- Sync paydoffs to the actual spoken word/number, using real per-word timestamps from the transcript (`edit/transcripts/<source>.json`) -- never estimate timing from the phrase-level text alone.
33	- **Animate transforms only** (`x`/`y`/`scale`/`opacity`). Never tween `letterSpacing`, `width`, `margin` or anything else that reflows text: those snap to whole device pixels during layout, which stutters visibly under the seek-by-frame capture engine. `hyperframes check` catches this as `gsap_non_transform_motion` -- run it after every composition edit, it has caught real defects that look fine in preview. To animate letter-spacing, split into per-character elements and animate each glyph's `x`.
34	- A count-up card should not sit on its zero state for long before counting. Two and a half seconds of a visible `$0` reads as a claim about the number, not a wind-up; keep it under ~1s by moving the card's own start closer to the count rather than by starting the count earlier than the spoken number.
35	
36	## Captions
37	
38	Glass-pill captions, bottom-center (clear of a corner webcam PIP), built via `helpers/gen_caption_cues.py` (chunk sizing) + a HyperFrames data-driven overlay (see `helpers/composite_pip.py`'s overlay pattern for how a long alpha-webm overlay gets composited).
39	
40	- **Chunk size: 5-7 words per caption** (not 2-3 -- tried the tighter chunking first, client wanted longer lines). `--max-chunk 6` is a good default.
41	- **Font size: 36px** Geist Bold (800) -- tried 50px first, too large for 5-7 word lines; 36px reads clearly and wraps cleanly to 2 lines on the longest cues. Pill `max-width` ~1600px.
42	- **Panel fill must be more opaque than other liquid-glass elements** -- captions sit over constantly-changing (often bright/light) backgrounds, unlike a graphic authored against one known background. A near-invisible white wash that looks fine in isolation can vanish against a light page. Use a darker tinted fill (~rgba(20-36,10-15,18-30, 0.64-0.72)) with real backdrop-filter blur, not the lighter ~0.1-0.2 alpha used on other cards -- verify legibility by test-compositing over BOTH a solid white and a bright brand-color background, not just dark video content.
43	- Pop-in (not slow reveal) per cue: quick `back.out` scale+opacity, ~0.04-0.08s -- a slow multi-second entrance looks laggy against fast speech cadence.
44	- Skip captioning any EDL range whose layout already carries its own on-screen kinetic type (e.g. an intro graphic) -- `gen_caption_cues.py --skip-layout` handles this, default skips `intro_graphic`.
45	
46	### Caption width vs. the webcam PIP (the constraint that sets both)
47	
48	A centred caption pill has to clear the PIP in **whichever corner that section uses**, and a video will usually use both. The clear centre band is `(1920 - 2*(MARGIN + PIP_W + border_glow))` wide -- with a 576px PIP that is only ~634px, which forces either an unreadably narrow pill or a ~17px gap. "Technically not touching" is not a gap.
49	
50	Ep. 1 (Kodely) resolved this by **shrinking the PIP to 512x384**, which opens the band to ~768px and lets a 620px pill clear the neon border by ~54px on both sides. Verified by measuring the rendered pill's alpha box (x 624-1295) against both corner positions. 512x384 still reads as a substantial corner webcam; prefer it over narrowing the captions.
51	
52	Consequence: the neon border must then be **scaled** in the PIP path too (`scale` the whole 1920x1080 border frame by `PIP_H / 432`, then offset by the scaled frame's own centred-rail origin). Keep the border's authored height (432) as its own constant -- in the first episode it happened to equal `PIP_H`, which made two different numbers look like one.
53	
54	### Caption overlay: render a strip, not a full frame
55	
56	The caption overlay is a pill in the bottom band; the rest of every frame is empty alpha that still costs full render time. Author the composition at **1920x320** and composite it at `y=760` (pill bottom then lands at y=988, same as a full-frame version). Measured on a 12.5-minute video: **~3.4x realtime instead of ~16x** -- 45 minutes instead of 3-4 hours, for an identical result.
57	
58	### Caption blackout windows
59	
60	`--skip-layout` skips a whole range, but a large card usually occupies only *part* of a range. Suppress cues whose output-timeline window overlaps a card's window (widened by the shrink-aside ease on either side) instead. Ep. 1 suppressed 36 of 441 cues this way -- every shrink-aside window plus one screen-stage card that sat 12px from the pill. The card is itself kinetic type carrying the same words, so nothing is lost.
61	
62	### Fix the ASR before it becomes permanent
63	
64	Burned-in captions make every mis-hearing permanent, and ASR reliably mangles brand names -- Kodely came through as "Codely" (the previous episode shipped a motion-graphic card with that spelling), Nxeon as "Nexion", Claude Max as "Cloudmax", Stripe as "Shrite", SaaS as "SAS". Run a correction pass over the transcript before generating cues, and **verify each spelling against what is actually on screen** (the site's own logo, the browser tab title, the URL) rather than guessing. faster-whisper also emits hyphenated compounds as separate tokens (`high`, `-functioning`), which a naive space-join renders as "high -functioning" -- merge any token starting with `-` onto the previous one.
65	
66	## Full-frame / long overlay lesson (learned the hard way)
67	
68	Any overlay graphic composited near a webcam PIP must clear the corner it might land in -- and since a PIP can be positioned in EITHER bottom corner depending on the segment (see `composite_pip.py`'s `pip_position` field), a graphic can't assume only one corner is at risk. First version of a multi-step explainer graphic spanned nearly the full frame height and ended up drawn directly over the presenter's face. Fix: anchor content-heavy overlays to the TOP portion of the frame (roughly y: 60-520 out of 1080) and leave the entire bottom band (~y 520-1080) clear, rather than just avoiding one specific corner.
69

   from `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/animations/` as a starting point
   (re-render only if a parameter genuinely needs to change — loop speed,

   Also reusable as-is: `slot_tag_bug`, `slot_tag_subscribe`,
   `slot_palette_reveal`, `slot_mic_indicator_1` (extended to 20s),
   `slot_kodely_reveal`, `slot_tag_nxeon` — the last two carry the CORRECT
   brand spellings (Kodely, NXEON); the `first-video` copies do not.
7. For new one-off motion graphics (stat cards, title reveals, tag callouts),
   build fresh per-episode — those are tied to that episode's content. Use
   `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/scripts/make_graphics.py`: it generates every
   card from one shared glass/palette/motion shell, so six cards are six
   content blocks rather than six near-identical HTML files, and the
   placement contract lives in one docstring.
8. **Verify every card's placement with `bbox.py`, not by reading its CSS.**
   It decodes the real alpha channel across the card's full duration. Glow
   and shadow routinely push the rendered box 40-50px past the authored one.
9. Run `npm run check` (hyperframes) on every composition before rendering —
   it catches real defects (e.g. tweening `letterSpacing`, which stutters
   under the frame-by-frame capture engine) that look fine in preview.

---
name: video-editing-style-prefs
description: "Nick's editing/motion-graphics style preferences for the video-use + HyperFrames pipeline, learned across the \"Kodely\"/Vibe Coding series edit"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b8931927-c4d2-4a39-ad0f-d47c389ed490
  modified: 2026-08-20T09:49:36.877Z
---

Visual style is "liquid glass" (iOS 26 aesthetic) tied to his own product's actual brand gradient: warm pink → peach → magenta. Applies to motion graphics, captions, and UI-adjacent overlays.
**Why:** he explicitly wants the video's visual language to match Kodely's own product design, not a generic template.
**How to apply:** default new motion graphics to frosted/translucent glass panels (backdrop-blur, soft shadow, subtle white edge-highlight, rounded corners) in that palette unless he specifies otherwise for a given video.

Webcam PIP: rounded corners + soft shadow + glass-edge ring, default bottom-right, dynamically repositions (smooth animated slide, never an instant teleport) when it would sit on top of something important on screen (e.g. a chat panel). Webcam goes fullscreen (blur-fill, not cropped) during pure talking-head sections where nothing relevant is on screen.
**Why:** explicit ask — "it can't just be a disappear and reappear in a new location."
**How to apply:** check what's actually on screen at each PIP placement before defaulting to a corner; don't just alternate corners arbitrarily.

Zoom-ins must be used sparingly and only on genuine focal points (something specifically being pointed at/discussed), never as decoration on broad layout commentary. Cap zoom around 2.0x — tighter crops visibly degrade quality. Verify zoom targets by densely sampling real frames, not by inferring from transcript text alone (a split-screen browser+chat-panel layout caused a real mistargeting bug once — the actual UI element referenced by narration can be in a different screen region than assumed).
**Why:** caught two rounds of zoom targeting errors (wrong panel, then over-tight crops) via direct feedback.
**How to apply:** before committing to a zoom plan, verify against actual frames near the target timestamp, not just the packed transcript text.

Very precise, detail-oriented about cut cleanliness — catches subtle mid-word cutoffs and redundant repeated phrases (stutters, doubled sentences) by ear that raw transcripts/timestamps can mis-represent (ASR can smear or merge repeated words; cross-checking against a second transcript of the same audio, e.g. screen vs. webcam track, can reveal what one run missed).
**Why:** flagged 5 distinct precise-timestamp cut issues in one pass after an initial "sounds good" pass — he re-watches carefully and expects frame/word-accurate fixes, not approximate ones.
**How to apply:** treat "sounds clean" feedback as provisional, not final sign-off. When fixing a flagged cut, pull exact word-level timestamps rather than eyeballing.

Motion graphics should be purposeful and tied to specific transcript content (a stat card for a specific number mentioned, a title reveal timed to when a name is said, a palette swatch synced to color words) — not generic decoration. Prefers a small number of well-placed graphics over covering every possible moment.
**Why:** his own creative direction throughout — e.g. specifically requested a retrowave-then-nebula intro synced word-by-word to the real audio, and asked for zooms only at genuine callouts.
**How to apply:** when proposing motion-graphic moments, ground each one in a specific line/word from the transcript and its real timestamp, not a generic template slot.

Is a working YouTuber making a "Vibe Coding till I reach one paying customer" series about building an app called Kodely with Claude Code — cost/token-conscious (asked directly about cumulative token spend on a video edit).
**How to apply:** be mindful of expensive sub-agent rebuild cycles; prefer fixing/patching over full rebuilds where the tooling allows it, and flag when a from-scratch build (e.g. a new motion graphic) is likely to cost a lot before doing it.

Wants the webcam PIP's neon-glow border present at ALL times the webcam is visible — not just during full-screen "hero" moments, also during the smaller screen-recording+PIP layout. When adding a new visual treatment to one layout mode, check whether it needs to apply to every layout mode the webcam appears in, not just the one being actively worked on.
**Why:** flagged directly — "the neon border also needs to stay on at all times, even when its over top of the screen recordings, i noticed in this video it wasnt."
**How to apply:** default to applying webcam-attached visual treatments (border, glow, mask) universally across every compositing function that draws the webcam, unless told otherwise.

Sub-agent "verified" reports in this pipeline have been wrong multiple times this session (a corner-PIP clipping bug reported clean, a card/webcam overlap reported as having "real margin" when it didn't, a grain-layer-scope claim) — always because the agent's own verification pass sampled only a couple of convenient timestamps (transition edges, opening frames) instead of densely sampling a feature's full active window.
**Why:** each time, independently re-checking with fresh frame extraction at different timestamps than the agent used caught a real, visible defect the agent's own report called "clean."
**How to apply:** before presenting delegated video/compositing work as done, independently extract and inspect at least one frame the sub-agent's own report didn't specifically call out — don't relay a "verified" claim without a spot-check of your own, especially for anything involving overlay positioning, alpha compositing, or multi-state animations (hero/corner/mid-transition).

Is building a living, reusable template for this series (not a one-off per-video edit) — see [[video_editing_pipeline_setup]] for where it lives. Explicitly wants Claude to accumulate and reuse style knowledge across episodes rather than rebuilding from scratch each time.
**Why:** "I want to save all of these skills and assets for future videos in this series... I want [Claude] to learn my style."
**How to apply:** when a style/technique choice is confirmed (not just tried once, but actually approved after iteration), fold it into `LIQUID_GLASS_STYLE.md` and the template README, not just this memory file — those are the artifacts a future episode's session will actually read.

See also [[video_editing_pipeline_setup]] for the technical pipeline this all runs on.
