"""Still-frame look test: current retrowave/neon style vs a restrained pass.

Stills rather than clips on purpose -- palette, grade, framing and chrome are
all judgeable from a frame, and this costs seconds instead of a render.

The restrained pass changes five things, all subtractive:
  1. background   retrowave scene -> near-black graded field + vignette + grain
  2. border       travelling neon comets -> hairline rim + real drop shadow
  3. grade        none -> lifted blacks, mild desaturation, warm highlights
  4. chrome       raw browser (tabs/URL/bookmarks) -> cropped away, page in a
                  floating rounded panel
  5. type         (see the card comparison; not in this frame test)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = EDIT / "verify" / "looktest"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
FONT = "fontfile='C\\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf'"

HERO_T = 1990.0
SCREEN_T = 2010.0

# Filmic-ish grade: lift the blacks off zero, pull a little saturation out,
# warm the highlights. Applied to the WEBCAM and SCREEN, never to the
# background plate (which is already authored at the target values).
GRADE = ("curves=all='0/0.045 0.25/0.26 0.5/0.5 0.75/0.76 1/0.97',"
         "eq=contrast=1.05:saturation=0.80:gamma=1.01,"
         "colorbalance=rh=0.03:gh=0.01:bh=-0.03")

# Restrained ground: a very dark desaturated field with a soft centre lift and
# fine animated-looking grain. Cheap to make in ffmpeg -- no render needed,
# which also means no 20s loop to keep in sync with anything.
def ground(w=1920, h=1080):
    return (
        f"color=c=0x0B0A0E:s={w}x{h},"
        f"geq=r='r(X,Y)+26*exp(-((X-{w/2})^2/(2*{(w*0.55)**2})+(Y-{h*0.42})^2/(2*{(h*0.62)**2})))'"
        f":g='g(X,Y)+22*exp(-((X-{w/2})^2/(2*{(w*0.55)**2})+(Y-{h*0.42})^2/(2*{(h*0.62)**2})))'"
        f":b='b(X,Y)+34*exp(-((X-{w/2})^2/(2*{(w*0.55)**2})+(Y-{h*0.42})^2/(2*{(h*0.62)**2})))',"
        f"noise=alls=6:allf=t+u,"
        f"vignette=angle=PI/5"
    )


def run(cmd):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", " ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:400])
        print(r.stderr[-2500:])
        sys.exit(1)


def label(p, text):
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".lbl.png")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(p), "-vf",
         f"drawtext={FONT}:text='{text}':x=24:y=22:fontsize=34:fontcolor=white:"
         f"box=1:boxcolor=black@0.75:boxborderw=12", str(tmp)])
    return tmp


def hero_premium(out: Path):
    src = resolve(HERO_T, HERO_T + 0.4)
    # webcam 1306x980 centred, rounded, hairline rim, real shadow
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error",
         "-f", "lavfi", "-i", ground(),
         "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
         "-i", str(EDIT / "assets" / "pip_mask.png"),
         "-filter_complex",
         f"[1:v]scale=1306:980,{GRADE}[cam];"
         f"[2:v]scale=1306:980[m];"
         f"[cam][m]alphamerge[camr];"
         # shadow: the mask itself, blurred and darkened, sat behind the box
         f"[2:v]scale=1306:980,boxblur=34:2,geq=lum='p(X,Y)*0.72':a='p(X,Y)'[sh];"
         f"color=c=black:s=1306x980[shc];[shc][sh]alphamerge[shadow];"
         f"[0:v][shadow]overlay=x=307:y=68[bgs];"
         f"[bgs][camr]overlay=x=307:y=50[v]",
         "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(out)])

    # in a rounded panel instead of showing raw OS chrome.

    # a Windows path's drive colon breaks filter-string parsing.

         "-f", "lavfi", "-i", ground(),
         "-ss", f"{src['screen_ss']}", "-i", src["screen_path"],
         "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
         "-i", str(EDIT / "assets" / "pip_mask.png"),
         "-filter_complex",
         # page: drop chrome, then fit the panel
         f"[1:v]crop=1920:960:0:120,scale={PW}:{PH},{GRADE}[pg];"
         f"color=c=white:s={PW}x{PH}[pm0];"
         f"[pm0]geq=lum='255':a='if(gt(hypot(max(0,26-X)+max(0,X-({PW}-27)),"
         f"max(0,26-Y)+max(0,Y-({PH}-27))),26),0,255)'[pmask];"

         f"[pmask]boxblur=30:2,geq=lum='p(X,Y)*0.7':a='p(X,Y)'[psh];"
         f"color=c=black:s={PW}x{PH}[pshc];[pshc][psh]alphamerge[pshadow];"
         f"[0:v][pshadow]overlay=x=210:y=118[bgs];"
         f"[bgs][pgr]overlay=x=210:y=100[withpg];"
         # webcam PIP bottom-right, graded, rounded
         f"[2:v]scale=512:384,{GRADE}[cam];"
         f"[3:v]scale=512:384[cm];"
         f"[cam][cm]alphamerge[camr];"
         f"[withpg][camr]overlay=x=1348:y=636[v]",
         "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(out)])


def main():
    cur_hero = OUT / "cur_hero.png"
    cur_scr = OUT / "cur_screen.png"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", "7.5",
         "-i", str(EDIT / "clips_composited" / "seg_52.mp4"),
         "-frames:v", "1", str(cur_hero)])
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", "8.0",
         "-i", str(EDIT / "clips_composited" / "seg_54.mp4"),
         "-frames:v", "1", str(cur_scr)])

    hero_premium(new_hero)
    screen_premium(new_scr)

    tiles = [label(cur_hero, "CURRENT  hero"), label(new_hero, "RESTRAINED  hero"),

    args = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error"]
    for t in tiles:

    args += ["-filter_complex",
             "[0:v]scale=960:540[a];[1:v]scale=960:540[b];"
             "[2:v]scale=960:540[c];[3:v]scale=960:540[d];"
             "[a][b][c][d]xstack=inputs=4:layout=0_0|960_0|0_540|960_540[v]",
             "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(OUT / "compare.png")]
    run(args)
    print(f"-> {OUT / 'compare.png'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
**On baz — I re-tested it per your template's own instruction, and it's still blocked both ways:**

- `--format webm` fails with the *identical* error filed back in August: the server won't switch off h264/aac. No alpha means no overlay assets. And it's a codec-selection bug, not a paywall — **a paid tier wouldn't fix it.**
- The free tier still watermarks. I ran a real mp4 export and "baz.studio" is burned into the corner.

So baz can't contribute finished assets here: not overlays (no alpha), not full-frame scenes (watermark). Its honest role is **free design ideation** — `scenes create`/`set-code` cost no AI tokens, so concepts can be iterated as TSX and used as reference for what I then build in HyperFrames. `baz prompt` does spend your credits, so I didn't touch it. I've recorded the re-test in the baz-assets README so nobody re-discovers it.

**The look test above** covers background, border, grade and browser chrome only.

What clearly works: losing the browser chrome is the biggest single upgrade — no more tabs, bookmarks, or that "secret stuff" bookmark. The grade calms the blown-out white page and the bright wall. Dropping the comet border reads far more grown-up.

**My first attempt was wrong and I fixed it before showing you:** I floated the page in a small panel with a generous margin, which looked tidy and made the page unreadable. On a screen-recording channel legibility beats margin, so the panel is now near-full-bleed — chrome cropped, corners rounded, soft shadow, but the content stays large.

**Two things worth saying plainly, because they cap how premium this can get and no amount of editing fixes them:**

1. **Your webcam is 640×480.** Every hero shot is a 2× upscale — that softness is visible in the right-hand frames and no grade removes it. Recording at 1080p would do more for perceived quality than everything else on my list combined.
2. **The wall behind you is bright beige**, which fights a dark restrained ground — you can see it pulling attention in the top-right frame. A darker backdrop and a little separation light would let the premium palette actually work.

Neither blocks the redesign; they just set the ceiling.

**Still to do on the visual side:** the type and motion pass on cards (lighter weights, solid fills, slow settles instead of pops and CRT flashes), then sound design via `/media-use` for the ambient bed and transition texture.

Before I build those — does the direction in the right-hand frames look right to you, or do you want it warmer, darker, or with more texture in the background? Easier to adjust now than after I've rebuilt 60 segments.

Retested — and it **has moved since yesterday**, but not far enough.

**What changed:** `--format webm` no longer errors. It completes and returns a real webm (VP8 + Opus) instead of failing on that h264/aac filename check. `--quality high` gives full 1920×1080, not the 854×480 I got at low.

I checked by decoding to RGBA and sampling actual pixels rather than trusting `pix_fmt` — exactly one alpha level (255) and **0.0% transparent pixels**, at both low and high quality. The transparent background comes back as opaque black. The watermark is also still there on both exports.

| | yesterday | today |
|---|---|---|
| webm export | hard error | ✅ completes, VP8/Opus |
| resolution | — | ✅ 1920×1080 at `--quality high` |
| alpha channel | none | ❌ still none (1 alpha level, 0% transparent) |
| watermark | present | ❌ still present |

So the practical conclusion is unchanged: **baz still can't contribute assets here.** No alpha means no overlay cards, borders or captions, and the watermark rules out full-frame scenes like a title or section card. It's genuinely closer than it was, though — the codec path is fixed, so if they wire up VP9-with-alpha it becomes usable overnight.

I've updated the baz-assets README with today's result, kept yesterday's state as history, and written down exactly what to re-test next time: whether the stream ever returns VP9 with `alpha levels > 1`, and whether the watermark is tier-gated. I also cleaned up both probe scenes from your project.

Worth flagging: I don't know whether a paid tier removes that watermark — that's the one thing I can't test without you upgrading. If it does, baz immediately becomes useful for **full-frame** work: an intro title lockup, section cards, or a data-viz beat like the 702-card board. Those are exactly the pieces that would sell the premium direction, and they don't need alpha.

Meanwhile the redesign path is unblocked without it — HyperFrames does the overlays, and the still comparison I sent is waiting on your read. Do you want it warmer, darker, or with more texture in the background before I take it to the type and motion pass?

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The user is producing episode 1 of a YouTube series "Vibe Coding till I reach one paying customer," documenting building an AI website builder app called **Kodely**. Requests evolved through several phases:

1. **Initial autonomous edit request**: A detailed hands-off starter prompt to edit raw OBS footage (6 part-pairs of Screen+Webcam recordings) into a finished video, following an established "liquid glass" retrowave/neon style from a previous episode (`first-video/`). Explicit instructions covered cut/pacing rules, layout decisions (hero vs PIP), motion graphics placement, zoom discipline, scene transitions, mic indicator usage, and one mandatory checkpoint after EDL build before compositing.
2. Mid-session: **"use the audio from the webcam footage so its lipsynced"** — pivot to webcam-as-master-audio architecture.
3. Post-delivery bug reports: **"at 40s, it skips to 44s when i play the video and then the audio is out of sync with my lips. also theres a lot of instances where my voice gets cut off short"** — required deep forensic debugging and fixes.
4. **"also theres a portion where im talking about NXEON in the video but it shows a URL at the top which is supposed to be secret, we need to block this out"** — privacy blur requirement.
5. **"the project id too"** — additional privacy blur for GCP project ID.
6. **"make a youtube title and description for this video"**
7. **"is there a way to turn this video into multiple engaging youtube shorts"** then **"start with one video"** — build one pilot vertical Short.
8. **"I would like to give my videos a more premium feel to them, something like fern (very premium motion graphics and editing style)"** — major style redesign request. User specified via AskUserQuestion: "Full restrained redesign" AND "lets use baz.studio skills to help with this alongside hyper frames and video use", plus "Yes — build it with the look" for sound design inclusion.
9. **"try baz now"** — most recent request, asking to re-verify whether baz.studio's alpha-export bug has been fixed since the last check (one day prior).

Throughout, the user expects rigorous verification (not just visual spot-checks) before work is presented as done — this was reinforced strongly after the audio-loss and clipped-cuts bugs shipped despite earlier "verified" claims.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **video-use / HyperFrames pipeline**: transcribe → pack → strategy → EDL → composite → finalize, using ffmpeg filter_complex chains and HyperFrames (GSAP-based HTML motion graphics rendered via `npx hyperframes@0.8.3 render`).
- **Global timeline abstraction** for multi-part OBS recordings (webcam clock as source of truth, screen recording offset per-part via audio cross-correlation).
- **Webcam-as-master-audio**: exact lip-sync since webcam video/audio share a container.
- **Word-boundary cut padding + silence-snapping** (two-pass cut refinement): ASR word timestamps are insufficient alone; must snap to real waveform silence with a locally-adaptive threshold.
- **Rounded-corner mask antialiasing**: PIL's `rounded_rectangle` doesn't antialias; fix is 4x supersample + LANCZOS downsample, authored at largest-use size (never upscaled).
- **Neon border scaling formula**: authored at 576x432/r=28, scaled by `box_height/432` to fit any target box (hero/aside/PIP).
- **PIP resized 576x432 → 512x384** to allow centered captions to clear both corner positions.
- **Caption strip optimization**: render captions as a 1920x320 strip (not full 1920x1080) composited at y=760, cutting render time from ~16x realtime to ~3.4x.
- **Caption/output-timeline drift bug**: cue timing must be computed from PROBED clip durations (including crossfade-chain arithmetic), never from nominal EDL duration summation, because crossfades shrink total duration.
- **Audio-graph isolation**: video and audio must be processed in SEPARATE ffmpeg passes then muxed — combining a slow VP9-alpha video filter with an audio filter in one `-filter_complex` silently drops audio frames.
- **Two-pass loudnorm**: measure then apply with `measured_*` params for determinism; target I=-14 LUFS, TP=-1.5 dBTP, LRA=11.
- **Decoded-sample-count verification**: the only reliable way to detect hidden audio loss (packet counts and declared durations can both lie).
- **Privacy blur technique**: pixelate-then-blur (16x downscale → nearest-neighbor upscale → boxblur), not plain blur, for credential-shaped text; must account for Ken-Burns zoom ramps that reveal/hide chrome at different frames.
- **Vertical Shorts compositing**: reuses 16:9 audio/cuts/transcript; webcam full-width (not cropped-and-scaled beyond ~1.7x), screen beats get targeted crops (not 9:16 slices) in a separate band.
- **baz.studio CLI** (Remotion-based, v0.8.28): `baz scenes create/set-code` cost no AI tokens; `baz prompt` does; `baz export start --format webm` for alpha-capable output (historically broken); free tier watermarks all exports.
- **"Fern-style" premium aesthetic**: restrained/subtractive — near-black graded backgrounds, single accent color, light-weight typography, slow single-element motion, minimal border treatment, ambient sound design, longer holds/pacing.
- **ffmpeg filter-graph gotchas discovered**: Windows drive-colon paths break `movie=` filter (must use real `-i` input instead); intermediate labels can only be consumed once (need explicit `split`); geq expressions with nested parens/commas are fragile — prefer pre-rendered antialiased PNG masks.

## 3. Files and Code Sections

### Core pipeline files under `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/scripts/`:

- **`timeline.py`**: Global timeline module. Maps global range → `(part, webcam_ss, screen_ss, dur)` via `resolve()`. Contains `PART_FILES`, `WEBCAM_DUR`, `SCREEN_DUR`, `SCREEN_OFFSET` (measured per-part: `{1: 0.030, 2: 0.030, 3: 0.030, 4: 0.010, 5: 0.050, 6: 0.050}`), `PART_START`, asserts no range spans a part boundary.

- **`sync_parts.py`**: Cross-correlation-based screen/webcam offset measurement using 3 sample windows per part.

- **`build_edl.py`**: Constructs `edl.json` with 60 ranges. Contains:
  - `REAL_MAX_WORD = 0.55`, `PAD_OUT = 0.15`, `PAD_IN = 0.12`, `GUARD = 0.06` for word-boundary autopad.
  - `NO_AUTOPAD` set of `(idx, edge)` tuples for deliberate exclusions.
  - `autopad()` function — first-pass padding.
  - Second pass added: imports `snap` from `snap_cuts.py`, snaps each boundary to silence with a `limit` bound derived from neighboring word onset (`+0.03s`/`-0.03s` guard).
  - Full `R` list of 60+ `(start, end, beat, layout, pip, quote, reason)` tuples covering the whole episode narrative (HOOK, BACKGROUND, TRACK_RECORD, STAKES, THESIS, COMMUNITY_WHY, PROJECT, AESTHETIC, PLAN, TOUR_BRAND/HOME/SECTIONS/SIGNUP/GLOW/NARROW/BLOG, BUG_1, TODO, DICTATION, WAIT, NXEON, BOARD, COMMUNITY, OAUTH, OFFLINE, BUG_2, DICTATION_2, CONTACT, DASHBOARD, PAYOFF, QOL, REALITY, OUTRO beats).

- **`snap_cuts.py`**: New file. Silence-based cut snapping.
  ```python
  SR = 16000
  HOP = 0.005
  HOLD = 0.060
  MAX_EXT_OUT = 0.45
  MAX_EXT_IN = 0.35
  INSET = 0.045
  CTX = 2.0
  BELOW_SPEECH_DB = 26.0
  ```
  `_local_floor()` computes threshold from 92nd percentile of local envelope minus 26dB. `snap(part, t_local, edge, limit=None)` walks forward/backward; OUT-only fallback extends to just before next word's onset if no gap found (no IN-side equivalent, since retreating with no silence drags in the previous word's tail).

- **`words.py`**: transcript lookup utility (`dump`, `find` by phrase).

- **`contact_sheet.py`**: extracts labeled frame grids from screen or webcam source for visual verification; supports `--webcam` flag.

- **`merge_transcripts.py`**, **`gen_caption_cues.py`** (early scaffolding, later superseded by `gen_captions.py`).

- **`gen_captions.py`**: ASR correction + caption cue generation.
  - `FIXES` dict: `{"codely":"kodely","Codely":"Kodely","Cloudmax":"Claude Max","Nexion":"Nxeon","Shrite":"Stripe","SAS":"SaaS"}`
  - `FIXES_AT = {1616.51: "Claude"}` (disambiguates "cloud" from "Claude").
  - `MERGE_PAIRS = [(1435.50, 1435.78, "Kodely")]` (merges split "Code"+".ly" tokens).
  - `BLACKOUT_RANGES = {3, 4, 7, 9, 11, 39, 52, 59}` — ranges where cards occupy screen space, cues suppressed.
  - **Critical fix added**: `output_starts(edl)` function — probes REAL clip durations from `clips_composited/` and `clips_transitions/`, handles crossfade-chain arithmetic (`starts[s] = cum + off; off += dur(clip) - cf.XFADE_DUR`), replacing the old nominal-duration-summation approach that caused up to 2s of caption drift.
  - `blackout_windows(edl, starts)` updated to take `starts` param.
  - `main()` updated to call `output_starts(edl)` and use per-range `cum = starts[idx]` instead of accumulating nominal durations.

- **`make_captions_slot.py`**: Builds `slot_captions` HyperFrames composition (1920x320 canvas, composited at y=760). `CANVAS_W, CANVAS_H = 1920, 320`, `MAX_WIDTH = 620`, dark pill fill `rgba(32,14,26,0.72)` / `rgba(22,10,20,0.64)`.

- **`bbox.py`**: Measures real alpha-channel content bounding box of rendered graphics across N samples over full duration (not just one frame). `ALPHA_MIN = 12`.

- **`make_graphics.py`**: Shared HyperFrames shell generator for 6 new cards (`slot_zero_stack`, `slot_todo_card`, `slot_credits_750`, `slot_board_stat`, `slot_kodely_live`, `slot_time_90`). Two background fills: `BG_STAGE` (light glass, for dark retrowave hero) and `BG_SCREEN` (dark tinted glass, for cards over light/unpredictable screen content) — picked by checking what's actually under the card, not by hero-vs-screen category (board_stat card kept BG_STAGE despite being a screen-beat card, because the board itself is dark).

- **`composite_full.py`**: Main compositing script. Key constants:
  ```python
  HERO_W, HERO_H = 1306, 980
  HERO_X, HERO_Y = 307, 50
  ASIDE_W, ASIDE_H = 850, 638
  ASIDE_CX, ASIDE_CY = 1455, 540
  SHRINK_DUR = 0.5
  BORDER_NATIVE_H = 432
  PIP_W, PIP_H = 512, 384  # changed from 576x432
  BORDER_W, BORDER_H = 1706, 960
  BORDER_DX, BORDER_DY = 597, 288
  POS = {"bottom_right": (1368, 656), "bottom_left": (40, 656)}
  XFADE_DUR = 0.4
  DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES = {3, 4, 7, 9, 39, 52, 59}
  ```
  `ZOOMS` dict with per-range Ken-Burns configs (verified against real frames). `OVERLAYS` dict mapping range→list of graphic overlay configs. `PRIVACY` dict added for blur regions:
  ```python
  _GCP_ID = dict(x=324, y=32, w=114, h=40)
  PRIVACY: dict[int, list[dict]] = {
      36: [dict(x=0, y=0, w=1010, h=128, at=[(0.0, 2.7), (12.2, 99.0)])],
      37: [dict(x=52, y=14, w=620, h=78)],
      40: [dict(**_GCP_ID)],
      41: [dict(**_GCP_ID)],
      42: [dict(**_GCP_ID)],
  }
  ```
  `privacy_chain()` function implements pixelate-then-blur via split/crop/scale-down/scale-up-nearest/boxblur/overlay-with-enable-window.
  Contains `overlay_chain()`, `build_webcam_primary()`, `build_screen_primary()`, `build_transition()`, `zoom_filter()`, `_shrink_u_expr()`, `_hero_transform()`, chain-grouping logic in `main()` for consecutive crossfade boundaries (fixed a double-emission bug when boundaries share a segment, e.g. 51→52→53).
  Also fixed: rounded-corner mask now authored at HERO size (`pip_mask.png` regenerated at 1306x980, r=64, antialiased via 4x supersample+LANCZOS in `make_pip_assets.py`), scaled DOWN for PIP path (previously it was PIP-sized and stretched UP 2.5x for hero shots, causing a jagged dark fringe on corner arcs — confirmed via native-resolution nearest-neighbor crop comparison).

- **`finalize.py`**: Rewritten to 3 separate steps (was 1 combined filter_complex):
  ```python
  TARGET_I, TARGET_TP, TARGET_LRA = -14.0, -1.5, 11.0
  ```
  `decoded_samples(p)` — ground-truth audio content check via raw PCM byte count.
  `hidden_time(p)` — sums excess duration across packets with `duration_time > AAC_FRAME*1.5` (AAC_FRAME=1024/48000≈0.0213s), distinguishing a harmless single stretched packet from real hidden holes (threshold 0.25s abort).
  Steps: [1/4] measure loudness, [2/4] video pass (caption overlay, `-an`), [3/4] audio pass (loudnorm, separate), [4/4] mux with `-c copy`. Verifies decoded sample count matches source within 0.25s tolerance, aborts otherwise.

- **`gen_captions.py`**, **`make_captions_slot.py`**, **`finalize.py`** — all re-run multiple times as bugs were found and fixed (captions rendered 3 times total: v1 wrong timing base, v2 still using nominal-duration timeline before the crossfade-fix was discovered, v3 final with `output_starts()` fix).

- **`shorts.py`**: New file for vertical (1080x1920) Shorts compositor.
  ```python
  W, H = 1080, 1920
  CAM_W, CAM_H, CAM_Y = 1080, 810, 100
  SLOT_Y, SLOT_H = 980, 608
  SCRIM = 0.25
  NEON_S = CAM_H / 432  # reused neon scaling trick
  ```
  `SHORTS["glow"]` dict defines the 3-clip Short: hero clip (1984.90-1996.74) with `slot_time_90` card, then 2 screen clips (1997.19-2003.61, 2003.81-2021.20) with `crop=(600, 458, 700, 394)` tightened from an initial looser crop.
  `bg_chain()` — retrowave scaled to cover 1080x1920 portrait, scrimmed.
  `build_clip()` — builds each vertical clip with webcam/screen/card compositing.

- **`shorts_captions.py`**: Vertical caption generator/finalizer. `STRIP_H=320`, `MAX_WIDTH=900`, `FONT_PX=50`, `MAX_CHUNK=5`. Fixed two Windows-specific bugs: (1) bare `["npx", ...]` argv fails with `FileNotFoundError [WinError 2]` — needed `shell=True` with a formatted string; (2) `-o render.webm` resolves against CWD not project dir — needed absolute path `str(slot / "render.webm")`.

- **`looktest.py`**: New file for premium-style look test (still-frame comparison, no render needed). 
  ```python
  HERO_T = 1990.0
  SCREEN_T = 2010.0
  GRADE = ("curves=all='0/0.028 0.25/0.255 0.5/0.5 0.75/0.765 1/0.975',"
           "eq=contrast=1.06:saturation=0.86:gamma=1.01,"
           "colorbalance=rh=0.03:gh=0.01:bh=-0.03")
  ```
  `ground()` — generates a dark graded field via ffmpeg `color`+`geq`+`noise`+`vignette` (no render pipeline needed). `hero_premium()` and `screen_premium()` build comparison frames. Final panel size for screen crop: `PW, PH = 1780, 890` (near-full-bleed, after an initial too-small 1500x812 attempt that sacrificed legibility). Uses new antialiased mask assets `panel_mask_1780x890.png` (generated via `make_pip_assets.py --width 1780 --height 890 --radius 22`).

### Assets:
- `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/assets/pip_mask.png` — regenerated at hero size (1306x980, r=64) with antialiasing.
- `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/assets/v_webcam_mask.png` (1080x810, r=53) and `v_screen_mask.png` (1080x608, r=26) for vertical Shorts.
- `vibe-coding-ep1-kodely/edit/assets/panel_mask_1780x890.png` for look-test screen panel.

### Documentation:
- **`tools/video-use/LIQUID_GLASS_STYLE.md`**: Extensively updated with new sections: "Motion" additions (transform-only animation rule, count-up timing), Caption sections (width-vs-PIP constraint math, strip-render optimization, blackout windows, ASR brand-name fixing), "Rounded-corner mask: antialias it, and author it at HERO size", "Cut boundaries, part 2: snap to SILENCE, not to ASR word times", "Final render: never put the caption overlay and the audio in one filter graph", "Do not confuse expected-timeline arithmetic with real drift", "Privacy: blocking out URLs and credentials on screen", "Caption cues must be built on the REAL output timeline".
- **`tools/video-use/templates/vibe-coding-series/README.md`**: Updated starting-episode steps (multi-part handling, silence-snapping requirement, three-step finalize), known-good parameter values table (PIP 512x384, caption specs, loudnorm target), "Lessons from episode 2's first cut" section, "Open items" section updated with episode-2 findings.
- **`tools/video-use/templates/vibe-coding-series/baz-assets/README.md`**: Originally documented August 2026 alpha-export bug. Updated 2026-08-21 with re-test confirming bug still present (verbatim error message preserved) plus watermark confirmation. **Most recently (2026-08-22, in-progress)**: being updated again with the "try baz now" re-test results — error is now GONE (webm exports complete successfully as VP8+Opus), but alpha is STILL absent (verified via pixel sampling: 1 unique alpha level, 0% transparent) and watermark still present at both low and high quality. This edit had just been applied via perl substitution when the conversation was cut off; the new section reads: "**Re-tested 2026-08-22 on baz CLI v0.8.28 -- PARTIALLY FIXED, still unusable.**" followed by details, then a "PREVIOUS STATE (2026-08-21, for history):" marker preserving the old findings below it.

### Memory files (referenced, not modified in the visible portion after the initial episode):
- `C:\Users\edmem\.claude\projects\...\memory\video_editing_style_prefs.md` — contains prior learned preferences (liquid-glass aesthetic default, PIP behavior, zoom discipline, webcam-audio-master rule, loudness-check requirement, verify-agent-work discipline). Two new entries were added earlier in the session (webcam-master-audio preference, loudness-check-before-shipping preference) — these are already-saved from before this summary window's tail end.

## 4. Errors and Fixes

1. **`contact_sheet.py` drawtext font crash**: bare `text='...'` font resolution failed on Windows console default fonts → fixed with explicit `fontfile='C\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf'`.
2. **`seg_frames.py` xstack error on single-tile input**: `subprocess.CalledProcessError` when only 1 frame passed to xstack — worked around by ensuring multiple frames or handling single case (not fully detailed but resolved by continuing with corrected paths).
3. **26 seconds of audio silently destroyed**: root cause = combining caption-overlay video filter + loudnorm audio filter in one `-filter_complex`. Fixed by splitting into 3 independent ffmpeg invocations (video-only, audio-only, then mux). Added hard verification gate (`decoded_samples()` comparison, abort if >0.25s missing).
4. **False "A/V drift" self-correction**: I initially reported growing drift up to -368ms across the video during debugging. Root cause was MY OWN measurement methodology using nominal EDL durations instead of real probed clip durations for expected timestamps. Recomputing with real probed durations (including crossfade-chain math) showed a FLAT -21ms offset (the correlation method's own constant), not real drift. I explicitly told the user I had made this error and corrected it.
5. **30/60 out-points, 11/60 in-points clipping speech**: root cause = relying solely on ASR word-timestamp padding (`autopad`), which is approximate/capped and doesn't guarantee the boundary lands in true silence. Fixed with `snap_cuts.py` silence-detection second pass. User's exact words: "theres a lot of instances where my voice gets cut off short" — treated as a serious, systemic bug requiring root-cause analysis, not a one-off tweak.
6. **Caption drift up to 2 seconds by video end**: root cause = `gen_captions.py` computing cue times by summing nominal EDL range durations, not accounting for the 6 scene-change crossfades each removing 0.4s from actual output length. Caught via `output_starts()` cross-check BEFORE wasting a ~45-minute caption re-render — I explicitly killed a running background render (`TaskStop` on `bnooolu8i`) upon discovering this, before it wasted more compute.
7. **Jagged webcam corners on hero shots**: root cause = non-antialiased rounded-rect mask (PIL default has only 0/255 alpha values) authored at PIP size and stretched 2.5x for hero — visible as dark stair-step fringe on the arc at native resolution. Fixed via 4x supersample+LANCZOS antialiasing AND authoring the mask at hero size (scaling down for PIP instead of up for hero).
8. **Naive "clipped word" detection metric was wrong**: an early check flagged 36 output-level cuts as bad by testing "is there speech energy right after the cut" — this incorrectly flags GOOD clean cuts too, since the next word naturally starts shortly after any cut. """Still-frame look test: current retrowave/neon style vs a restrained pass.

Stills rather than clips on purpose -- palette, grade, framing and chrome are
all judgeable from a frame, and this costs seconds instead of a render.

The restrained pass changes five things, all subtractive:
  1. background   retrowave scene -> near-black graded field + vignette + grain
  2. border       travelling neon comets -> hairline rim + real drop shadow
  3. grade        none -> lifted blacks, mild desaturation, warm highlights
  4. chrome       raw browser (tabs/URL/bookmarks) -> cropped away, page in a
                  floating rounded panel
  5. type         (see the card comparison; not in this frame test)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = EDIT / "verify" / "looktest"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
FONT = "fontfile='C\\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf'"

HERO_T = 1990.0
SCREEN_T = 2010.0

# Filmic-ish grade: lift the blacks off zero, pull a little saturation out,
# warm the highlights. Applied to the WEBCAM and SCREEN, never to the
# background plate (which is already authored at the target values).
GRADE = ("curves=all='0/0.028 0.25/0.255 0.5/0.5 0.75/0.765 1/0.975',"
         "eq=contrast=1.06:saturation=0.86:gamma=1.01,"
         "colorbalance=rh=0.03:gh=0.01:bh=-0.03")

# Restrained ground: a very dark desaturated field with a soft centre lift and
# fine animated-looking grain. Cheap to make in ffmpeg -- no render needed,
# which also means no 20s loop to keep in sync with anything.
def ground(w=1920, h=1080):
    return (
        f"color=c=0x0B0A0E:s={w}x{h},"
        f"geq=r='r(X,Y)+44*exp(-((X-{w/2})^2/(2*{(w*0.55)**2})+(Y-{h*0.42})^2/(2*{(h*0.62)**2})))'"
        f":g='g(X,Y)+27*exp(-((X-{w/2})^2/(2*{(w*0.55)**2})+(Y-{h*0.42})^2/(2*{(h*0.62)**2})))'"
        f":b='b(X,Y)+34*exp(-((X-{w/2})^2/(2*{(w*0.55)**2})+(Y-{h*0.42})^2/(2*{(h*0.62)**2})))',"
        f"noise=alls=6:allf=t+u,"
        f"vignette=angle=PI/5"
    )


def run(cmd):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", " ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:400])
        print(r.stderr[-2500:])
        sys.exit(1)


def label(p, text):
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".lbl.png")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(p), "-vf",
         f"drawtext={FONT}:text='{text}':x=24:y=22:fontsize=34:fontcolor=white:"
         f"box=1:boxcolor=black@0.75:boxborderw=12", str(tmp)])
    return tmp


def hero_premium(out: Path):
    src = resolve(HERO_T, HERO_T + 0.4)
    # webcam 1306x980 centred, rounded, hairline rim, real shadow
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error",
         "-f", "lavfi", "-i", ground(),
         "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
         "-i", str(EDIT / "assets" / "pip_mask.png"),
         "-filter_complex",
         f"[1:v]scale=1306:980,{GRADE}[cam];"
         f"[2:v]scale=1306:980[m];"
         f"[cam][m]alphamerge[camr];"
         # shadow: the mask itself, blurred and darkened, sat behind the box
         f"[2:v]scale=1306:980,boxblur=34:2,geq=lum='p(X,Y)*0.72':a='p(X,Y)'[sh];"
         f"color=c=black:s=1306x980[shc];[shc][sh]alphamerge[shadow];"
         f"[0:v][shadow]overlay=x=307:y=68[bgs];"
         f"[bgs][camr]overlay=x=307:y=50[v]",
         "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(out)])


def screen_premium(out: Path):
    src = resolve(SCREEN_T, SCREEN_T + 0.4)
    # Browser chrome lives in the top ~120px. Crop it away and float the page
    # in a rounded panel instead of showing raw OS chrome.
    PW, PH = 1780, 890   # near-full-bleed: shrinking the page for aesthetics
                          # costs legibility, which matters more on a
                          # screen-recording channel than the margin does
    # NB: the mask goes in as a real -i input, not via the movie= filter --
    # a Windows path's drive colon breaks filter-string parsing.
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error",
         "-f", "lavfi", "-i", ground(),
         "-ss", f"{src['screen_ss']}", "-i", src["screen_path"],
         "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
         "-i", str(EDIT / "assets" / "pip_mask.png"),
         "-i", str(EDIT / "assets" / "panel_mask_1780x890.png"),
         "-filter_complex",
         # page: drop chrome, then fit the panel
         f"[1:v]crop=1920:960:0:120,scale={PW}:{PH},{GRADE}[pg];"
         # The rounded panel mask is a real antialiased PNG (make_pip_assets),
         # not a geq expression -- easier to get right and it gets a proper
         # alpha ramp on the corners. alphamerge reads its second input's
         # LUMA, and the shadow blurs the same shape, so one gray image
         # serves both. ffmpeg auto-splits an INPUT pad used twice; an
         # intermediate label would need an explicit split.
         f"[4:v][pg]scale2ref=w=iw:h=ih[pm][pg2];"
         f"[pg2][pm]alphamerge[pgr];"
         f"[4:v]boxblur=30:2,eq=brightness=-0.18[psh];"
         f"color=c=black:s={PW}x{PH}[pshc];[pshc][psh]alphamerge[pshadow];"
         f"[0:v][pshadow]overlay=x=70:y=112[bgs];"
         f"[bgs][pgr]overlay=x=70:y=95[withpg];"
         # webcam PIP bottom-right, graded, rounded
         f"[2:v]scale=512:384,{GRADE}[cam];"
         f"[3:v]scale=512:384[cm];"
         f"[cam][cm]alphamerge[camr];"
         f"[withpg][camr]overlay=x=1352:y=640[v]",
         "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(out)])


def main():
    cur_hero = OUT / "cur_hero.png"
    cur_scr = OUT / "cur_screen.png"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", "7.5",
         "-i", str(EDIT / "clips_composited" / "seg_52.mp4"),
         "-frames:v", "1", str(cur_hero)])
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", "8.0",
         "-i", str(EDIT / "clips_composited" / "seg_54.mp4"),
         "-frames:v", "1", str(cur_scr)])
    new_hero, new_scr = OUT / "new_hero.png", OUT / "new_screen.png"
    hero_premium(new_hero)
    screen_premium(new_scr)

    tiles = [label(cur_hero, "CURRENT  hero"), label(new_hero, "RESTRAINED  hero"),
             label(cur_scr, "CURRENT  screen"), label(new_scr, "RESTRAINED  screen")]
    args = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error"]
    for t in tiles:
        args += ["-i", str(t)]
    args += ["-filter_complex",
             "[0:v]scale=960:540[a];[1:v]scale=960:540[b];"
             "[2:v]scale=960:540[c];[3:v]scale=960:540[d];"
             "[a][b][c][d]xstack=inputs=4:layout=0_0|960_0|0_540|960_540[v]",
             "-map", "[v]", "-frames:v", "1", str(OUT / "compare.png")]
    run(args)
    print(f"-> {OUT / 'compare.png'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Build vertical (1080x1920) YouTube Shorts from this episode's footage.

A Short is NOT a crop of the 16:9 edit. Two things force a different build:

* The webcam source is 640x480. Filling a 1080x1920 frame from it means a ~4x
  upscale, which looks awful. So the webcam stays modest at 1000x750 (a
  1.56x upscale) and the rest of the frame is used for other things rather
  than for more webcam.
* A 9:16 slice of a 1920x1080 browser loses whatever is being pointed at.
  Screen beats instead get a CROP of the region that matters, taken at or
  near native resolution and placed in its own band below the webcam.

Layout (1080x1920), and note what drives it -- the SHORTS UI SAFE AREA:
    y   60.. 810   webcam, 1000x750, rounded + neon border
    y  850..1390   screen crop, or a motion-graphic card on talking-head beats
    y ~1420..1600  caption pill
    y 1600..1920   left empty ON PURPOSE

YouTube overlays the bottom of a Short with the title, channel handle and
description, and stacks the like/comment/share buttons up the right side.
A first pass put the caption pill 80px from the bottom edge, which puts it
straight behind that UI. Everything that must be readable now ends by y=1600,
leaving a 320px bottom margin. That constraint is what sizes the webcam
(1000x750, not full-width) and the screen band -- not aesthetics.

Audio, cut points and the transcript all come straight from the 16:9 build --
the cuts are already snapped to silence there, so they are reused as-is.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from timeline import resolve  # noqa: E402

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ANIM = EDIT / "animations"
ASSETS = EDIT / "assets"
OUT_DIR = EDIT / "shorts"
OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

RETROWAVE = ANIM / "slot_retrowave_bg_loop" / "render.mp4"
NEON = ANIM / "slot_neon_border_loop" / "render.webm"
W, H = 1080, 1920

CAM_W, CAM_H, CAM_Y = 1000, 750, 60
CAM_X = (1080 - CAM_W) // 2
SLOT_Y, SLOT_H, SLOT_W = 850, 540, 1000   # screen crop / card band
SCRIM = 0.25

# The neon rail is authored as 576x432 centred in a 1920x1080 frame. Scale the
# whole frame by CAM_H/432 and the rail becomes exactly the webcam box; then
# offset so that rail lands at (0, CAM_Y). Same trick as the 16:9 build.
NEON_S = CAM_H / 432                       # 1.875
NEON_W = 2 * round(1920 * NEON_S / 2)      # 3600
NEON_H = 2 * round(1080 * NEON_S / 2)      # 2026
NEON_X = CAM_X - ((NEON_W - CAM_W) // 2)
NEON_Y = CAM_Y - ((NEON_H - CAM_H) // 2)

SHORTS = {
    # "90 minutes on one glow" -- hook is the frustration, payoff is the fix
    # actually working on screen. Cut points are the 16:9 edit's, already
    # snapped to silence.
    "glow": dict(
        title="90 minutes to fix one glow",
        clips=[
            dict(kind="hero", start=1984.90, end=1996.74,
                 card=dict(path=ANIM / "slot_time_90" / "render.webm",
                           # crop the card down to its measured content box
                           # (bbox.py said x41..837 y263..746) so it can be
                           # scaled to the vertical slot without dead margin
                           src=(41, 263, 800, 484), out_w=900,
                           rel_start=1.30, dur=5.85)),
            dict(kind="screen", start=1997.19, end=2003.61,
                 crop=(600, 466, 700, 378)),
            dict(kind="screen", start=2003.81, end=2021.20,
                 crop=(600, 466, 700, 378)),
        ],
    ),
}


def run(cmd, label):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("FAILED:", label)
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe(p):
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def afade(dur):
    return f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={max(0.0,dur-0.03):.3f}:d=0.03"


def bg_chain():
    """Retrowave scaled to COVER 1080x1920 and centre-cropped, with the scrim.
    The source is 1920x1080, so covering a portrait frame means a 1.78x
    upscale -- fine for a soft gradient, and it puts the horizon band right
    around the middle of the frame, between the webcam and the lower slot."""
    keep = 1 - SCRIM
    sw = 2 * round(1920 * (H / 1080) / 2)
    return (f"[1:v]scale={sw}:{H},crop={W}:{H}:{(sw - W) // 2}:0,"
            f"colorchannelmixer=rr={keep}:gg={keep}:bb={keep}[bg];")


def build_clip(i, c, out: Path):
    src = resolve(c["start"], c["end"])
    dur = src["dur"]
    inputs = [
        "-ss", f"{src['webcam_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["webcam_path"],
        "-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE),
        "-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON),
        "-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "v_webcam_mask.png"),
    ]
    nxt = 4
    filt = bg_chain()
    # webcam: scale to the band, round the corners, neon rail on top of the bg
    filt += (
        f"[0:v]scale={CAM_W}:{CAM_H}[cam];"
        f"[3:v]scale={CAM_W}:{CAM_H}[cmask];"
        f"[cam][cmask]alphamerge[camr];"
        f"[2:v]scale={NEON_W}:{NEON_H}:flags=bilinear[nb];"
        f"[bg][nb]overlay=x={NEON_X}:y={NEON_Y}[bgb];"
        f"[bgb][camr]overlay=x={CAM_X}:y={CAM_Y}[base];"
    )
    label = "base"

    if c["kind"] == "screen":
        cx, cy, cw, ch = c["crop"]
        inputs += ["-ss", f"{src['screen_ss']}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", src["screen_path"],
                   "-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "v_screen_mask.png")]
        si, mi = nxt, nxt + 1
        nxt += 2
        filt += (
            f"[{si}:v]crop={cw}:{ch}:{cx}:{cy},scale={SLOT_W}:{SLOT_H}:flags=lanczos[scr];"
            f"[{mi}:v]scale={SLOT_W}:{SLOT_H}[smask];"
            f"[scr][smask]alphamerge[scrr];"
            f"[{label}][scrr]overlay=x={(W - SLOT_W) // 2}:y={SLOT_Y}[withscr];"
        )
        label = "withscr"
    elif c.get("card"):
        cd = c["card"]
        sx, sy, sw_, sh_ = cd["src"]
        ow = cd["out_w"]
        oh = 2 * round((sh_ * ow / sw_) / 2)
        inputs += ["-itsoffset", f"{cd['rel_start']}", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9",
                   "-i", str(cd["path"])]
        ci = nxt
        nxt += 1
        s, e = cd["rel_start"], cd["rel_start"] + cd["dur"]
        filt += (
            f"[{ci}:v]crop={sw_}:{sh_}:{sx}:{sy},scale={ow}:{oh}:flags=bilinear[card];"
            f"[{label}][card]overlay=x={(W - ow) // 2}:y={SLOT_Y}:"
            f"enable='between(t\\,{s}\\,{e})'[withcard];"
        )
        label = "withcard"

    filt += f"[0:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", f"[{label}]", "-map", "[a]",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:a", "aac", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", "-r", "60", "-t", f"{dur}",
         str(out), "-loglevel", "error"], f"clip {i}")


def main():
    name = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "glow"
    spec = SHORTS[name]
    d = OUT_DIR / name
    d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    paths = []
    for i, c in enumerate(spec["clips"]):
        p = d / f"c{i:02d}.mp4"
        if not p.exists():
            build_clip(i, c, p)
        paths.append(p)
        print(f"  clip {i} {c['kind']:<6} {c['start']:.2f}-{c['end']:.2f}  "
              f"{probe(p):.2f}s")
    lst = d / "concat.txt"
    lst.write_text("\n".join(f"file '{p.as_posix()}'" for p in paths), encoding="utf-8")
    out = d / "silent.mp4"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", str(lst),
         "-c", "copy", str(out), "-loglevel", "error"], "concat")
    print(f"\n{name}: {probe(out):.2f}s -> {out}")
    # real output start of each clip, for caption timing
    starts, cum = [], 0.0
    for p in paths:
        starts.append(cum)
        cum += probe(p)
    (d / "starts.json").write_text(json.dumps(starts), encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Final pass: burn in captions and fix the audio level.

Input:  composited_draft.mp4 (segments + graphics + transitions, concatenated)
Output: final.mp4

WHY THIS IS THREE STEPS AND NOT ONE FILTER GRAPH
------------------------------------------------
The obvious version does the caption overlay and the loudness normalisation
in a single `-filter_complex` with both a video and an audio branch. That
version SILENTLY DROPPED 26 SECONDS OF AUDIO on this episode: 1252 AAC frames
vanished at 10 points, and the muxer papered over each hole by writing a
single packet with a ~3s `duration` instead of 21ms. The file still reported
the right total duration, so nothing looked wrong -- but players jumped
forward at each hole and the audio ran ahead of the picture from then on.

The audio chain on its own is fine (verified: zero samples lost). It only
breaks when it shares a graph with the slow VP9-alpha video branch. So the
two are processed independently and muxed at the end, which also makes each
step separately checkable.

VERIFY_* below are not optional decoration -- they are the check that would
have caught the bug. Any mismatch aborts instead of writing a broken file.

AUDIO: sources sit around -44 LUFS, ~30 dB under the -14 LUFS streaming
target. Normalised ONCE on the whole concatenated track (never per segment,
which would pump at every cut), two-pass so it is deterministic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = EDIT / "composited_draft.mp4"
CAPTIONS = EDIT / "animations" / "slot_captions" / "render.webm"
OUT = EDIT / "final.mp4"
TMP_V = EDIT / "_final_video.mp4"
TMP_A = EDIT / "_final_audio.m4a"

CAPTION_Y = 760
TARGET_I, TARGET_TP, TARGET_LRA = -14.0, -1.5, 11.0


def run(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(cmd)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {label}")
        sys.exit(1)


def probe(p: Path, stream: str, entries: str) -> str:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", stream,
                        "-show_entries", entries, "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout.strip()


def decoded_samples(p: Path) -> int:
    """Number of mono samples ffmpeg actually decodes -- the ground truth for
    'is any audio missing', which packet counts and declared durations do not
    tell you."""
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-f", "s16le", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "48000", "-"],
                       capture_output=True)
    return len(r.stdout) // 2


AAC_FRAME = 1024 / 48000.0  # 21.3ms


def hidden_time(p: Path) -> tuple[float, int]:
    """Total time the container claims for audio packets BEYOND one AAC
    frame each, plus how many such packets there are.

    This is the fingerprint of a muxer papering over dropped audio: when a
    hole appears, the packet before it gets its duration stretched to span
    the gap. Report the SUM, not the count -- a single stretched packet can
    be a harmless timestamp quirk (an isolated ~80ms one here was verified
    against the source waveform as bit-identical, lag 0, r=0.99997), whereas
    the real failure this guards against was 10 packets hiding 26.9 SECONDS.
    Counting packets flags both identically; summing separates them."""
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "a:0",
                        "-show_entries", "packet=duration_time", "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    excess, n = 0.0, 0
    for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
        line = line.strip().rstrip(",")
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            d = float(line.split(",")[0])
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if d > AAC_FRAME * 1.5:
            excess += d - AAC_FRAME
            n += 1
    return excess, n


def measure(p: Path) -> dict:
    print("[1/4] measuring loudness ...")
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-af", f"loudnorm=I={TARGET_I}:TP={TARGET_TP}:LRA={TARGET_LRA}"
                               ":print_format=json", "-f", "null", "-"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = re.findall(r"\{[^{}]*\"input_i\"[^{}]*\}", r.stderr, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("could not parse loudnorm measurement:\n", r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)
    d = json.loads(m[-1])
    print(f"      in: I={d['input_i']} LUFS  TP={d['input_tp']} dBTP  LRA={d['input_lra']}")
    return d


def main() -> None:
    if not SRC.exists():
        print(f"missing {SRC} -- run composite_full.py first")
        sys.exit(1)
    if not CAPTIONS.exists():
        print(f"missing {CAPTIONS} -- render the caption slot first")
        sys.exit(1)

    ref_samples = decoded_samples(SRC)
    print(f"      source audio: {ref_samples} samples ({ref_samples/48000:.2f}s)")

    d = measure(SRC)

    print("[2/4] video: burning in captions ...")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-stats",
         "-i", str(SRC), "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(CAPTIONS),
         "-filter_complex", f"[0:v][1:v]overlay=x=0:y={CAPTION_Y}:eof_action=pass[v]",
         "-map", "[v]", "-an",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "19",
         "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-r", "60", str(TMP_V)], "video pass")

    print("[3/4] audio: normalising ...")
    af = (f"loudnorm=I={TARGET_I}:TP={TARGET_TP}:LRA={TARGET_LRA}"
          f":measured_I={d['input_i']}:measured_TP={d['input_tp']}"
          f":measured_LRA={d['input_lra']}:measured_thresh={d['input_thresh']}"
          f":offset={d['target_offset']}:linear=true,aresample=48000")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(SRC), "-map", "0:a", "-af", af,
         "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(TMP_A)],
        "audio pass")

    got = decoded_samples(TMP_A)
    lost = ref_samples - got
    print(f"      audio out: {got} samples, delta {lost:+d} ({lost/48000:+.3f}s)")
    if abs(lost) > 48000 * 0.25:   # a quarter second of slack for codec padding
        print(f"ABORT: audio pass lost {lost/48000:.2f}s of content.")
        sys.exit(1)

    print("[4/4] muxing ...")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(TMP_V), "-i", str(TMP_A),
         "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c", "copy",
         "-movflags", "+faststart", str(OUT)], "mux")

    # --- verify the thing we actually ship -------------------------------
    fin = decoded_samples(OUT)
    excess, n_odd = hidden_time(OUT)
    vdur = float(probe(OUT, "v:0", "stream=duration") or 0)
    adur = float(probe(OUT, "a:0", "stream=duration") or 0)
    ok = True
    print(f"\nfinal: video {vdur:.2f}s  audio {adur:.2f}s  "
          f"decoded {fin} samples ({fin/48000:.2f}s)")
    if abs(fin - ref_samples) > 48000 * 0.25:
        print(f"  FAIL: {(ref_samples-fin)/48000:.2f}s of audio missing vs source"); ok = False
    if excess > 0.25:
        print(f"  FAIL: {excess:.2f}s hidden behind {n_odd} stretched audio packets"); ok = False
    elif n_odd:
        print(f"  note: {n_odd} stretched audio packet(s) totalling {excess*1000:.0f}ms "
              f"-- below the 250ms threshold, content verified intact")
    if abs(vdur - adur) > 0.5:
        print(f"  FAIL: video/audio length differ by {abs(vdur-adur):.2f}s"); ok = False
    if not ok:
        sys.exit(1)
    print("  audio content intact, no hidden holes, streams aligned")

    v = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(OUT), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-af", "ebur128=peak=true", "-f", "null", "-"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
    for key in ("I:", "LRA:", "Peak:"):
        for line in v.splitlines()[-40:]:
            if line.strip().startswith(key):
                print("  ", line.strip())
                break
    TMP_V.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    TMP_A.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    print(f"\ndone: {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
