**Done** — the video's built and sent above. Here's how the tools split up the work:

- **ffmpeg** (video-use conventions) — logged the raw 127s recording into a shot list, cut 13 footage micro-clips, crossfaded everything into one 27.2s timeline, then built the entire soundtrack (ambient bed, whoosh transitions, a success chime) from scratch — the recording's audio track turned out to be true digital silence.
- **Remotion** (self-hosted, no watermark) — rendered the 5 full-frame graphic cards: the "47+ games" poster grid, "70,000+ mods / 14B+ downloads" grid, the 50%-off discount reveal, the support/dev-team card, and the logo outro.
- **baz.studio** — authored 2 of those 5 scenes via its AI agent (`baz prompt`) before the account's $0.03 balance ran out; the other 3 I hand-wrote in the same style and added for free via `baz scenes create`. Also used it to set project-level brand/requirements context up front.
- **HyperFrames** — rendered the 4 transparent text callouts layered over the live footage (hook line, "player counts are a guide" note, "14 data centers · 4 continents" stat, dashboard lower-third).

Two things worth flagging:
1. **HyperFrames' webm/VP9 alpha export is broken** in this build (v0.8.3) — it decodes as fully opaque even though the renderer logs "needsAlpha: true". `.mov` (ProRes 4444) alpha works correctly and is what I used instead. Left a comment in [composite_overlays.py](nxeon-promo/edit/scripts/composite_overlays.py) so this doesn't need rediscovering.
2. **baz balance is $0.03.** If you top it up, two things become available: more AI-generated scene iterations, and a real Suno-composed music bed (~$0.50/call) instead of the synthesized ambient pad I built procedurally. Your call on whether that's worth it — the current soundtrack is clean and on-brand, just simpler.

Also confirmed the demo data in the recording (card `4242 4242...`, `demo@nxeon.cloud`) is all placeholder/Stripe-test data, not real — nothing needed blurring here.

content.text: Now the big piece — rebuilding the timeline with fewer/longer holds, Ken Burns zooms, and varied transitions.

input.content:
"""Step 1: cut the screen recording's juiciest moments, drop in the five
Remotion graphic cards, and crossfade the whole thing into one silent
1920x1080/60fps base video.

Revision 2 -- fixes from first-cut feedback:
  - fewer, LONGER footage holds (cut the three <=0.6s "flash" clips
    entirely -- they were the main source of the choppy/cut-off feeling,
    not worth the screen time they cost)
  - every footage clip now gets a slow Ken-Burns push toward a focal point
    instead of sitting static
  - transitions vary by context instead of one flat crossfade: quick
    same-mode footage cuts dissolve, section boundaries (footage<->
    graphic) fade through black for a more cinematic beat, and the two
    graphic-to-graphic cuts (support->outro) use a plain fade

Footage audio is real digital silence (measured -91dB across the whole
127s source) so it is dropped entirely here -- audio is built from scratch
in build_audio.py and only meets the picture at the final mux.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = EDIT.parent / "footage" / "nxeonscreen.mp4"
GFX = EDIT / "graphics"
CLIPS = EDIT / "clips"
CLIPS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
OUT = EDIT / "base_video.mp4"

FPS = 60
W, H = 1920, 1080

# (kind, src_in, src_out, file, label, transition_in, xfade_dur, focal)
# focal = (fx, fy, zoom_end) as fraction-of-frame focal point + end zoom
# factor for a slow Ken-Burns push; None for graphics (they animate
# themselves) and for the two hero shots long enough to hold static.
SHOTS = [
    ("footage", 1.00, 2.60, None, "hero", None, 0.00, (0.72, 0.35, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 10.00, 11.20, None, "build_way", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.50, 0.45, 1.06)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "poster_grid_games.mp4", "poster_games", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 16.60, 17.90, None, "plan_a", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.42, 0.40, 1.07)),
    ("footage", 20.20, 21.50, None, "plan_b", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.35, 0.55, 1.06)),
    ("footage", 27.00, 30.00, None, "globe", "dissolve", 0.18, (0.50, 0.45, 1.10)),
    ("footage", 34.00, 34.90, None, "payment", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.50, 0.40, 1.06)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "discount_reveal.mp4", "discount", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 68.20, 69.30, None, "deploy_mid", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.30, 0.35, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 72.00, 73.50, None, "deploy_live", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.30, 0.30, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 80.00, 81.30, None, "dash_a", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.42, 0.42, 1.07)),
    ("footage", 84.60, 85.90, None, "dash_b", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.60, 0.35, 1.07)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "poster_grid_mods.mp4", "poster_mods", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 104.00, 105.10, None, "config", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.35, 0.50, 1.07)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "support_card.mp4", "support", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "outro_cta.mp4", "outro", "fade", 0.22, None),
]


def run(cmd, label):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {label}")
        print(" ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:500])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_dur(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def zoom_filter(dur: float, fx: float, fy: float, zoom_end: float) -> str:
    """Slow Ken-Burns push toward (fx,fy) (fractions of frame), reaching
    zoom_end by the end of the clip. Crop a shrinking window centred on the
    focal point then scale back up -- reliable in plain ffmpeg, no zoompan
    per-frame quirks."""
    z = f"(1+({zoom_end}-1)*t/{dur})"
    w = f"(1920/{z})"
    h = f"(1080/{z})"
    x = f"max(0,min({fx}*1920-({w})/2,1920-({w})))"
    y = f"max(0,min({fy}*1080-({h})/2,1080-({h})))"
    return f"crop=w='{w}':h='{h}':x='{x}':y='{y}',scale={W}:{H}"


def extract_footage(i, s_in, s_out, focal, out: Path):
    dur = s_out - s_in
    vf = f"scale={W}:{H}"
    if focal is not None:
        fx, fy, zoom_end = focal
        vf = zoom_filter(dur, fx, fy, zoom_end)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{s_in}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", str(SRC),
         "-an", "-r", str(FPS), "-vf", vf,
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         str(out)], f"extract {i}")


def conform_graphic(i, src: Path, out: Path):
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(src), "-an",
         "-r", str(FPS), "-vf", f"scale={W}:{H}",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         str(out)], f"conform {i}")


def main():
    clip_paths = []
    for i, (kind, s_in, s_out, gfile, label, _tt, _xf, focal) in enumerate(SHOTS):
        out = CLIPS / f"{i:02d}_{label}.mp4"
        if kind == "footage":
            extract_footage(i, s_in, s_out, focal, out)
        else:
            conform_graphic(i, gfile, out)
        clip_paths.append(out)
        print(f"  {i:02d} {label:<14} {kind:<8} {probe_dur(out):.2f}s"
              f"{'  zoom->' + str(focal[2]) if focal else ''}")

    n = len(clip_paths)
    inputs = []
    for p in clip_paths:
        inputs += ["-i", str(p)]

    filt = []
    cur = "0:v"
    running = probe_dur(clip_paths[0])
    for i in range(1, n):
        ttype = SHOTS[i][5]
        xf = SHOTS[i][6]
        d_i = probe_dur(clip_paths[i])
        offset = running - xf
        nxt = f"x{i}"
        filt.append(f"[{cur}][{i}:v]xfade=transition={ttype}:duration={xf}:offset={offset:.3f}[{nxt}]")
        cur = nxt
        running = offset + d_i

    filter_complex = ";".join(filt)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filter_complex,
         "-map", f"[{cur}]", "-r", str(FPS), "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", str(OUT)], "crossfade chain")

    real = probe_dur(OUT)
    print(f"\nbase video: {real:.2f}s (planned {running:.2f}s) -> {OUT}")
    if real > 30.0:
        print(f"WARNING: {real:.2f}s exceeds the 30s cap")

    starts, cum = [], 0.0
    for i, (kind, s_in, s_out, gfile, label, ttype, xf, focal) in enumerate(SHOTS):
        cum -= xf
        starts.append({"label": label, "start": round(cum, 3)})
        d = probe_dur(clip_paths[i])
        cum += d
    (EDIT / "shot_starts.json").write_text(json.dumps(starts, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {EDIT / 'shot_starts.json'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Step 1: cut the screen recording's juiciest moments, drop in the five
Remotion graphic cards, and crossfade the whole thing into one silent
1920x1080/60fps base video.

Revision 2 -- fixes from first-cut feedback:
  - fewer, LONGER footage holds (cut the three <=0.6s "flash" clips
    entirely -- they were the main source of the choppy/cut-off feeling,
    not worth the screen time they cost)
  - every footage clip now gets a slow Ken-Burns push toward a focal point
    instead of sitting static
  - transitions vary by context instead of one flat crossfade: quick
    same-mode footage cuts dissolve, section boundaries (footage<->
    graphic) fade through black for a more cinematic beat, and the two
    graphic-to-graphic cuts (support->outro) use a plain fade

Footage audio is real digital silence (measured -91dB across the whole
127s source) so it is dropped entirely here -- audio is built from scratch
in build_audio.py and only meets the picture at the final mux.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = EDIT.parent / "footage" / "nxeonscreen.mp4"
GFX = EDIT / "graphics"
CLIPS = EDIT / "clips"
CLIPS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
OUT = EDIT / "base_video.mp4"

FPS = 60
W, H = 1920, 1080

# (kind, src_in, src_out, file, label, transition_in, xfade_dur, focal)
# focal = (fx, fy, zoom_end) as fraction-of-frame focal point + end zoom
# factor for a slow Ken-Burns push; None for graphics (they animate
# themselves) and for the two hero shots long enough to hold static.
SHOTS = [
    ("footage", 1.00, 2.60, None, "hero", None, 0.00, (0.72, 0.35, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 10.00, 11.20, None, "build_way", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.50, 0.45, 1.06)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "poster_grid_games.mp4", "poster_games", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 16.60, 17.90, None, "plan_a", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.42, 0.40, 1.07)),
    ("footage", 20.20, 21.50, None, "plan_b", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.35, 0.55, 1.06)),
    ("footage", 27.00, 30.00, None, "globe", "dissolve", 0.18, (0.50, 0.45, 1.10)),
    ("footage", 34.00, 34.90, None, "payment", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.50, 0.40, 1.06)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "discount_reveal.mp4", "discount", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 68.20, 69.30, None, "deploy_mid", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.30, 0.35, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 72.00, 73.50, None, "deploy_live", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.30, 0.30, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 80.00, 81.30, None, "dash_a", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.42, 0.42, 1.07)),
    ("footage", 84.60, 85.90, None, "dash_b", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.60, 0.35, 1.07)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "poster_grid_mods.mp4", "poster_mods", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 104.00, 105.10, None, "config", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.35, 0.50, 1.07)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "support_card.mp4", "support", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "outro_cta.mp4", "outro", "fade", 0.22, None),
]


def run(cmd, label):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {label}")
        print(" ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:500])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_dur(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def zoom_filter(dur: float, fx: float, fy: float, zoom_end: float) -> str:
    """Slow Ken-Burns push toward (fx,fy) (fractions of frame), reaching
    zoom_end by the end of the clip. Crop a shrinking window centred on the
    focal point then scale back up -- reliable in plain ffmpeg, no zoompan
    per-frame quirks."""
    z = f"(1+({zoom_end}-1)*t/{dur})"
    w = f"(1920/{z})"
    h = f"(1080/{z})"
    x = f"max(0,min({fx}*1920-({w})/2,1920-({w})))"
    y = f"max(0,min({fy}*1080-({h})/2,1080-({h})))"
    return f"crop=w='{w}':h='{h}':x='{x}':y='{y}',scale={W}:{H}"


def extract_footage(i, s_in, s_out, focal, out: Path):
    dur = s_out - s_in
    vf = f"scale={W}:{H}"
    if focal is not None:
        fx, fy, zoom_end = focal
        vf = zoom_filter(dur, fx, fy, zoom_end)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{s_in}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", str(SRC),
         "-an", "-r", str(FPS), "-vf", vf,
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         str(out)], f"extract {i}")


def conform_graphic(i, src: Path, out: Path):
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(src), "-an",
         "-r", str(FPS), "-vf", f"scale={W}:{H}",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         str(out)], f"conform {i}")


def main():
    clip_paths = []
    for i, (kind, s_in, s_out, gfile, label, _tt, _xf, focal) in enumerate(SHOTS):
        out = CLIPS / f"{i:02d}_{label}.mp4"
        if kind == "footage":
            extract_footage(i, s_in, s_out, focal, out)
        else:
            conform_graphic(i, gfile, out)
        clip_paths.append(out)
        print(f"  {i:02d} {label:<14} {kind:<8} {probe_dur(out):.2f}s"
              f"{'  zoom->' + str(focal[2]) if focal else ''}")

    n = len(clip_paths)
    inputs = []
    for p in clip_paths:
        inputs += ["-i", str(p)]

    filt = []
    cur = "0:v"
    running = probe_dur(clip_paths[0])
    for i in range(1, n):
        ttype = SHOTS[i][5]
        xf = SHOTS[i][6]
        d_i = probe_dur(clip_paths[i])
        offset = running - xf
        nxt = f"x{i}"
        filt.append(f"[{cur}][{i}:v]xfade=transition={ttype}:duration={xf}:offset={offset:.3f}[{nxt}]")
        cur = nxt
        running = offset + d_i

    filter_complex = ";".join(filt)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filter_complex,
         "-map", f"[{cur}]", "-r", str(FPS), "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", str(OUT)], "crossfade chain")

    real = probe_dur(OUT)
    print(f"\nbase video: {real:.2f}s (planned {running:.2f}s) -> {OUT}")
    if real > 30.0:
        print(f"WARNING: {real:.2f}s exceeds the 30s cap")

    starts, cum = [], 0.0
    for i, (kind, s_in, s_out, gfile, label, ttype, xf, focal) in enumerate(SHOTS):
        cum -= xf
        starts.append({"label": label, "start": round(cum, 3)})
        d = probe_dur(clip_paths[i])
        cum += d
    (EDIT / "shot_starts.json").write_text(json.dumps(starts, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {EDIT / 'shot_starts.json'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    same-mode footage cuts dissolve, section boundaries (footage<->
    graphic) fade through black for a more cinematic beat, and the two
    graphic-to-graphic cuts (support->outro) use a plain fade

Footage audio is real digital silence (measured -91dB across the whole
127s source) so it is dropped entirely here -- audio is built from scratch
in build_audio.py and only meets the picture at the final mux.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = EDIT.parent / "footage" / "nxeonscreen.mp4"
GFX = EDIT / "graphics"
CLIPS = EDIT / "clips"
CLIPS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
OUT = EDIT / "base_video.mp4"

FPS = 60
W, H = 1920, 1080

# (kind, src_in, src_out, file, label, transition_in, xfade_dur, focal)
# focal = (fx, fy, zoom_end) as fraction-of-frame focal point + end zoom
# factor for a slow Ken-Burns push; None for graphics (they animate
# themselves) and for the two hero shots long enough to hold static.
SHOTS = [
    ("footage", 1.00, 2.60, None, "hero", None, 0.00, (0.72, 0.35, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 10.00, 11.20, None, "build_way", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.50, 0.45, 1.06)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "poster_grid_games.mp4", "poster_games", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 16.60, 17.90, None, "plan_a", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.42, 0.40, 1.07)),
    ("footage", 20.20, 21.50, None, "plan_b", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.35, 0.55, 1.06)),
    ("footage", 27.00, 30.00, None, "globe", "dissolve", 0.18, (0.50, 0.45, 1.10)),
    ("footage", 34.00, 34.90, None, "payment", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.50, 0.40, 1.06)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "discount_reveal.mp4", "discount", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 68.20, 69.30, None, "deploy_mid", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.30, 0.35, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 72.00, 73.50, None, "deploy_live", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.30, 0.30, 1.08)),
    ("footage", 80.00, 81.30, None, "dash_a", "dissolve", 0.15, (0.42, 0.42, 1.07)),
    ("footage", 84.60, 85.90, None, "dash_b", "dissolve", 0.12, (0.60, 0.35, 1.07)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "poster_grid_mods.mp4", "poster_mods", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("footage", 104.00, 105.10, None, "config", "fadeblack", 0.20, (0.35, 0.50, 1.07)),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "support_card.mp4", "support", "fadeblack", 0.20, None),
    ("graphic", None, None, GFX / "outro_cta.mp4", "outro", "fade", 0.22, None),
]


def run(cmd, label):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {label}")
        print(" ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:500])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_dur(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


def zoom_filter(dur: float, fx: float, fy: float, zoom_end: float) -> str:
    """Slow Ken-Burns push toward (fx,fy) (fractions of frame), reaching
    zoom_end by the end of the clip. Crop a shrinking window centred on the
    focal point then scale back up -- reliable in plain ffmpeg, no zoompan
    per-frame quirks."""
    z = f"(1+({zoom_end}-1)*t/{dur})"
    w = f"(1920/{z})"
    h = f"(1080/{z})"
    x = f"max(0,min({fx}*1920-({w})/2,1920-({w})))"
    y = f"max(0,min({fy}*1080-({h})/2,1080-({h})))"
    return f"crop=w='{w}':h='{h}':x='{x}':y='{y}':eval=frame,scale={W}:{H}"


def extract_footage(i, s_in, s_out, focal, out: Path):
    dur = s_out - s_in
    vf = f"scale={W}:{H}"
    if focal is not None:
        fx, fy, zoom_end = focal
        vf = zoom_filter(dur, fx, fy, zoom_end)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{s_in}", "-t", f"{dur}", "-i", str(SRC),
         "-an", "-r", str(FPS), "-vf", vf,
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         str(out)], f"extract {i}")


def conform_graphic(i, src: Path, out: Path):
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(src), "-an",
         "-r", str(FPS), "-vf", f"scale={W}:{H}",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         str(out)], f"conform {i}")


def main():
    clip_paths = []
    for i, (kind, s_in, s_out, gfile, label, _tt, _xf, focal) in enumerate(SHOTS):
        out = CLIPS / f"{i:02d}_{label}.mp4"
        if kind == "footage":
            extract_footage(i, s_in, s_out, focal, out)
        else:
            conform_graphic(i, gfile, out)
        clip_paths.append(out)
        print(f"  {i:02d} {label:<14} {kind:<8} {probe_dur(out):.2f}s"
              f"{'  zoom->' + str(focal[2]) if focal else ''}")

    n = len(clip_paths)
    inputs = []
    for p in clip_paths:
        inputs += ["-i", str(p)]

    filt = []
    cur = "0:v"
    running = probe_dur(clip_paths[0])
    for i in range(1, n):
        ttype = SHOTS[i][5]
        xf = SHOTS[i][6]
        d_i = probe_dur(clip_paths[i])
        offset = running - xf
        nxt = f"x{i}"
        filt.append(f"[{cur}][{i}:v]xfade=transition={ttype}:duration={xf}:offset={offset:.3f}[{nxt}]")
        cur = nxt
        running = offset + d_i

    filter_complex = ";".join(filt)
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filter_complex,
         "-map", f"[{cur}]", "-r", str(FPS), "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "16", str(OUT)], "crossfade chain")

    real = probe_dur(OUT)
    print(f"\nbase video: {real:.2f}s (planned {running:.2f}s) -> {OUT}")
    if real > 30.0:
        print(f"WARNING: {real:.2f}s exceeds the 30s cap")

    starts, cum = [], 0.0
    for i, (kind, s_in, s_out, gfile, label, ttype, xf, focal) in enumerate(SHOTS):
        cum -= xf
        starts.append({"label": label, "start": round(cum, 3)})
        d = probe_dur(clip_paths[i])
        cum += d
    (EDIT / "shot_starts.json").write_text(json.dumps(starts, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {EDIT / 'shot_starts.json'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Build the 4 transparent HyperFrames text overlays that sit on top of the live screen-recording footage (the poster/discount/mod/support/outro cards are full-frame Remotion scenes and need no overlay -- these four are for the in-between footage beats where the real product UI is doing the talking and we just add a short callout). import os, json
from PIL import Image

src_root = 'assets/Mod covers/logos'
dst = 'edit/remotion/public/mods'
manifest = []
i = 0
for game in sorted(os.listdir(src_root)):
    gdir = os.path.join(src_root, game)
    if not os.path.isdir(gdir):
        continue
    for f in sorted(os.listdir(gdir)):
        path = os.path.join(gdir, f)
        try:
            im = Image.open(path)
            im.seek(0)
            im = im.convert('RGBA')
        except Exception as e:
            print('ERROR', path, e)
            continue
        out_name = f'm{i:02d}.png'
        im.save(os.path.join(dst, out_name))
        manifest.append(out_name)
        i += 1
print(len(manifest), 'mod logos converted')
print(json.dumps(manifest))
"

1	---
2	name: baz
3	description: Create professional motion graphics and videos from the terminal. AI-powered composition with multi-track layering, choreography, voiceovers, and Lambda rendering. Gated 5-phase workflow ensures quality.
4	metadata:
5	  openclaw:
6	    requires:
7	      bins:
8	        - node
9	        - baz
10	    primaryEnv: BAZ_API_KEY
11	    envVars:
12	      - name: BAZ_API_KEY
13	        required: false
14	        description: Optional API key override. The CLI can also use its saved config or register a new account.
15	    install:
16	      - id: node
17	        kind: node
18	        package: bazaar.it
19	        bins:
20	          - baz
21	        label: Install Bazaar CLI (npm)
22	    homepage: https://baz.studio
23	    emoji: "\U0001F3AC"
24	---
25	
26	# baz CLI — Mandatory Video Generation Workflow
27	
28	Use this skill when the user wants to create, edit, or export videos using the Bazaar CLI (`baz`).
29	
30	**This is a GATED workflow.** You MUST complete each phase in order. Do NOT skip phases. Do NOT declare "done" until the completion checklist at the bottom passes.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Getting Started (New Agents)
35	
36	Install the published CLI first. Then register without opening the web app:
37	
38	```bash
39	# 1. Discover what Bazaar can do.
40	curl https://baz.studio/api/v1/capabilities
41	
42	# 2. Install the CLI and create an account. The CLI stores the API key.
43	npm install -g bazaar.it@latest
44	baz auth register --email <account-email> --name "My Agent"
45	
46	# 3. Switch to compact machine output and install public video skills.
47	export BAZ_AGENT=1
48	baz agent init --skills all-free --agent auto
49	
50	# 4. Check live balance and pricing.
51	baz balance --pricing --json
52	```
53	
54	**Balance starts at $0.** Run `baz balance topup 5` to get the minimum $5 Stripe checkout URL. A human must approve that payment. After checkout, run `baz balance --json` and retry the same command. Use `baz prompt --budget <dollars>` only when the user explicitly asks for a cap. A low cap is a stop condition and can create a partial video.
55	
56	**Shortcut:** If your human creates an account at baz.studio, ask them to provide an API key, then run `baz auth login <your-api-key>` instead of registering. New accounts start at $0 — fund via the top-up flow above before the first paid operation.
57	
58	Already have an API key? Skip to Phase 1.
59	
60	### One-line cold-agent requests
61	
62	When the user gives only a request such as `make a launch video for X`, do not stop to ask for creative preferences that can be inferred safely.
63	
64	1. Identify `X` from the user's text and any public URL they supplied.
65	2. Default to a 15-second landscape product launch video unless the request implies another format or duration.
66	3. State the assumptions in the run context. Infer a restrained brand system when no assets or brand rules are available.
67	4. Add one `goal`, one `requirement`, one `brand`, and one `instructions` context entry before generation.
68	5. Run the normal generate, preview, review, validate, repair, and export gates below.
69	6. Ask the user only when identity, rights, payment, or a destructive action needs human authority.
70	
71	The one-line request reduces user input. It does not remove the quality gates.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## When to Use
76	
77	- User asks to create, edit, or export videos via CLI
78	- User wants to automate video generation
79	- User mentions "baz", "bazaar CLI", or "video generation from terminal"
80	
81	## Report CLI Feedback
82	
83	Submit one feedback item when baz behavior differs from its documented contract, an error gives no actionable recovery, or a required capability is missing:
84	
85	```bash
86	baz feedback "Expected timing to remain unchanged, but the scene moved" \
87	  --kind unexpected-behavior \
88	  --command "baz scenes set-code <scene-id> --file ./scene.tsx"
89	```
90	
91	Use `--kind bug`, `friction`, `unexpected-behavior`, `missing-capability`, `docs`, or `idea`. Do not include API keys, credentials, private file contents, or other secrets. The command sends the explicit message, feedback category, displayed command, CLI version, agent type, and active project ID to the baz.studio team. Do not submit expected validation failures or duplicate feedback.
92	
93	## When to Use `baz prompt` vs Spar
94	
95	- **Direct `baz prompt`** — Scene creation, edits, full agent orchestration
96	- **`baz prompt --spar`** — Planning-only conversation (no timeline mutations)
97	
98	### Trend-to-Skill Factory Override
99	
100	When `.agents/skills/trend-to-skill/SKILL.md` is active, never use `baz prompt` or prompt-driven repair, even for brand-new scenes. Codex or Claude must author the TSX locally, create scenes with `baz scenes create --file ...`, and repair them with `baz scenes set-code`. In that workflow, Bazaar is the persistence/review/export control plane, not the code generator.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Phase 1: Context (REQUIRED — do NOT skip)
105	
106	You MUST set project context BEFORE generating any scenes. This gives the composition agent the information it needs to produce correct output on the first try.
107	
108	### Minimum context required:
109	1. **Goal** — What is this video for? Who is the audience? What should they feel/do?
110	2. **Requirements** — Specific, verifiable things the video must contain
111	3. **Brand** — Colors, fonts, logo placement, visual style
112	4. **Director's treatment** — The non-generic creative idea: core metaphor, point of view, pacing shape, visual grammar, and anti-patterns
113	
114	**Shippable quality warning:** "World-class", "premium", "Bloomberg-grade", "cinematic", "editorial", and "not generic" are aspirations, not direction. Do not rely on those words as the prompt. Convert them into a concrete treatment first:
115	
116	- **Core metaphor:** receipt, dossier, pressure gauge, courtroom exhibit, operating-room monitor, teardown, map, timeline, market microstructure, etc.
117	- **Point of view:** the one sentence the video argues, not just the topic it covers.
118	- **Visual grammar:** what kinds of frames repeat, how data is represented, what is deliberately avoided.
119	- **Pacing shape:** where tension rises, where proof lands, where the ending resolves.
120	- **Anti-patterns:** generic KPI cards, interchangeable stock chart panels, decorative data, one-track slideshow pacing, vague finance filler.
121	
122	**Parallel sessions:** If multiple agents share the same machine, do NOT use `baz project use` — it writes to a shared config file and agents will stomp each other. Instead, set the env var for your session:
123	```bash
124	export BAZ_PROJECT_ID=<id>   # Session-scoped, no file contention
125	```
126	
127	```bash
128	# Create or select project
129	baz project create --name "Descriptive Name - Date/Purpose" --json
130	# OR (single-agent only — see parallel sessions note above)
131	baz project use <id>
132	
133	# Set goal (be specific — audience, purpose, desired outcome)
134	baz context add "Create 45-60 second feature announcement for [Product]. \
135	Audience: [who]. Key value: [what they get]." --label "goal"
136	
137	# Add requirements (each one should be independently verifiable)
138	baz context add "Show [specific feature interaction]" --label "requirement"
139	baz context add "Include CTA: '[specific text]'" --label "requirement"
140	baz context add "Total duration: [range]" --label "requirement"
141	
142	# Set brand guidelines
143	baz context add "Brand: [Name]. Primary [hex], accent [hex]. Font: [name]. \
144	[Logo placement]. [Visual style notes]." --label "brand"
145	
146	baz context add "DIRECTOR TREATMENT: [specific visual thesis]. \
147	Core metaphor: [not a style adjective]. Point of view: [argument]. \
148	Visual grammar: [repeatable frame system]. Pacing: [tension/proof/resolution]. \
149	Avoid: generic KPI cards, interchangeable chart panels, decorative data." --label "instructions"
150	```
151	
152	### Verify context is set:
153	```bash
154	baz context list --json
155	```
156	
157	**Gate:** Do NOT proceed to Phase 2 until `baz context list` shows at least one goal, one requirement, one brand entry, and one director-treatment/instructions entry.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Phase 2: Generate
162	
163	Now prompt the agent to create scenes. You can use one big prompt or multiple scene-by-scene prompts.
164	
165	```bash
166	# Option A: One comprehensive prompt
167	baz prompt "Create a video with: [scene 1 description], [scene 2], ..." --stream-json
168	
169	# Option B: Scene-by-scene (more control)
170	baz prompt "Scene 1 (5s): Dark gradient intro, logo top-left, title slides up" --stream-json
171	baz prompt "Scene 2 (7s): Problem statement with mock UI..." --stream-json
172	baz prompt "Scene 3 (18s): Feature walkthrough..." --stream-json
173	```
174	
175	Tips:
176	- Include duration in each prompt
177	- Be specific about animations, colors, layout
178	- Reference brand context set in Phase 1
179	
180	### Choreography (REQUIRED for 3+ scene videos)
181	
182	For videos with 3 or more scenes, plan choreography BEFORE generating. This prevents the "lockstep slideshow" pattern where all layers swap at the same frame boundary.
183	
184	#### Actor Planning Template
185	
186	Before prompting, plan your actors:
187	
188	| Actor | Track | Lifetime | Role |
189	|-------|-------|----------|------|
190	| Background | 0 | Full duration | Evolving gradient, particles |
191	| Hero | 1 | 60-80% | Main UI, enters, demotes to corner, returns |
192	| Supporting | 1-2 | 20-40% | Cards/charts, appear during hero demotion |
193	| Text | 2+ | 10-30% | Headlines, arrive at beat points, explicit exits |
194	
195	#### 5 Prompt Enrichment Rules
196	
197	1. **Every content prompt includes exit instructions** (exempt: persistent backgrounds, final CTA)
198	2. **Prefer ONE background** on Track 0 for the full video duration
199	3. **Every overlay prompt includes position and size** — scenes that share screen time must not share screen space
200	4. **Specify spring animation** for hero elements (`spring() for hero entrance`)
201	5. **Include energy level hints** in prompts ("high energy entrance", "calm sustained section")
202	
203	#### Landscape Occupancy Rule (REQUIRED for 16:9)
204	
205	If the project is landscape, do not let the scene collapse into a small claim floating in a giant matte.
206	
207	- Main proof beats should usually use roughly `60-80%` of the frame width, or resolve as a deliberate two-zone composition
208	- Prefer wide proof rails, claim-left / proof-right layouts, split fields, and full-width chart bands
209	- Tiny centered headlines, short decorative lines, or small chart islands are only acceptable as very brief punctuation beats
210	- If a landscape frame feels empty, fix scale and composition first before adding more text
211	
212	#### GOOD Example — context injection + one natural prompt:
213	```bash
214	baz context add "CHOREOGRAPHY: Every overlay scene must specify its position and size. \
215	  Use spring() for hero elements. Every non-final scene must have exit animations. \
216	  Prefer one continuous background. In landscape, main proof beats should occupy roughly 60-80% of width or resolve as a wide split-field layout — avoid tiny centered claim clusters." --label "instructions"
217	
218	baz prompt "Create a 15-second product demo: dark theme intro with logo, \
219	  feature showcase with 3 cards, area chart showing growth, and a CTA. \
220	  Brand: #6366f1 purple, #10b981 green, Inter font." --stream-json
221	```
222	
223	ONE natural prompt. The composition agent handles decomposition into tracks + spatial layout internally based on choreography context.
224	
225	---
226	
227	## Phase 3: Preview, Review & Validate (REQUIRED — NEVER skip)
228	
229	After generation, you MUST visually inspect the output and run structural validation. This is not optional.
230	
231	### Step 1: Preview
232	```bash
233	baz preview --frames 0,150,300 --json
234	```
235	
236	Use preview for visual and semantic checks:
237	- Is the logo actually visible?
238	- Is the CTA on screen?
239	- Does the style feel on-brand?
240	- Are screenshots being used as reference/recreated UI or charts instead of raw webpage collage?
241	- Are self-claims attributed with small source labels/footers rather than ugly headline copy like "Ramp says..."?
242	- What is the specific visual thesis only this video has?
243	- Could these scenes be reused for any other topic with only text swaps? If yes, fail it.
244	- Are charts and diagrams semantically tied to the story, or just decorative finance motion?
245	- Does the reel feel directed, with a shape and point of view, or like a one-prompt AI slideshow?
246	
247	**Do not accept generic AI slop.** A video can pass validation and still be a 4/10. If the preview reads as generic KPI cards, stock editorial styling, or interchangeable finance graphics, mark it unshippable and return to Phase 1/2 with a stronger treatment. Do not declare done.
248	
249	**Do not accept static infographics.** A still dashboard frame with one glowing line, one receipt/card, and small labels is not a motion-graphics video. Audio timing, word anchors, and a compiled export do not make it shippable. If most preview frames show the same layout with only tiny changes, fail the video as 0-3/10. Require visible choreography: changing composition, object transformations, depth, camera/scale moves, foreground/background interaction, kinetic evidence reveals, and meaningful motion throughout the run.
250	
251	### Step 2: Review
252	```bash
253	baz review --summary --json
254	```
255	
256	Read the project summary. Compare scenes, timing, and context against what Phase 1 asked for.
257	
258	### Step 3: Validate
259	```bash
260	baz project validate --json
261	```
262	
263	This is the authoritative machine check for compilation errors, invalid durations, overlaps, and other structural issues.
264	
265	### Optional: Deterministic Verify
266	```bash
267	baz verify --criteria "duration <= 60s,scenes >= 5,portrait" --json
268	```
269	
270	`baz verify` is now only for deterministic checks like duration, scene count, and format. Do NOT use it for visual/content/style questions.
271	
272	**Gate:** If preview/review reveal problems, or `baz project validate` returns errors, or deterministic `baz verify` fails, you MUST proceed to Phase 4. Do NOT export. Do NOT declare done.
273	
274	---
275	
276	## Phase 4: Iterate (REQUIRED if Phase 3 fails)
277	
278	Fix the issues. Then re-preview, re-review, and re-validate.
279	
280	```
281	LOOP:
282	  1. Read the visual/content/structural issues from Phase 3
283	  2. Fix with: baz prompt "Fix: [specific issue]" --stream-json
284	  3. Re-run: baz preview --frames 0,150,300 --json
285	  4. Re-run: baz review --summary --json
286	  5. Re-run: baz project validate --json
287	  6. Optional: baz verify --criteria "duration <= 60s,scenes >= 5,portrait" --json
288	  7. If issues remain → GOTO 1
289	  8. If clean enough → proceed to Phase 5
290	```
291	
292	Do NOT exit this loop until the video looks right and structural validation passes.
293	
294	### Deterministic Edits (skip the AI, save tokens)
295	
296	When you know exactly what code change to make — fixing a color, adjusting timing, replacing text, swapping an emoji for an SVG — use `set-code` instead of `baz prompt`. This bypasses the AI agent entirely: you write the code, CLI pushes it to the server. No tokens spent, no prompt randomness.
297	
298	```bash
299	# 1. Read current scene code
300	baz scenes code <scene-id> --output /tmp/scene.tsx
301	
302	# 2. Edit the file locally (your edits, deterministic)
303	
304	# 3. Push it back
305	baz scenes set-code <scene-id> --file /tmp/scene.tsx
306	```
307	
308	**When to use `set-code` vs `baz prompt`:**
309	- `set-code` — You can see the exact code change needed (wrong color, broken animation, timing fix, text update)
310	- `baz prompt` — You need the AI to design something new or make a creative decision
311	
312	After a batch of edits, run `baz review --json` to sanity-check the composition before asking the user.
313	
314	---
315	
316	## Phase 5: Export (only if requested)
317	
318	Only export if the user explicitly asked for a rendered video AND Phase 3/4 passed.
319	
320	```bash
321	baz export start --wait --json
322	```
323	
324	---
325	
326	## Command Quick Reference
327	
328	| Command | Purpose |
329	|---------|---------|
330	| `baz project create --name "..." --json` | Create new project |
331	| `baz project use <id>` | Set active project (single-agent only) |
332	| `export BAZ_PROJECT_ID=<id>` | Set active project (parallel-safe) |

342	| `baz verify --criteria "..." --json` | Optional deterministic checks only |

347	| `baz scenes positions --updates-json '...' --apply` | Apply timeline position changes |
348	| `baz export start --wait --json` | Render final video |

352	| Category | Action |
353	|----------|--------|
354	| `transient` | Retry with backoff (wait `retry_after` seconds) |
355	| `validation` | Fix input, do not retry same request |
356	| `auth` | Check API key with `baz auth status` |
357	| `fatal` | Stop and report to user |

360	
361	## Completion Checklist
362	
363	You are NOT done until ALL of these are true:
364	
365	- [ ] Phase 1: `baz context list` shows goal + requirements + brand + director treatment/instructions
366	- [ ] Phase 2: Scenes generated via `baz prompt`, except trend-to-skill factory runs, which require manual TSX via `baz scenes create`
367	- [ ] Phase 3: `baz preview --frames ...`, `baz review --summary --json`, and `baz project validate --json` run
368	- [ ] Phase 4: No blocking structural errors remain; optional deterministic `baz verify` passes if used
369	- [ ] Phase 5: Export started (only if user requested it)
370	- [ ] Visual quality: no raw screenshot filler, no random color palette, no attribution legalese in hero/body copy

---
name: baz
description: Create professional motion graphics and videos from the terminal. AI-powered composition with multi-track layering, choreography, voiceovers, and Lambda rendering. Gated 5-phase workflow ensures quality.
metadata:
  openclaw:
    requires:
      bins:
        - node
        - baz
    primaryEnv: BAZ_API_KEY
    envVars:

    install:
      - id: node
        kind: node
        package: bazaar.it
        bins:
          - baz
        label: Install Bazaar CLI (npm)
    homepage: https://baz.studio
    emoji: "\U0001F3AC"
---

# baz CLI — Mandatory Video Generation Workflow

Use this skill when the user wants to create, edit, or export videos using the Bazaar CLI (`baz`).

**This is a GATED workflow.** You MUST complete each phase in order. Do NOT skip phases. Do NOT declare "done" until the completion checklist at the bottom passes.

---

## Getting Started (New Agents)

Install the published CLI first. Then register without opening the web app:

```bash
# 1. Discover what Bazaar can do.
curl https://baz.studio/api/v1/capabilities

# 2. Install the CLI and create an account. The CLI stores the API key.
npm install -g bazaar.it@latest
baz auth register --email <account-email> --name "My Agent"

# 3. Switch to compact machine output and install public video skills.
export BAZ_AGENT=1
baz agent init --skills all-free --agent auto

# 4. Check live balance and pricing.
baz balance --pricing --json
```

**Balance starts at $0.** Run `baz balance topup 5` to get the minimum $5 Stripe checkout URL. A human must approve that payment. After checkout, run `baz balance --json` and retry the same command. Use `baz prompt --budget <dollars>` only when the user explicitly asks for a cap. A low cap is a stop condition and can create a partial video.

**Shortcut:** If your human creates an account at baz.studio, ask them to provide an API key, then run `baz auth login <your-api-key>` instead of registering. New accounts start at $0 — fund via the top-up flow above before the first paid operation.

Already have an API key? Skip to Phase 1.

### One-line cold-agent requests

When the user gives only a request such as `make a launch video for X`, do not stop to ask for creative preferences that can be inferred safely.

1. Identify `X` from the user's text and any public URL they supplied.
2. Default to a 15-second landscape product launch video unless the request implies another format or duration.
3. State the assumptions in the run context. Infer a restrained brand system when no assets or brand rules are available.
4. Add one `goal`, one `requirement`, one `brand`, and one `instructions` context entry before generation.
5. Run the normal generate, preview, review, validate, repair, and export gates below.
6. Ask the user only when identity, rights, payment, or a destructive action needs human authority.

The one-line request reduces user input. It does not remove the quality gates.

---

## When to Use

- User asks to create, edit, or export videos via CLI
- User wants to automate video generation
- User mentions "baz", "bazaar CLI", or "video generation from terminal"

## Report CLI Feedback

Submit one feedback item when baz behavior differs from its documented contract, an error gives no actionable recovery, or a required capability is missing:

```bash
baz feedback "Expected timing to remain unchanged, but the scene moved" \
  --kind unexpected-behavior \
  --command "baz scenes set-code <scene-id> --file ./scene.tsx"
```

Use `--kind bug`, `friction`, `unexpected-behavior`, `missing-capability`, `docs`, or `idea`. Do not include API keys, credentials, private file contents, or other secrets. The command sends the explicit message, feedback category, displayed command, CLI version, agent type, and active project ID to the baz.studio team. Do not submit expected validation failures or duplicate feedback.

## When to Use `baz prompt` vs Spar

- **Direct `baz prompt`** — Scene creation, edits, full agent orchestration
- **`baz prompt --spar`** — Planning-only conversation (no timeline mutations)

### Trend-to-Skill Factory Override

When `.agents/skills/trend-to-skill/SKILL.md` is active, never use `baz prompt` or prompt-driven repair, even for brand-new scenes. Codex or Claude must author the TSX locally, create scenes with `baz scenes create --file ...`, and repair them with `baz scenes set-code`. In that workflow, Bazaar is the persistence/review/export control plane, not the code generator.

---

## Phase 1: Context (REQUIRED — do NOT skip)

You MUST set project context BEFORE generating any scenes. This gives the composition agent the information it needs to produce correct output on the first try.

### Minimum context required:
1. **Goal** — What is this video for? Who is the audience? What should they feel/do?
2. **Requirements** — Specific, verifiable things the video must contain
3. **Brand** — Colors, fonts, logo placement, visual style
4. **Director's treatment** — The non-generic creative idea: core metaphor, point of view, pacing shape, visual grammar, and anti-patterns

**Shippable quality warning:** "World-class", "premium", "Bloomberg-grade", "cinematic", "editorial", and "not generic" are aspirations, not direction. Do not rely on those words as the prompt. Convert them into a concrete treatment first:

- **Core metaphor:** receipt, dossier, pressure gauge, courtroom exhibit, operating-room monitor, teardown, map, timeline, market microstructure, etc.
- **Point of view:** the one sentence the video argues, not just the topic it covers.
- **Visual grammar:** what kinds of frames repeat, how data is represented, what is deliberately avoided.
- **Pacing shape:** where tension rises, where proof lands, where the ending resolves.
- **Anti-patterns:** generic KPI cards, interchangeable stock chart panels, decorative data, one-track slideshow pacing, vague finance filler.

**Parallel sessions:** If multiple agents share the same machine, do NOT use `baz project use` — it writes to a shared config file and agents will stomp each other. Instead, set the env var for your session:
```bash
export BAZ_PROJECT_ID=<id>   # Session-scoped, no file contention
```

```bash
# Create or select project
baz project create --name "Descriptive Name - Date/Purpose" --json
# OR (single-agent only — see parallel sessions note above)
baz project use <id>

# Set goal (be specific — audience, purpose, desired outcome)
baz context add "Create 45-60 second feature announcement for [Product]. \
Audience: [who]. Key value: [what they get]." --label "goal"

# Add requirements (each one should be independently verifiable)
baz context add "Show [specific feature interaction]" --label "requirement"
baz context add "Include CTA: '[specific text]'" --label "requirement"
baz context add "Total duration: [range]" --label "requirement"

# Set brand guidelines
baz context add "Brand: [Name]. Primary [hex], accent [hex]. Font: [name]. \
[Logo placement]. [Visual style notes]." --label "brand"

baz context add "DIRECTOR TREATMENT: [specific visual thesis]. \
Core metaphor: [not a style adjective]. Point of view: [argument]. \
Visual grammar: [repeatable frame system]. Pacing: [tension/proof/resolution]. \
Avoid: generic KPI cards, interchangeable chart panels, decorative data." --label "instructions"
```

### Verify context is set:
```bash
baz context list --json
```

**Gate:** Do NOT proceed to Phase 2 until `baz context list` shows at least one goal, one requirement, one brand entry, and one director-treatment/instructions entry.

---

## Phase 2: Generate

Now prompt the agent to create scenes. You can use one big prompt or multiple scene-by-scene prompts.

```bash
# Option A: One comprehensive prompt
baz prompt "Create a video with: [scene 1 description], [scene 2], ..." --stream-json

# Option B: Scene-by-scene (more control)
baz prompt "Scene 1 (5s): Dark gradient intro, logo top-left, title slides up" --stream-json
baz prompt "Scene 2 (7s): Problem statement with mock UI..." --stream-json
baz prompt "Scene 3 (18s): Feature walkthrough..." --stream-json
```

Tips:
- Include duration in each prompt
- Be specific about animations, colors, layout
- Reference brand context set in Phase 1

### Choreography (REQUIRED for 3+ scene videos)

For videos with 3 or more scenes, plan choreography BEFORE generating. This prevents the "lockstep slideshow" pattern where all layers swap at the same frame boundary.

#### Actor Planning Template

Before prompting, plan your actors:

| Actor | Track | Lifetime | Role |
|-------|-------|----------|------|
| Background | 0 | Full duration | Evolving gradient, particles |
| Hero | 1 | 60-80% | Main UI, enters, demotes to corner, returns |
| Supporting | 1-2 | 20-40% | Cards/charts, appear during hero demotion |
| Text | 2+ | 10-30% | Headlines, arrive at beat points, explicit exits |

#### 5 Prompt Enrichment Rules

1. **Every content prompt includes exit instructions** (exempt: persistent backgrounds, final CTA)
2. **Prefer ONE background** on Track 0 for the full video duration
3. **Every overlay prompt includes position and size** — scenes that share screen time must not share screen space
4. **Specify spring animation** for hero elements (`spring() for hero entrance`)
5. **Include energy level hints** in prompts ("high energy entrance", "calm sustained section")

#### Landscape Occupancy Rule (REQUIRED for 16:9)

If the project is landscape, do not let the scene collapse into a small claim floating in a giant matte.

- Main proof beats should usually use roughly `60-80%` of the frame width, or resolve as a deliberate two-zone composition
- Prefer wide proof rails, claim-left / proof-right layouts, split fields, and full-width chart bands
- Tiny centered headlines, short decorative lines, or small chart islands are only acceptable as very brief punctuation beats
- If a landscape frame feels empty, fix scale and composition first before adding more text

#### GOOD Example — context injection + one natural prompt:
```bash
baz context add "CHOREOGRAPHY: Every overlay scene must specify its position and size. \
  Use spring() for hero elements. Every non-final scene must have exit animations. \
  Prefer one continuous background. In landscape, main proof beats should occupy roughly 60-80% of width or resolve as a wide split-field layout — avoid tiny centered claim clusters." --label "instructions"

baz prompt "Create a 15-second product demo: dark theme intro with logo, \
  feature showcase with 3 cards, area chart showing growth, and a CTA. \
  Brand: #6366f1 purple, #10b981 green, Inter font." --stream-json
```

ONE natural prompt. The composition agent handles decomposition into tracks + spatial layout internally based on choreography context.

---

## Phase 3: Preview, Review & Validate (REQUIRED — NEVER skip)

After generation, you MUST visually inspect the output and run structural validation. This is not optional.

### Step 1: Preview
```bash
baz preview --frames 0,150,300 --json
```

Use preview for visual and semantic checks:
- Is the logo actually visible?
- Is the CTA on screen?
- Does the style feel on-brand?
- Are screenshots being used as reference/recreated UI or charts instead of raw webpage collage?
- Are self-claims attributed with small source labels/footers rather than ugly headline copy like "Ramp says..."?
- What is the specific visual thesis only this video has?
- Could these scenes be reused for any other topic with only text swaps? If yes, fail it.
- Are charts and diagrams semantically tied to the story, or just decorative finance motion?
- Does the reel feel directed, with a shape and point of view, or like a one-prompt AI slideshow?

**Do not accept generic AI slop.** A video can pass validation and still be a 4/10. If the preview reads as generic KPI cards, stock editorial styling, or interchangeable finance graphics, mark it unshippable and return to Phase 1/2 with a stronger treatment. Do not declare done.

**Do not accept static infographics.** A still dashboard frame with one glowing line, one receipt/card, and small labels is not a motion-graphics video. Audio timing, word anchors, and a compiled export do not make it shippable. If most preview frames show the same layout with only tiny changes, fail the video as 0-3/10. Require visible choreography: changing composition, object transformations, depth, camera/scale moves, foreground/background interaction, kinetic evidence reveals, and meaningful motion throughout the run.

### Step 2: Review
```bash
baz review --summary --json
```

Read the project summary. Compare scenes, timing, and context against what Phase 1 asked for.

### Step 3: Validate
```bash
baz project validate --json
```

This is the authoritative machine check for compilation errors, invalid durations, overlaps, and other structural issues.

### Optional: Deterministic Verify
```bash
baz verify --criteria "duration <= 60s,scenes >= 5,portrait" --json
```

`baz verify` is now only for deterministic checks like duration, scene count, and format. Do NOT use it for visual/content/style questions.

**Gate:** If preview/review reveal problems, or `baz project validate` returns errors, or deterministic `baz verify` fails, you MUST proceed to Phase 4. Do NOT export. Do NOT declare done.

---

## Phase 4: Iterate (REQUIRED if Phase 3 fails)

Fix the issues. Then re-preview, re-review, and re-validate.

```
LOOP:
  1. Read the visual/content/structural issues from Phase 3
  2. Fix with: baz prompt "Fix: [specific issue]" --stream-json
  3. Re-run: baz preview --frames 0,150,300 --json
  4. Re-run: baz review --summary --json
  5. Re-run: baz project validate --json
  6. Optional: baz verify --criteria "duration <= 60s,scenes >= 5,portrait" --json
  7. If issues remain → GOTO 1
  8. If clean enough → proceed to Phase 5
```

Do NOT exit this loop until the video looks right and structural validation passes.

### Deterministic Edits (skip the AI, save tokens)

When you know exactly what code change to make — fixing a color, adjusting timing, replacing text, swapping an emoji for an SVG — use `set-code` instead of `baz prompt`. This bypasses the AI agent entirely: you write the code, CLI pushes it to the server. No tokens spent, no prompt randomness.

```bash
# 1. Read current scene code
baz scenes code <scene-id> --output /tmp/scene.tsx

# 2. Edit the file locally (your edits, deterministic)

# 3. Push it back
baz scenes set-code <scene-id> --file /tmp/scene.tsx
```

**When to use `set-code` vs `baz prompt`:**
- `set-code` — You can see the exact code change needed (wrong color, broken animation, timing fix, text update)
- `baz prompt` — You need the AI to design something new or make a creative decision

After a batch of edits, run `baz review --json` to sanity-check the composition before asking the user.

---

## Phase 5: Export (only if requested)

Only export if the user explicitly asked for a rendered video AND Phase 3/4 passed.

```bash
baz export start --wait --json
```

---

## Command Quick Reference

| Command | Purpose |

| `baz project create --name "..." --json` | Create new project |
| `baz project use <id>` | Set active project (single-agent only) |
| `export BAZ_PROJECT_ID=<id>` | Set active project (parallel-safe) |

| `baz context add "..." --label "requirement"` | Add verifiable requirement |

| `baz preview --frames 0,150,300 --json` | Render visual spot-check frames |
| `baz review --json` | Get full project state for review |
| `baz project validate --json` | Validate structural timeline health |
| `baz verify --criteria "..." --json` | Optional deterministic checks only |

| `baz scenes code <id> --output file.tsx` | Read scene TSX code to file |
| `baz scenes set-code <id> --file file.tsx` | Replace scene code (deterministic, no AI) |
| `baz scenes positions --updates-json '...'` | Preview timeline position changes (dry-run) |
| `baz scenes positions --updates-json '...' --apply` | Apply timeline position changes |
| `baz export start --wait --json` | Render final video |

## Error Handling

| Category | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `transient` | Retry with backoff (wait `retry_after` seconds) |
| `validation` | Fix input, do not retry same request |
| `auth` | Check API key with `baz auth status` |
| `fatal` | Stop and report to user |

---

## Completion Checklist

You are NOT done until ALL of these are true:

- [ ] Phase 1: `baz context list` shows goal + requirements + brand + director treatment/instructions
- [ ] Phase 2: Scenes generated via `baz prompt`, except trend-to-skill factory runs, which require manual TSX via `baz scenes create`
- [ ] Phase 3: `baz preview --frames ...`, `baz review --summary --json`, and `baz project validate --json` run
- [ ] Phase 4: No blocking structural errors remain; optional deterministic `baz verify` passes if used
- [ ] Phase 5: Export started (only if user requested it)
- [ ] Visual quality: no raw screenshot filler, no random color palette, no attribution legalese in hero/body copy

**If you skipped preview/review/validate, you are not done. Go back and run them.**

---

## External Endpoints

| URL | Method | Data Sent | Purpose |
|-----|--------|-----------|---------|
| `baz.studio/api/v1/capabilities` | GET | None | Discover available tools |

"""Audio pass for the recreated-UI cursor demo (main_demo.mp4).

The old version of this script was built for the screen-recording edit
(whoosh transitions between clips). That architecture is gone -- this is
now one continuous Remotion timeline driven by a synthetic cursor clicking
through the real product flow, so the soundtrack changes to match: a soft
UI "tick" at every cursor click (tactile feedback, like a real product
demo), a success chime at "Your server is live", and a whoosh reserved for
only the two marketing-card transitions at the very end (Support, Outro)
since those are deliberately a different mode from the in-app screens.

Cue points below are computed from the exact Sequence durations/overlaps in
mainDemoStack.ts (dashboard 84/10, choose-game 78/10, size-server 72/10,
region 78/10, payment 90/12, deploy 78/10, live-dashboard 72/10, mods
72/10, config 60/14, support 102/14, outro 96) plus each screen's own
Cursor click frames -- not eyeballed against the render.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SFX = EDIT / "sfx"
SFX.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
VIDEO = EDIT / "main_demo.mp4"
FINAL = EDIT / "final.mp4"

CLICK_FRAMES = [58, 124, 180, 204, 246, 270, 354, 422, 464, 524, 576]
CHIME_FRAME = 396
WHOOSH_FRAMES = [588, 676]
FPS = 30

CLICKS_S = [f / FPS for f in CLICK_FRAMES]
CHIME_S = CHIME_FRAME / FPS
WHOOSH_S = [f / FPS for f in WHOOSH_FRAMES]


def run(cmd, label):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {label}")
        print(" ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:500])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_dur(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


VIDEO_DUR = probe_dur(VIDEO)
print(f"video duration: {VIDEO_DUR:.3f}s ({VIDEO_DUR*FPS:.0f} frames)")


def make_bed(out: Path, dur: float):
    inputs = []
    for freq in (110, 110.6, 164.8):
        inputs += ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"sine=frequency={freq}:duration={dur}"]
    filt = (
        "[0:a][1:a][2:a]amix=inputs=3:weights=1 0.8 0.5:normalize=0,"
        "tremolo=f=0.15:d=0.35,"
        "lowpass=f=900,"
        "volume=0.085[bed]"
    )
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[bed]",
         "-t", f"{dur}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "bed")


def make_click(out: Path):
    """Soft UI tick -- short sine blip with a fast decay, higher pitch so
    it reads as tactile feedback rather than a musical note."""
    dur = 0.09
    filt = (
        f"sine=frequency=980:duration={dur},"
        f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.004,afade=t=out:st=0.02:d={dur-0.02:.3f},"
        f"volume=0.22[click]"
    )
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[click]",
         "-t", f"{dur}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "click")


def make_whoosh(out: Path, dur: float = 0.42):
    filt = (
        f"anoisesrc=color=pink:duration={dur}:amplitude=1,"
        f"bandpass=f=1400:width_type=h:w=1800,"
        f"volume=0.45,"
        f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.05,"
        f"afade=t=out:st={dur-0.22:.3f}:d=0.22"
    )
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", filt,
         "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "whoosh")


def make_chime(out: Path):
    notes = [(523.25, 0.00), (659.25, 0.09), (783.99, 0.18)]
    dur = 0.62
    parts, labels = [], []
    for i, (freq, start) in enumerate(notes):
        lbl = f"n{i}"
        parts.append(
            f"sine=frequency={freq}:duration={dur - start:.3f},"
            f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.01,afade=t=out:st={dur-start-0.28:.3f}:d=0.28,"
            f"adelay={int(start*1000)}|{int(start*1000)}[{lbl}]"
        )
        labels.append(f"[{lbl}]")
    filt = (";".join(parts) +
            f";{''.join(labels)}amix=inputs={len(notes)}:normalize=0,"
            f"volume=0.35,aecho=0.8:0.7:60:0.25[chime]")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[chime]",
         "-t", f"{dur}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "chime")


def mix(out: Path):
    bed = SFX / "bed.wav"
    click = SFX / "click.wav"
    whoosh = SFX / "whoosh.wav"
    chime = SFX / "chime.wav"
    make_bed(bed, VIDEO_DUR)
    make_click(click)
    make_whoosh(whoosh)
    make_chime(chime)

    inputs = ["-i", str(bed)]
    filt_parts = ["[0:a]anull[bed]"]
    labels = ["[bed]"]

    idx = 1
    for i, t in enumerate(CLICKS_S):
        inputs += ["-i", str(click)]
        ms = int(t * 1000)
        filt_parts.append(f"[{idx}:a]adelay={ms}|{ms}[c{i}]")
        labels.append(f"[c{i}]")
        idx += 1

    inputs += ["-i", str(chime)]
    ms = int(CHIME_S * 1000)
    filt_parts.append(f"[{idx}:a]adelay={ms}|{ms}[chime0]")
    labels.append("[chime0]")
    idx += 1

    for i, t in enumerate(WHOOSH_S):
        inputs += ["-i", str(whoosh)]
        ms = int(t * 1000)
        filt_parts.append(f"[{idx}:a]adelay={ms}|{ms}[w{i}]")
        labels.append(f"[w{i}]")
        idx += 1

    filt = ";".join(filt_parts) + f";{''.join(labels)}amix=inputs={len(labels)}:normalize=0[mix]"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", "[mix]", "-t", f"{VIDEO_DUR}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "mix")


def decoded_samples(p: Path) -> int:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-f", "s16le", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "48000", "-"],
                       capture_output=True)
    return len(r.stdout) // 2


def measure(p: Path) -> dict:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-af", "loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11:print_format=json",
                        "-f", "null", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = re.findall(r"\{[^{}]*\"input_i\"[^{}]*\}", r.stderr, re.S)
    return json.loads(m[-1])


def main():
    raw = SFX / "mix_raw.wav"
    mix(raw)

    d = measure(raw)
    print(f"raw mix: I={d['input_i']} LUFS TP={d['input_tp']} dBTP")
    af = (f"loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11:measured_I={d['input_i']}:measured_TP={d['input_tp']}"
          f":measured_LRA={d['input_lra']}:measured_thresh={d['input_thresh']}"
          f":offset={d['target_offset']}:linear=true,aresample=48000")
    normed = SFX / "mix_normed.m4a"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(raw), "-af", af,
         "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(normed)], "loudnorm")

    ref = decoded_samples(raw)
    got = decoded_samples(normed)
    print(f"samples: raw {ref} normed {got} delta {(got-ref)/48000:+.3f}s")
    if abs(got - ref) > 48000 * 0.25:
        print("ABORT: loudnorm pass lost audio content")
        sys.exit(1)

    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(VIDEO), "-i", str(normed),
         "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "copy",
         "-shortest", "-movflags", "+faststart", str(FINAL)], "mux")

    vdur = probe_dur(FINAL)
    print(f"\nfinal: {vdur:.2f}s -> {FINAL}")
    if vdur > 30.0:
        print(f"WARNING: final duration {vdur:.2f}s exceeds the 30s cap")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Step 3: build the soundtrack from scratch (the source footage audio is
real digital silence -- measured -91dB across the whole recording, verified
with volumedetect, not assumed) and mux it onto graded_video.mp4.

Three synthesized layers, each rendered to its own short WAV first so the
mix step is simple arithmetic (adelay + amix), then two-pass loudnorm and a
final decoded-sample-count verification against the muxed output -- the same
discipline as the sibling Kodely project's finalize.py, applied here even
though there's no source audio to lose, because the loudnorm/mux step can
still silently truncate a track if a filter or duration mismatches.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

EDIT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SFX = EDIT / "sfx"
SFX.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
VIDEO = EDIT / "graded_video.mp4"
FINAL = EDIT / "final.mp4"

starts = {s["label"]: s["start"] for s in json.loads((EDIT / "shot_starts.json").read_text())}


def run(cmd, label):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED: {label}")
        print(" ".join(str(c) for c in cmd)[:500])
        print(r.stderr[-3000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def probe_dur(p: Path) -> float:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", str(p)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())


VIDEO_DUR = probe_dur(VIDEO)
print(f"video duration: {VIDEO_DUR:.2f}s")


def make_bed(out: Path, dur: float):
    """Soft layered pad: two gently detuned low sines plus a fifth, slow
    tremolo swell, lowpassed for warmth. Sits well under -30dB so it never
    competes with the whooshes/chime. Three plain lavfi inputs mixed
    directly -- same reliable pattern as make_chime, no nested lavfi-in-lavfi
    tricks."""
    inputs = []
    for freq in (110, 110.6, 164.8):
        inputs += ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"sine=frequency={freq}:duration={dur}"]
    filt = (
        "[0:a][1:a][2:a]amix=inputs=3:weights=1 0.8 0.5:normalize=0,"
        "tremolo=f=0.15:d=0.35,"
        "lowpass=f=900,"
        "volume=0.09[bed]"
    )
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[bed]",
         "-t", f"{dur}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "bed")


def make_whoosh(out: Path, dur: float = 0.42):
    """Bandpass-swept noise burst -- a soft filtered-noise transition
    texture, not a literal pitch sweep (ffmpeg lavfi has no cheap chirp
    generator), fast in / slow out envelope so it reads as a push forward."""
    filt = (
        f"anoisesrc=color=pink:duration={dur}:amplitude=1,"
        f"bandpass=f=1400:width_type=h:w=1800,"
        f"volume=0.5,"
        f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.05,"
        f"afade=t=out:st={dur-0.22:.3f}:d=0.22"
    )
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", filt,
         "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "whoosh")


def make_chime(out: Path):
    """Bright 3-note ascending arpeggio (C5-E5-G5) for the 'server is live'
    beat -- short, clean, no drama. Pure source filters, no -i inputs
    needed: ffmpeg lets sine/adelay chains stand alone in filter_complex."""
    notes = [(523.25, 0.00), (659.25, 0.09), (783.99, 0.18)]
    dur = 0.62
    parts = []
    labels = []
    for i, (freq, start) in enumerate(notes):
        lbl = f"n{i}"
        parts.append(
            f"sine=frequency={freq}:duration={dur - start:.3f},"
            f"afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.01,afade=t=out:st={dur-start-0.28:.3f}:d=0.28,"
            f"adelay={int(start*1000)}|{int(start*1000)}[{lbl}]"
        )
        labels.append(f"[{lbl}]")
    filt = (";".join(parts) +
            f";{''.join(labels)}amix=inputs={len(notes)}:normalize=0,"
            f"volume=0.35,aecho=0.8:0.7:60:0.25[chime]")
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-filter_complex", filt, "-map", "[chime]",
         "-t", f"{dur}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "chime")


def mix(out: Path):
    bed = SFX / "bed.wav"
    whoosh = SFX / "whoosh.wav"
    chime = SFX / "chime.wav"
    make_bed(bed, VIDEO_DUR)
    make_whoosh(whoosh)
    make_chime(chime)

    whoosh_at = [starts["poster_games"], starts["globe"], starts["discount"],
                 starts["poster_mods"], starts["outro"]]
    chime_at = starts["deploy_live"]

    inputs = ["-i", str(bed)]
    filt_parts = ["[0:a]anull[bed]"]
    labels = ["[bed]"]
    for i, t in enumerate(whoosh_at):
        inputs += ["-i", str(whoosh)]
        idx = i + 1
        ms = int(t * 1000)
        filt_parts.append(f"[{idx}:a]adelay={ms}|{ms}[wh{i}]")
        labels.append(f"[wh{i}]")
    inputs += ["-i", str(chime)]
    cidx = len(whoosh_at) + 1
    ms = int(chime_at * 1000)
    filt_parts.append(f"[{cidx}:a]adelay={ms}|{ms}[chime0]")
    labels.append("[chime0]")

    filt = ";".join(filt_parts) + f";{''.join(labels)}amix=inputs={len(labels)}:normalize=0[mix]"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", *inputs, "-filter_complex", filt,
         "-map", "[mix]", "-t", f"{VIDEO_DUR}", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(out)], "mix")


def decoded_samples(p: Path) -> int:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-f", "s16le", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "48000", "-"],
                       capture_output=True)
    return len(r.stdout) // 2


def measure(p: Path) -> dict:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(p), "-map", "0:a",
                        "-af", "loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11:print_format=json",
                        "-f", "null", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = re.findall(r"\{[^{}]*\"input_i\"[^{}]*\}", r.stderr, re.S)
    return json.loads(m[-1])


def main():
    raw = SFX / "mix_raw.wav"
    mix(raw)

    d = measure(raw)
    print(f"raw mix: I={d['input_i']} LUFS TP={d['input_tp']} dBTP")
    af = (f"loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11:measured_I={d['input_i']}:measured_TP={d['input_tp']}"
          f":measured_LRA={d['input_lra']}:measured_thresh={d['input_thresh']}"
          f":offset={d['target_offset']}:linear=true,aresample=48000")
    normed = SFX / "mix_normed.m4a"
    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(raw), "-af", af,
         "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", str(normed)], "loudnorm")

    ref = decoded_samples(raw)
    got = decoded_samples(normed)
    print(f"samples: raw {ref} normed {got} delta {(got-ref)/48000:+.3f}s")
    if abs(got - ref) > 48000 * 0.25:
        print("ABORT: loudnorm pass lost audio content")
        sys.exit(1)

    run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-i", str(VIDEO), "-i", str(normed),
         "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "copy",
         "-shortest", "-movflags", "+faststart", str(FINAL)], "mux")

    vdur = probe_dur(FINAL)
    print(f"\nfinal: {vdur:.2f}s -> {FINAL}")
    if vdur > 30.0:
        print(f"WARNING: final duration {vdur:.2f}s exceeds the 30s cap")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Push the recreated-UI demo's scene code to the baz project (free path --
`baz scenes create --file`, no AI tokens per the 'trend-to-skill factory'
pattern in the installed baz skill: author TSX locally, baz is the
persistence/review layer, not the generator).

baz scenes are standalone TSX files (window.Remotion globals, no cross-file
imports), so each screen's shared UI (AppShell, Cursor, tokens,
primitives, WizardSteps) is inlined here rather than imported -- matching
what the local Remotion project does via real ES imports.

Known limitation, stated plainly rather than silently worked around: image
sources use staticFile("games/g00.jpg") etc., which resolve against THIS
project's local Remotion public/ folder. baz's own preview/export won't be
able to load those files since they were never uploaded to baz's media
library (79 game-cover + mod-logo files -- not uploaded here to keep this
free/fast). The pushed code is correct and complete for reference/editing;
only image rendering inside baz's own preview will show broken images
until/unless those assets are uploaded to that project too.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

RM = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "remotion" / "src"
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "baz-assets" / "pushed"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

SHARED_FILES = [
    RM / "ui" / "tokens.ts",
    RM / "ui" / "Cursor.tsx",
    RM / "ui" / "primitives.tsx",
    RM / "ui" / "WizardSteps.tsx",
    RM / "ui" / "AppShell.tsx",
]

# (screen file, component name, duration const, start frame, baz scene name)
SCENES = [
    ("screens/DashboardScreen.tsx", "DashboardScreen", "DURATION_DASHBOARD", 0, "demo_01_dashboard"),
    ("screens/ChooseGameScreen.tsx", "ChooseGameScreen", "DURATION_CHOOSE_GAME", 74, "demo_02_choose_game"),
    ("screens/SizeServerScreen.tsx", "SizeServerScreen", "DURATION_SIZE_SERVER", 142, "demo_03_size_server"),
    ("screens/RegionScreen.tsx", "RegionScreen", "DURATION_REGION", 204, "demo_04_region"),
    ("screens/PaymentScreen.tsx", "PaymentScreen", "DURATION_PAYMENT", 272, "demo_05_payment"),
    ("screens/DeployProgressScreen.tsx", "DeployProgressScreen", "DURATION_DEPLOY_PROGRESS", 350, "demo_06_deploy"),
    ("screens/LiveDashboardScreen.tsx", "LiveDashboardScreen", "DURATION_LIVE_DASHBOARD", 418, "demo_07_live_dashboard"),
    ("screens/ModsScreen.tsx", "ModsScreen", "DURATION_MODS", 480, "demo_08_mods"),
    ("screens/ConfigScreen.tsx", "ConfigScreen", "DURATION_CONFIG", 542, "demo_09_config"),
    ("scenes/SupportCard.tsx", "SupportCard", "DURATION_SUPPORT", 588, "demo_10_support"),
    ("scenes/OutroCta.tsx", "OutroCta", "DURATION_OUTRO", 676, "demo_11_outro"),
]

IMPORT_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*import\s+.*?;?\s*$', re.MULTILINE)
EXPORT_CONST_RE = re.compile(r'^export const ')
EXPORT_FUNC_RE = re.compile(r'^export default function')


def strip_imports(src: str) -> str:
    return IMPORT_RE.sub("", src)


def build_shared_prelude() -> str:
    parts = []
    for f in SHARED_FILES:
        src = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        src = strip_imports(src)
        src = EXPORT_CONST_RE.sub("const ", src)
        src = re.sub(r'^export function ', 'function ', src, flags=re.MULTILINE)
        parts.append(f"// --- inlined from ui/{f.name} ---\n{src.strip()}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def build_scene(rel_path: str, comp_name: str, dur_const: str) -> str:
    src = (RM / rel_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    src = strip_imports(src)
    src = EXPORT_FUNC_RE.sub("function", src)
    src = re.sub(rf'^export const {dur_const}', f'const {dur_const}', src, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    return src.strip()


HEADER = """const {
  AbsoluteFill, Sequence, Img, interpolate, Easing, staticFile, useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig,
} = window.Remotion;

// NOTE: image sources below (staticFile("games/..."), staticFile("mods/..."),
// staticFile("nxeon-logo-crop.png")) point at this project's local Remotion
// public/ folder and were NOT re-uploaded to this baz project's media
// library -- they will not resolve inside baz's own preview/export. The
// scene logic/layout/choreography is otherwise complete and matches the
// delivered video exactly.
"""


def main():
    prelude = build_shared_prelude()
    run(["baz", "context", "add",
         "This project mirrors an 11-scene recreated-UI cursor demo built and rendered "
         "locally in a self-hosted Remotion project (nxeon-promo/edit/remotion). Scenes "
         "demo_01..demo_11 are pushed here via scenes create (deterministic, no AI tokens) "
         "for reference/editing, not as the render source -- the delivered video is "
         "rendered locally. Image assets referenced via staticFile() are NOT in this "
         "project's media library (not uploaded, to stay free/fast); they will 404 in "
         "baz's own preview.", "--label", "instructions"])

    for rel_path, comp_name, dur_const, start, scene_name in SCENES:
        scene_src = build_scene(rel_path, comp_name, dur_const)
        full = f"{HEADER}\n{prelude}\n\n// --- scene: {rel_path} ---\n{scene_src}\n"
        out_file = OUT / f"{scene_name}.tsx"
        out_file.write_text(full, encoding="utf-8")

        # duration is a literal number in each screen file; pull it back out
        m = re.search(rf'const {dur_const}\s*=\s*(\d+)', scene_src)
        duration = m.group(1) if m else "90"

        print(f"-- pushing {scene_name} (start={start}, duration={duration}) --")
        run(["baz", "scenes", "create", "--name", scene_name, "--file", str(out_file),
             "--duration", duration, "--track", "1", "--start", str(start)])


def run(cmd):
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent))
    print(r.stdout[-1500:])
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("STDERR:", r.stderr[-1500:])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
